vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 (one) + 切 (cut) = "one cut" that includes everything.
vocabulary.etymology: From 一 (yī, one) and 切 (qiè, to cut). The idea is "all things brought together into one" or "a unified whole".

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yī qiè shùn lì!
examples.english: I wish you all the best! (Literally: smooth in everything)

examples.pinyin: Zhè lǐ de yī qiè dōu hěn guì.
examples.english: Everything here is very expensive.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用作宾语，如“关心一切”。通常和“都”一起用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of holding up one finger to make your first point.
vocabulary.etymology: Literal: one (一) side/aspect (方面).

examples.chinese: 一方面我想去，另一方面我又很累。
examples.pinyin: Yī fāng miàn wǒ xiǎng qù, lìng yī fāng miàn wǒ yòu hěn lèi.
examples.english: On one hand I want to go, on the other hand I'm very tired.

examples.chinese: 一方面他很聪明，另一方面他不太努力。
examples.pinyin: Yī fāng miàn tā hěn cōng ming, lìng yī fāng miàn tā bú tài nǔ lì.
examples.english: On one hand he is very smart, on the other hand he doesn't work very hard.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 几乎总是和“另一方面”一起用，来对比两个观点或情况。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (up) + 升 (ascend) = double the "up-ness".
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 上 (shàng, up) and 升 (shēng, to rise, to hoist).

examples.pinyin: Qì wēn zhèng zài kuài sù shàng shēng.
examples.english: The temperature is rising quickly.

examples.pinyin: Tā de zhí wèi jīn nián shàng shēng le.
examples.english: His position rose this year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用于抽象事物（如温度、价格、地位）和具体事物（如电梯、热气球）。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (up) + 去 (to go, away) = go up and away.
vocabulary.etymology: Combination of the verb 上 (to go up) and the directional complement 去 (qù, indicating movement away from the speaker).

examples.pinyin: Bǎ xiāng zi bān dào lóu shàng qù.
examples.english: Carry the box upstairs (away from here).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kě yǐ zuò diàn tī shàng qù.
examples.english: You can take the elevator up.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在动词后表示动作的方向，如“爬上去”。主语或物体远离说话者。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (up) + 来 (come) = come up to me.
vocabulary.etymology: Combination of the verb 上 (to go up) and the directional complement 来 (lái, indicating movement towards the speaker).

examples.pinyin: Kuài shàng lái, chē yào kāi le!
examples.english: Come up quickly, the bus is about to leave! (Speaker is on the bus)

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ cài duān shàng lái.
examples.english: Please bring the dishes up (to the table/to me).

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在动词后表示动作的方向，如“跑上来”。主语或物体向说话者移动。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (upper) + 衣 (clothing) = clothing for your upper body.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 上 (shàng, upper) and 衣 (yī, clothing).

examples.chinese: 我今天穿了一件新上衣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīn tiān chuān le yī jiàn xīn shàng yī.
examples.english: I'm wearing a new top today.

examples.chinese: 这件上衣配什么裤子好看？
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shàng yī pèi shén me kù zi hǎo kàn?
examples.english: What pants look good with this top?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 泛指所有上半身穿的衣物，包括衬衫、T恤、毛衣等，不包括外套。

vocabulary.english: above; on top of; the top
vocabulary.mnemonic: 上 (up) + 面 (surface) = the surface that is up.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 上 (shàng, up) and 面 (miàn, face, surface).

examples.pinyin: Shū zài zhuō zi shàng miàn.
examples.english: The book is on the table.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn shàng miàn de lì zi.
examples.english: Please look at the example above.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 表示具体或抽象的位置。常和“在”一起用，构成“在...上面”。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 下 (down) + 去 (to go, away) = go down and away.
vocabulary.etymology: Combination of the verb 下 (to go down) and the directional complement 去 (qù, indicating movement away from the speaker).

examples.pinyin: Tā xià lóu qù le.
examples.english: He went downstairs (away from here).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zuò xià qù.
examples.english: Please sit down (and stay there).

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在动词后表示动作的方向，如“跳下去”。主语或物体远离说话者。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 下 (down) + 来 (come) = come down to me.
vocabulary.etymology: Combination of the verb 下 (to go down) and the directional complement 来 (lái, indicating movement towards the speaker).

examples.pinyin: Kuài cóng shù shàng xià lai!
examples.english: Come down from the tree quickly! (Speaker is below)

examples.pinyin: Jià gé zhōng yú xià lai le.
examples.english: The price has finally come down.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在动词后表示动作的方向，如“走下来”。也用于表示状态变化完成，如“停下来”。主语或物体向说话者移动或状态变化影响说话者。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 下 (down) + 面 (surface) = the surface that is down.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 下 (xià, down) and 面 (miàn, face, surface).

examples.pinyin: Māo zài chuáng xià miàn.
examples.english: The cat is under the bed.

examples.pinyin: Xià miàn de nèi róng hěn zhòng yào.
examples.english: The content below is very important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 表示具体或抽象的位置。常和“在”一起用，构成“在...下面”。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 仅 (only) = "not only".
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 仅 (jǐn, only, merely).

examples.pinyin: Tā bù jǐn cōng ming, hái hěn nǔ lì.
examples.english: He is not only smart, but also very hardworking.

examples.chinese: 这不仅是个问题，还是个机会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù jǐn shì gè wèn tí, hái shì gè jī huì.
examples.english: This is not only a problem, but also an opportunity.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 通常和“而且”、“还”、“也”一起用，构成“不仅...而且...”结构。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 光 (just/only) = "not just".
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 光 (guāng, here meaning 'just', 'only', 'merely').

examples.chinese: 他不光会说中文，还会说法语。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù guāng huì shuō Zhōng wén, hái huì shuō Fǎ yǔ.
examples.english: He can not only speak Chinese, but also French.

examples.chinese: 这不光是我一个人的想法。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù guāng shì wǒ yī gè rén de xiǎng fǎ.
examples.english: This is not just my idea alone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 和“不仅”意思一样，但更口语化。同样需要和“还”、“也”等词搭配。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 安 (peaceful/calm) = not calm.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 安 (ān, peace, calm, safe).

examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐ lái yǒu diǎn bù ān.
examples.english: He looks a bit uneasy.

examples.chinese: 这个消息让我感到不安。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiāo xi ràng wǒ gǎn dào bù ān.
examples.english: This news makes me feel anxious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 描述一种担心的心理状态。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 得 (must) + 不 (not) = double negative meaning "must".
vocabulary.etymology: Lit. "not get not", a double negative construction that results in an affirmative meaning of obligation.

examples.chinese: 下雨了，我不得不取消计划。
examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, wǒ bù dé bù qǔ xiāo jì huà.
examples.english: It's raining, I have to cancel the plan.

examples.chinese: 时间不够，我不得不快点。
examples.pinyin: Shí jiān bú gòu, wǒ bù dé bù kuài diǎn.
examples.english: There's not enough time, I have to hurry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 表示因外部原因或情况所迫而必须做某事，语气比“必须”更强，带有无奈感。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 必 (must) = "not must".
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 必 (bì, must, certainly).

examples.chinese: 你不必担心，一切都会好的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú bì dān xīn, yī qiè dōu huì hǎo de.
examples.english: You don't have to worry, everything will be fine.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān bú bì chuān zhèng zhuāng.
examples.english: You don't need to wear formal clothes today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 比“不用”稍微正式一点，表示没有必要做某事。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 断 (break) = "unbroken", meaning continuous.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 断 (duàn, to break, to sever).

examples.pinyin: Tā bú duàn de liàn xí shuō Zhōng wén.
examples.english: He practices speaking Chinese continuously.

examples.pinyin: Yǔ zài bú duàn de xià.
examples.english: It's raining continuously.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 放在动词前面，表示动作或状态没有间断。常和“地”一起用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 不 (not) + 论 (discuss/consider) = "do not consider [differences]".
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 不 (bù, not) and 论 (lùn, to discuss, to consider).

examples.chinese: 不论你去哪儿，我都跟你一起去。
examples.pinyin: Bù lùn nǐ qù nǎr, wǒ dōu gēn nǐ yī qǐ qù.
examples.english: No matter where you go, I'll go with you.

examples.chinese: 不论天气如何，比赛都会举行。
examples.pinyin: Bù lùn tiān qì rú hé, bǐ sài dōu huì jǔ xíng.
examples.english: Regardless of the weather, the match will be held.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在条件从句的开头，主句常用“都”或“也”呼应。和“无论”意思相同。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 (specialize) + 业 (business/field) = a specialized field.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 专 (zhuān, specialized, focused) and 业 (yè, business, occupation, undertaking).

examples.chinese: 我的专业是计算机科学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhuān yè shì jì suàn jī kē xué.
examples.english: My major is computer science.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiū chē hěn zhuān yè.
examples.english: He is very professional at repairing cars.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作名词指大学的主修科目或某个行业领域；作形容词指具有专业知识或技能的。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 (specialize) + 家 (master/person) = a person who specializes.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 专 (zhuān, specialized) and 家 (jiā, here meaning a person skilled in a particular field).

examples.chinese: 他是电脑安全方面的专家。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì diàn nǎo ān quán fāng miàn de zhuān jiā.
examples.english: He is an expert in computer security.

examples.chinese: 我们需要请一位专家来看看。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào qǐng yī wèi zhuān jiā lái kàn kan.
examples.english: We need to invite an expert to take a look.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 指在某个特定领域有深入知识和丰富经验的人。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 (focus) + 门 (gate/door) = focusing on one specific "door" or area.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 专 (zhuān, focused) and 门 (mén, door, gateway, field of study).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhuān mén wèi nǐ zuò le dàn gāo.
examples.english: I made the cake specially for you.

examples.chinese: 这是一家专门卖川菜的饭店。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī jiā zhuān mén mài chuān cài de fàn diàn.
examples.english: This is a restaurant that specifically sells Sichuan cuisine.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作副词表示“特意地”；作形容词表示“专用于某个目的的”。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 专 is 'special', 题 is 'topic' — it's a special topic report.
vocabulary.etymology: 专 (專) originally depicted a hand spinning thread (focusing on one task). 题 (題) combines 是 (this) + 页 (head/page), meaning a topic or subject heading.

examples.chinese: 今晚的新闻有个关于环保的专题。
examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn de xīnwén yǒu gè guānyú huánbǎo de zhuāntí.
examples.english: Tonight's news has a special feature on environmental protection.

examples.chinese: 他在写一个历史专题的博客。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xiě yī gè lìshǐ zhuāntí de bókè.
examples.english: He is writing a blog on a special historical topic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for media reports, academic papers, or focused projects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 世 (generation) + 界 (boundary) = the boundary of generations, the whole world.
vocabulary.etymology: 世 depicted sprouts/plants, representing generations. 界 originally meant a boundary between fields. Together, they signify the bounded realm of human existence.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù kàn kàn zhège shìjiè.
examples.english: I want to go see the world.

examples.chinese: 在互联网上，你能连接整个世界。
examples.pinyin: Zài hùliánwǎng shàng, nǐ néng liánjiē zhěnggè shìjiè.
examples.english: On the internet, you can connect with the whole world.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common. Can be used literally or figuratively (e.g., 内心世界 'inner world').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 世界 (world) + 杯 (cup) = the world's cup.
vocabulary.etymology: A modern compound: 世界 (world) + 杯 (cup/trophy).

examples.pinyin: Èr líng èr èr nián Shìjièbēi zài Kǎtǎ'ěr jǔbàn.
examples.english: The 2022 World Cup was held in Qatar.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn Shìjièbēi juésài le ma?
examples.english: Did you watch the World Cup final?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to the FIFA足球世界杯, but can also refer to other sports (e.g., 篮球世界杯).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 世 (generation) + 纪 (record) = a record of generations, a century.
vocabulary.etymology: 世 (generation/era). 纪 (紀) originally meant to separate silk threads, later came to mean to record or an era. Together they signify a recorded era of 100 years.

examples.chinese: 我们生活在二十一世纪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shēnghuó zài èrshí yī shìjì.
examples.english: We live in the 21st century.

examples.chinese: 这座桥已经有半个世纪的历史了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo yǐjīng yǒu bàn gè shìjì de lìshǐ le.
examples.english: This bridge already has half a century of history.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 东 (east) + 部 (part) = the eastern part.
vocabulary.etymology: 东 (東) depicts the sun rising behind a tree (the east). 部 means a division or part.

examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi zài Zhōngguó de dōngbù.
examples.english: Shanghai is in the eastern part of China.

examples.chinese: 公司准备在东部开一家新工厂。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhǔnbèi zài dōngbù kāi yī jiā xīn gōngchǎng.
examples.english: The company plans to open a new factory in the east.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for geographical divisions of countries, cities, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 个 (single) + 人 (person) = a single person, an individual.
vocabulary.etymology: 个 (個) is a common measure word for people/items. 人 is person.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ shì wǒ gèrén de yìjiàn.
examples.english: This is just my personal opinion.

examples.chinese: 每个人都要对自己的行为负责。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yào duì zìjǐ de xíngwéi fùzé.
examples.english: Every individual must be responsible for their own actions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a noun (individual) or an adjective (personal).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 个 (individual) + 性 (nature) = an individual's nature, their personality.
vocabulary.etymology: 个 (individual). 性 means nature, character, or property.

examples.pinyin: Tā de gèxìng fēicháng kāilǎng.
examples.english: Her personality is very cheerful.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēiguǎn hěn yǒu gèxìng.
examples.english: This café has a lot of character.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a person's character or something's distinctive style.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 中华 (China) + 民族 (ethnic group) = the Chinese ethnic nation.
vocabulary.etymology: 中华 refers to China (central and splendid). 民族 means ethnic group or nation.

examples.chinese: 中华民族有五千多年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhōnghuá mínzú yǒu wǔ qiān duō nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: The Chinese nation has a history of over five thousand years.

examples.chinese: 春节是中华民族最重要的节日。
examples.pinyin: Chūnjié shì Zhōnghuá mínzú zuì zhòngyào de jiérì.
examples.english: The Spring Festival is the most important festival for the Chinese nation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal and patriotic term encompassing all ethnic groups within China.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 丰 (abundant) + 富 (wealthy) = doubly abundant and rich!
vocabulary.etymology: 丰 (豐) depicted a ritual vessel full of offerings. 富 shows wealth under a roof. Both contribute to the meaning of abundance.

examples.chinese: 这个国家的自然资源很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de zìrán zīyuán hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: This country has very rich natural resources.

examples.chinese: 旅行可以丰富你的人生经验。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng kěyǐ fēngfù nǐ de rénshēng jīngyàn.
examples.english: Traveling can enrich your life experience.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective, it describes abundance. As a verb, it means 'to make something richer/more varied'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 主 (in charge) + 任 (responsibility) = the person in charge, the director.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 shows a flame (the main part). 任 depicted carrying a burden on a pole, meaning responsibility.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen bùmén de zhǔrèn.
examples.english: He is the director of our department.

examples.chinese: 王主任今天不在办公室。
examples.pinyin: Wáng zhǔrèn jīntiān bù zài bàngōngshì.
examples.english: Director Wang is not in the office today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common title for heads of departments, offices, or committees.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 主 (master) + 动 (move) = to move like a master, taking the lead.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (to master/to be in charge). 动 (動) depicts strength moving a heavy object.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔdòng bāng wǒ ná xínglǐ.
examples.english: He proactively helped me with my luggage.

examples.pinyin: Zhǎo gōngzuò yào zhǔdòng yīdiǎn.
examples.english: You need to be more proactive when looking for a job.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes voluntary action, the opposite of 被动 (passive).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 主 (in charge) + 张 (to spread/open) = to spread your charge/opinion.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (to master/hold a view). 张 (張) depicts drawing a bowstring, meaning to extend or spread.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔzhāng bǎohù huánjìng.
examples.english: He advocates for environmental protection.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de gèrén zhǔzhāng.
examples.english: This is my personal viewpoint.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, it's stronger than 'think'—it implies advocating for an idea. As a noun, it's a formal word for 'viewpoint'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 主 (main) + 意 (thought) = the main thought, your idea.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (main). 意 (thought/idea).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shé me hǎo zhǔyi?
examples.english: Do you have any good ideas?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎi zhǔyi le, bù xiǎng qù le.
examples.english: I changed my mind, I don't want to go.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese for 'idea' or 'mind' (as in 改变主意 'change one's mind').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 主 (in charge) + 持 (to hold) = to hold charge of an event.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (to be in charge). 持 depicts a hand holding something.

examples.chinese: 她经常主持公司的会议。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng zhǔchí gōngsī de huìyì.
examples.english: She often chairs the company meetings.

examples.pinyin: Zhège wǎnhuì shì tā zhǔchí de.
examples.english: This evening party was hosted by him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for hosting shows, chairing meetings, or presiding over ceremonies.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 举 (raise/lift up) + 办 (do/manage) = to lift up and manage an event.
vocabulary.etymology: 举 (舉) shows hands lifting something. 办 (辦) depicts managing with effort (力) over disputes (辛辛).

examples.chinese: 下个月我们学校要举办运动会。
examples.pinyin: Xià gè yuè wǒmen xuéxiào yào jǔbàn yùndònghuì.
examples.english: Our school will hold a sports meet next month.

examples.pinyin: Shéi fùzé jǔbàn zhè cì jùhuì?
examples.english: Who is responsible for organizing this party?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial and common for holding parties, competitions, exhibitions, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a person (人) leaning against a wall for a loooong time. It's just 久.
vocabulary.etymology: The character's origin is uncertain. One theory is it depicts a person with a bent back, suggesting a long duration.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hǎo jiǔ méi jiàn le!
examples.english: Long time no see!

examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài yào zhǔ de jiǔ yīdiǎn.
examples.english: This dish needs to be cooked a bit longer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used after verbs to indicate duration (e.g., 等久了 'waited for a long time').

vocabulary.mnemonic: A tree (木) with something joyful hanging on it — simple happiness.
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional form 樂 is thought to depict wooden bells or drums on a stand, representing music which brings joy.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhěng tiān lèhēhē de.
examples.english: He's cheerful all day long.

examples.pinyin: Lè yú zhù rén shì gè hǎo pǐnzhì.
examples.english: Being willing to help others is a good quality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 读 lè. Common in compounds and set phrases. Can be a verb meaning 'to be happy to' (乐于).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 乐 (happy) + 观 (view) = having a happy view of things.
vocabulary.etymology: 乐 (happy). 观 (觀) means to observe or a viewpoint.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì wèilái hěn lèguān.
examples.english: She is very optimistic about the future.

examples.pinyin: Bǎochí lèguān hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Staying optimistic is very important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The direct opposite is 悲观 (pessimistic).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 乐 (music) + 队 (team) = a team that makes music.
vocabulary.etymology: 乐 (music). 队 (隊) originally meant to fall from a height, later came to mean a rank/team.

examples.chinese: 他大学时组过一个摇滚乐队。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàxué shí zǔ guò yī gè yáogǔn yuèduì.
examples.english: He formed a rock band when he was in college.

examples.chinese: 婚礼上请了一支很棒的乐队。
examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ shàng qǐng le yī zhī hěn bàng de yuèduì.
examples.english: They hired a great band for the wedding.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 读 yuèduì. Refers to any musical band, from rock to jazz to traditional.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 书 (book) + 架 (rack/frame) = a rack for books.
vocabulary.etymology: 书 (書) depicts a hand holding a brush writing. 架 is a phonetic-semantic compound meaning a frame or support.

examples.chinese: 我的书架上放满了小说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shūjià shàng fàng mǎn le xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: My bookshelf is full of novels.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào mǎi gè xīn shūjià.
examples.english: We need to buy a new bookshelf.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like tangled threads — a mess!
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional form 亂 depicts hands untangling silk threads on a loom, representing disorder.

examples.chinese: 我的房间太乱了，得收拾一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān tài luàn le, děi shōushi yīxià.
examples.english: My room is too messy, I need to tidy up.

examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ dōngxi luàn fàng.
examples.english: Don't put things away randomly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe physical disorder, chaotic situations, or acting without order (乱说 'to talk nonsense').

vocabulary.mnemonic: Two hands (爫) pulling something down — fighting over it.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts two hands (variant of 爪) pulling something down, representing a struggle or contention.

examples.chinese: 孩子们在争最后一个苹果。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài zhēng zuìhòu yī gè píngguǒ.
examples.english: The kids are fighting over the last apple.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào wèi mèngxiǎng ér zhēng.
examples.english: We must strive for our dreams.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Core meaning is contention or competition. Often used in compounds.

vocabulary.english: to strive for / to fight for
vocabulary.mnemonic: 争 (strive) + 取 (take) = strive to take something.
vocabulary.etymology: 争 (to strive). 取 depicts a hand taking an ear (as war trophy), meaning to take.

examples.chinese: 我要争取这次升职的机会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào zhēngqǔ zhè cì shēngzhí de jīhuì.
examples.english: I'm going to strive for this promotion opportunity.

examples.pinyin: Zhēngqǔ zǎo diǎn wánchéng rènwù.
examples.english: Strive to finish the task earlier.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies active effort to achieve a positive goal (opportunity, time, victory).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 事 (affair) + 业 (vocation) = the affair of your vocation, your career.
vocabulary.etymology: 事 depicts a hand holding an official register, meaning an affair. 业 (業) depicted a large wooden frame for hanging musical instruments, later extended to mean work/vocation.

examples.chinese: 他把教育当作一生的事业。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ jiàoyù dàngzuò yīshēng de shìyè.
examples.english: He treats education as his lifelong career.

examples.chinese: 慈善事业需要大家的支持。
examples.pinyin: Císhàn shìyè xūyào dàjiā de zhīchí.
examples.english: Charitable undertakings need everyone's support.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Broader than just a 'job'; implies a significant, often long-term, pursuit or enterprise.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a person (亻) holding out just one hand, saying "仅此而已" (that's all).
vocabulary.etymology: From 亻(person) + 又(again/also). The original meaning was 'numerous' but evolved to mean 'only'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jǐn yǒu yī gè píng guǒ.
examples.english: I have only one apple.

examples.chinese: 他仅用了五分钟就完成了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǐn yòng le wǔ fēn zhōng jiù wán chéng le.
examples.english: He finished it in only five minutes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before verbs or adjectives to emphasize a small quantity or degree. Slightly more formal than "只".

vocabulary.mnemonic: Double the "仅", double the emphasis on how little or small something is.
vocabulary.etymology: The reduplicated form of 仅 (jǐn), used for emphasis.

examples.chinese: 这不仅仅是一个工作，更是我的梦想。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù jǐn jǐn shì yī gè gōng zuò, gèng shì wǒ de mèng xiǎng.
examples.english: This is not merely a job; it's my dream.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men jǐn jǐn shì péng you.
examples.english: We are merely friends.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More emphatic than the single "仅". Often implies a limit or restriction.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a person (亻) standing on a hill, still there as time passes (乃).
vocabulary.etymology: Pictogram depicting a person (亻) standing steadily. The core meaning relates to continuation.

examples.chinese: 十年过去了，他仍住在那里。
examples.pinyin: Shí nián guò qù le, tā réng zhù zài nà lǐ.
examples.english: Ten years have passed, and he still lives there.

examples.chinese: 我提醒了他三次，但他仍忘了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tí xǐng le tā sān cì, dàn tā réng wàng le.
examples.english: I reminded him three times, but he still forgot.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before verbs/adjectives to indicate a continuous state. Slightly formal or written, often used with "然" in 仍然.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "仍" (still) + "然" (-ly) = "still-ly" → describes something continuing in the same way.
vocabulary.etymology: 仍 (continue) + 然 (suffix indicating state). Together, they emphasize the state of continuing.

examples.chinese: 虽然他退休了，但仍然很忙。
examples.pinyin: Suī rán tā tuì xiū le, dàn réng rán hěn máng.
examples.english: Although he's retired, he's still very busy.

examples.pinyin: Tiān réng rán zài xià yǔ.
examples.english: It's still raining.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in both spoken and written Chinese. Slightly more formal than "还是" but widely used.

vocabulary.english: to be engaged in; to go in for
vocabulary.mnemonic: "从" (follow) a "事" (affair) → you follow an affair as your profession.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (to follow) + 事 (affair, matter). Means to follow a certain matter as one's work.

examples.chinese: 他从事教育工作二十年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng shì jiào yù gōng zuò èr shí nián le.
examples.english: He has been engaged in education work for twenty years.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng cóng shì IT háng yè.
examples.english: I want to go into the IT industry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for professions, careers, or major activities. Often followed by a noun phrase like "...工作" or a specific field.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "从" (from) "前" (front/before) → from a time before now.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (from) + 前 (front, before). Literally "from before".

examples.chinese: 从前，这里有一个美丽的湖。
examples.pinyin: Cóng qián, zhè lǐ yǒu yī gè měi lì de hú.
examples.english: Once upon a time, there was a beautiful lake here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng qián bù ài chī shū cài.
examples.english: I didn't like to eat vegetables in the past.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used like "once upon a time" or "in the old days". Can start a story. Similar to "以前".

vocabulary.mnemonic: "从" (from) "来" (come) → from the time coming up until now, indicating a consistent history.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (from) + 来 (come). Suggests "from the past until now".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng lái méi jiàn guò tā.
examples.english: I have never seen him.

examples.pinyin: Tā zuò shì cóng lái dōu hěn rèn zhēn.
examples.english: He always does things very conscientiously.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with "不", "没", or "都" to emphasize a persistent state from past to present. "从来没" = have never.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) handing over a dollar sign (寸 is like a hand giving something).
vocabulary.etymology: 亻(person) + 寸(hand/measure). Originally meant 'to hand over' or 'to give', now specialized for payment.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ fù xiàn jīn.
examples.english: I'll pay cash.

examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn wǒ lái fù.
examples.english: I'll pay for this meal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial verb for paying money. Often used with specific payment methods: 付钱, 付现金, 付微信.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) holding a weapon (弋) passing it to the next person → passing between generations.
vocabulary.etymology: 亻(person) + 弋(a peg/ stake, suggesting succession). Relates to replacement or succession over time.

examples.chinese: 我们这一代人都用手机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhè yī dài rén dōu yòng shǒu jī.
examples.english: Everyone in our generation uses smartphones.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng dài wǒ kāi huì ma?
examples.english: Can you attend the meeting in my place?

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, often with a number: 一代人 (one generation). As a verb, means to do something on behalf of someone else.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "代" (substitute) "表" (surface/express) → someone who substitutes to express a group's will.
vocabulary.etymology: 代 (to substitute) + 表 (to express, surface). One who expresses/stands in for others.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ men gōng sī de dài biǎo.
examples.english: He is our company's representative.

examples.chinese: 红色在中国文化中代表好运。
examples.pinyin: Hóng sè zài Zhōng guó wén huà zhōng dài biǎo hǎo yùn.
examples.english: Red represents good luck in Chinese culture.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for people (e.g., student representative) or symbols (e.g., a color represents an idea).

vocabulary.mnemonic: "代表" (representative) + "团" (group) = a group of representatives.
vocabulary.etymology: 代表 (representative) + 团 (group).

examples.chinese: 学校派出了一个代表团去参加会议。
examples.pinyin: Xué xiào pài chū le yī gè dài biǎo tuán qù cān jiā huì yì.
examples.english: The school sent a delegation to attend the conference.

examples.pinyin: Měi guó dài biǎo tuán míng tiān dào dá.
examples.english: The American delegation arrives tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to an official group sent to represent a country, organization, etc., often for meetings or events.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "以" (with) "来" (come) → with the coming of a point in time until now.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (with) + 来 (come). Indicates the period coming from a past point.

examples.chinese: 毕业以来，我再也没见过他。
examples.pinyin: Bì yè yǐ lái, wǒ zài yě méi jiàn guò tā.
examples.english: I haven't seen him since graduation.

examples.chinese: 三个月以来，他一直在找工作。
examples.pinyin: Sān gè yuè yǐ lái, tā yī zhí zài zhǎo gōng zuò.
examples.english: He has been looking for a job for the past three months.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used after a time noun or event to indicate the period from that point until the present. Often with 自/从 at the start: "自...以来".

vocabulary.mnemonic: "价" (price) + "值" (worth) = the worth something has, which determines its price.
vocabulary.etymology: 价 (price) + 值 (value, worth).

examples.chinese: 这幅画有很大的艺术价值。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà yǒu hěn dà de yì shù jià zhí.
examples.english: This painting has great artistic value.

examples.pinyin: Tā míng bai yǒu yì de jià zhí.
examples.english: He understands the value of friendship.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be monetary or abstract (emotional, moral value). 价值观 means "values" (principles).

vocabulary.mnemonic: "价" (price) "格" (standard/pattern) → the standard pattern for what something costs.
vocabulary.etymology: 价 (price) + 格 (standard, rank).

examples.chinese: 这个手机的价格是多少？
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shǒu jī de jià gé shì duō shao?
examples.english: What's the price of this phone?

examples.pinyin: Zuì jìn shū cài jià gé zhǎng le.
examples.english: Vegetable prices have risen recently.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard, formal word for price. Used in stores, economics, etc. Similar to "价钱" but more formal/written.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "价" (price) "钱" (money) → the money-price of something.
vocabulary.etymology: 价 (price) + 钱 (money). Literally "price money".

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yī fu jià qian bù cuò.
examples.english: The price of this piece of clothing is good.

examples.pinyin: Zán men tán tan jià qian ba.
examples.english: Let's talk about the price.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Everyday, spoken word for price. Used when shopping, bargaining, or casually asking "how much?".

vocabulary.english: to appoint; to assume a post; no matter (when used with 何)
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) holding a royal scepter (王) with extra power (丿) → being entrusted with an important post.
vocabulary.etymology: 亻(person) + 壬 (the 9th Heavenly Stem, also associated with burden). Original meaning related to burden or responsibility.

examples.pinyin: Tā bèi rèn wéi jīng lǐ.
examples.english: He was appointed as manager.

examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Rén.
examples.english: His surname is Ren.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, formal for appointing someone to a position. Also a common surname (Rén). Forms part of "任何" and "任务".

vocabulary.mnemonic: "任" (no matter) + "何" (what) = no matter what → any.
vocabulary.etymology: 任 (to bear, allow) + 何 (what). The sense is "bearing/accepting whatever".

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kě yǐ wèn rèn hé wèn tí.
examples.english: You can ask any question.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ rèn hé shí jiān dōu yǒu kòng.
examples.english: I'm free at any time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before nouns to mean "any". Often used with 都 or 也 for emphasis: "任何人都可以" = anyone can.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "任" (appoint/burden) + "务" (affair) → an appointed affair you must do.
vocabulary.etymology: 任 (responsibility) + 务 (affair, business).

examples.chinese: 今天的工作任务完成了。
examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān de gōng zuò rèn wu wán chéng le.
examples.english: Today's work tasks are finished.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gè zhòng yào de rèn wu.
examples.english: This is an important mission.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for assigned work, chores, or missions (in games/work). Can be big or small.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "优" (excellent) "势" (power/position) → the excellent position you have over others.
vocabulary.etymology: 优 (excellent) + 势 (power, situation).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men de yōu shì shì jià gé dī.
examples.english: Our advantage is the low price.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎ qiú yǒu shēn gāo yōu shì.
examples.english: He has a height advantage in playing ball.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in competition, business, or personal traits. Opposite is 劣势 (disadvantage).

vocabulary.mnemonic: "优" (excellent) "点" (point) → an excellent point about someone/something.
vocabulary.etymology: 优 (excellent) + 点 (point, dot).

examples.pinyin: Tā de yōu diǎn shì hěn yǒu nài xīn.
examples.english: One of her strong points is that she is very patient.

examples.chinese: 这个方法的优点是简单。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè fāng fǎ de yōu diǎn shì jiǎn dān.
examples.english: The merit of this method is its simplicity.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to specific good qualities of a person, thing, or method. Opposite is 缺点 (shortcoming).

vocabulary.mnemonic: "会" (association) + "员" (person) → a person in an association.
vocabulary.etymology: 会 (meeting, association) + 员 (person, member).

examples.chinese: 我是这家健身房的会员。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì zhè jiā jiàn shēn fáng de huì yuán.
examples.english: I'm a member of this gym.

examples.pinyin: Huì yuán yǒu dǎ zhé.
examples.english: Members get a discount.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to members of clubs, stores (membership programs), or organizations. 会员卡 = membership card.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "会" (meet) + "议" (discuss) = a meet-up for discussion.
vocabulary.etymology: 会 (to meet) + 议 (to discuss).

examples.chinese: 下午三点有个重要会议。
examples.pinyin: Xià wǔ sān diǎn yǒu gè zhòng yào huì yì.
examples.english: There's an important meeting at 3 PM.

examples.pinyin: Shì pín huì yì hěn fāng biàn.
examples.english: Video conferences are very convenient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal word for a meeting or conference, from small office meetings to large international ones.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "伟" (big/mighty) "大" (big) → doubly big and impressive.
vocabulary.etymology: 伟 (big, extraordinary) + 大 (big). A reinforcing compound.

examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó yǒu wěi dà de lì shǐ.
examples.english: China has a great history.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī wèi wěi dà de mǔ qin.
examples.english: She is a great mother.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for people, achievements, or things of extraordinary scale or importance. Formal and positive.

vocabulary.english: to pass on; to spread; to transmit
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) using a specialized tool (专) to pass something along.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 傳: 亻(person) + 專 (specialized, focus). The idea is a person focusing on transmitting something.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yán chuán gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please pass the salt to me.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiāo xi chuán de hěn kuài.
examples.english: This news spread very quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very versatile: can be physical (pass an object), abstract (spread news), or technical (transmit data).

vocabulary.english: to come over (sound/news); to be heard
vocabulary.mnemonic: "传" (transmit) + "来" (come) → sound or news transmitting and coming to you.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 (to transmit) + 来 (to come).

examples.pinyin: Yuǎn chù chuán lái le yīn yuè shēng.
examples.english: The sound of music came from the distance.

examples.pinyin: Cóng fáng jiān lǐ chuán lái xiào shēng.
examples.english: Laughter came from the room.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically used for sounds, voices, or news reaching one's ears. Often used with 声音, 消息, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a thing (事) that is built or established (件). Imagine a newspaper headline about a major established thing that happened.
vocabulary.etymology: 事 (affair, matter) + 件 (item, component). The combination implies an item or occurrence that constitutes a matter.

measure_word.example: 一个事件 (yī gè shì jiàn)

examples.chinese: 那是个让人难过的事件。
examples.pinyin: Nà shì gè ràng rén nánguò de shì jiàn.
examples.english: That was a sad incident.

examples.chinese: 网上都在讨论这个事件。
examples.pinyin: Wǎng shàng dōu zài tǎolùn zhège shì jiàn.
examples.english: People are discussing this event online.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for noteworthy or negative occurrences.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The real (实) matter (事). Think of it as the solid truth about a situation.
vocabulary.etymology: 事 (affair, matter) + 实 (real, solid). Literally 'solid/real affair'.

measure_word.example: 一个事实 (yī gè shì shí)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ děi miànduì shì shí.
examples.english: You have to face the facts.

examples.chinese: 他说的话跟事实完全不一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà gēn shì shí wánquán bù yīyàng.
examples.english: What he said is completely different from the facts.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in phrases like '事实是...' (The fact is...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's right on top (上) of the facts (事实). Use it to introduce what's really going on.
vocabulary.etymology: 事实 (fact) + 上 (on, above). A grammatical construction meaning 'on the basis of facts'.

examples.pinyin: Shì shí shàng, wǒ yǐjīng zhīdào le.
examples.english: In fact, I already know.

examples.chinese: 他说很忙，事实上他就在家玩游戏。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō hěn máng, shì shí shàng tā jiù zài jiā wán yóuxì.
examples.english: He said he was busy, but actually he was just at home playing games.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a clause to correct or clarify.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A matter (事) that is old or a cause (故). Think of an old, unexpected cause of trouble.
vocabulary.etymology: 事 (affair, matter) + 故 (reason, cause; old). Originally implying an unforeseen event or mishap.

measure_word.example: 一起事故 (yī qǐ shì gù)

examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn hǎoxiàng yǒu jiāotōng shì gù.
examples.english: There seems to be a traffic accident ahead.

examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shēngchǎn shì gù hěn yánzhòng.
examples.english: This production accident is very serious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always negative, implying damage or injury.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Two people guarding (互) each other from opposite sides (相). Visualize a mutual handshake.
vocabulary.etymology: 互 (mutual) + 相 (mutually). A doubling of the mutual concept.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hù xiāng bāngzhù.
examples.english: We should help each other.

examples.chinese: 他们互相看了一眼就笑了。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen hù xiāng kàn le yī yǎn jiù xiào le.
examples.english: They looked at each other and smiled.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Always followed by a verb (互相 + V).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A mutual (互) connection (联) network (网). The web that links everyone together.
vocabulary.etymology: 互 (mutual) + 联 (connect) + 网 (net). A calque of 'internet' (interconnected network).

examples.chinese: 现在买东西都用互联网。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài mǎi dōngxi dōu yòng Hù lián wǎng.
examples.english: Nowadays we use the internet to buy things.

examples.chinese: 互联网让生活方便多了。
examples.pinyin: Hù lián wǎng ràng shēnghuó fāngbiàn duō le.
examples.english: The internet makes life much more convenient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The formal term for 'internet', often shortened to '网络'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Cross (交) and go (往). People's paths cross as they go about their lives together.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (cross, exchange) + 往 (go towards, past). Implies a going back and forth in interaction.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen jiāo wǎng sān nián le.
examples.english: They have been dating for three years.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢和开朗的人交往。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan hé kāilǎng de rén jiāo wǎng.
examples.english: I like to associate with cheerful people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be platonic or romantic; context clarifies. Often used for serious relationships.

vocabulary.mnemonic: An exchange (交) that is easy (易). Think of a quick and easy hand-off of goods for money.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (exchange) + 易 (easy, exchange). Originally meant bartering or exchanging goods.

measure_word.example: 一笔交易 (yī bǐ jiāo yì)

examples.chinese: 这笔交易对我们很划算。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ jiāo yì duì wǒmen hěn huásuàn.
examples.english: This deal is very cost-effective for us.

examples.chinese: 他们在网上交易游戏账号。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài wǎng shàng jiāo yì yóuxì zhànghào.
examples.english: They trade game accounts online.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for both business and informal deals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Cross (交) and flow (流). Ideas and words flow back and forth between people.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (cross, exchange) + 流 (flow). Implies a flowing exchange.

examples.chinese: 我们经常交流学习经验。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīngcháng jiāo liú xuéxí jīngyàn.
examples.english: We often exchange learning experiences.

examples.chinese: 这次文化交流活动很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wénhuà jiāo liú huódòng hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: This cultural exchange activity is very interesting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for both personal and professional communication.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Handles traffic (交) and is an officer (警). The police you see at intersections.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (traffic, crossing) + 警 (police, alert). Short for 交通警察 (jiāotōng jǐngchá).

measure_word.example: 一位交警 (yī wèi jiāo jǐng)

examples.pinyin: Jiāo jǐng zài lùkǒu zhǐhuī chēliàng.
examples.english: The traffic police are directing vehicles at the intersection.

examples.chinese: 我因为没戴头盔被交警拦下了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yīnwèi méi dài tóukuī bèi jiāo jǐng lán xià le.
examples.english: I was pulled over by a traffic cop for not wearing a helmet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A specific type of police officer.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Hand over (交) the fee (费). Imagine handing money to complete a transaction.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (hand over) + 费 (fee, expense).

examples.chinese: 别忘了下个月要交物业费。
examples.pinyin: Bié wàng le xià gè yuè yào jiāo wùyè fèi.
examples.english: Don't forget to pay the property management fee next month.

examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn zài nǎlǐ jiāo tíngchē fèi?
examples.english: Excuse me, where do I pay the parking fee?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common daily life verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To give birth (产) and cause to grow (生). Something new comes into being.
vocabulary.etymology: 产 (give birth, produce) + 生 (birth, life). A compound emphasizing the origin of something.

examples.chinese: 这个决定会产生很大影响。
examples.pinyin: Zhège juédìng huì chǎn shēng hěn dà yǐngxiǎng.
examples.english: This decision will have a big impact (produce a big influence).

examples.chinese: 工厂每天产生很多垃圾。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng měi tiān chǎn shēng hěn duō lājī.
examples.english: The factory produces a lot of garbage every day.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for abstract things (feelings, results) and physical things (waste, products).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The capital's (京) drama (剧). The classic opera from Beijing.
vocabulary.etymology: 京 (capital) + 剧 (drama, play). Short for 北京戏曲 (Běijīng xìqǔ).

measure_word.example: 一出京剧 (yī chū Jīng jù)

examples.chinese: 我爷爷特别喜欢看京剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye tèbié xǐhuan kàn Jīng jù.
examples.english: My grandpa really likes watching Beijing opera.

examples.chinese: 京剧的服装和化妆都很特别。
examples.pinyin: Jīng jù de fúzhuāng hé huàzhuāng dōu hěn tèbié.
examples.english: The costumes and makeup in Beijing opera are very special.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A proper noun, often capitalized in pinyin (Jīngjù).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of someone you're so close to, you see them standing (立) on a tree (木) – you'd shout '亲!' to get their attention. Also, the sound of a kiss.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 親. Original character showed a person (見) visiting a relative (辛). The core meaning is 'close relation'.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì qīn de péngyou.
examples.english: She is my closest friend.

examples.chinese: 妈妈亲了一下宝宝的脸。
examples.pinyin: Māma qīn le yīxià bǎobao de liǎn.
examples.english: Mom kissed the baby's cheek.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Context sensitive. As an adjective: 'close'. As a noun: 'relative' (less common alone). As a verb: 'to kiss'. Also a casual online greeting ('亲~' on shopping sites).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Close/dear (亲) people (人). The people you are intimately connected to.
vocabulary.etymology: 亲 (close, kin) + 人 (person).

measure_word.example: 一个亲人 (yī gè qīn rén)

examples.chinese: 过年了，亲人都要回来团聚。
examples.pinyin: Guònián le, qīn rén dōu yào huílái tuánjù.
examples.english: It's Chinese New Year, all family members are coming back for a reunion.

examples.chinese: 在医院的时候，最需要亲人的陪伴。
examples.pinyin: Zài yīyuàn de shíhou, zuì xūyào qīn rén de péibàn.
examples.english: When you're in the hospital, you most need the company of loved ones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes emotional closeness, not just legal relation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Close (亲) and cut (切) – imagine a warm hug that cuts through formalities.
vocabulary.etymology: 亲 (close) + 切 (cut, close to). The combination implies a feeling of closeness and sincerity.

examples.pinyin: Xīn lǎoshī duì wǒmen hěn qīn qiè.
examples.english: The new teacher is very kind to us.

examples.chinese: 回到家乡，感觉特别亲切。
examples.pinyin: Huí dào jiāxiāng, gǎnjué tèbié qīn qiè.
examples.english: Returning to my hometown feels especially warm and familiar.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a person's demeanor or a familiar, welcoming atmosphere.

vocabulary.mnemonic: By your own (自) close self (亲). Not delegating, but doing it yourself.
vocabulary.etymology: 亲 (close, self) + 自 (self). Emphasizes the self.

examples.chinese: 老板亲自检查了每一个细节。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn qīn zì jiǎnchá le měi yī gè xìjié.
examples.english: The boss personally checked every detail.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ děi qīn zì qù bàn.
examples.english: I have to handle this matter in person.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stresses personal involvement, often for important or meticulous tasks.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People (人) who are members (员). Think of employees on a roster.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 员 (member).

measure_word.example: 一名人员 (yī míng rén yuán)

examples.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèngzài zhāopìn xīn rén yuán.
examples.english: The company is recruiting new personnel.

examples.chinese: 救援人员很快就赶到了。
examples.pinyin: Jiùyuán rén yuán hěn kuài jiù gǎndào le.
examples.english: Rescue personnel arrived very quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compound nouns like '工作人员', '救援人员'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Made by people (人) with work (工), not by nature or machines.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 工 (work, labor).

examples.pinyin: Zhège hú shì rén gōng wā de.
examples.english: This lake is man-made (artificially dug).

examples.pinyin: Yòng jīqì bǐ yòng rén gōng piányi.
examples.english: Using machines is cheaper than using manual labor.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Contrasts with '自然' (natural) or '自动' (automatic).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (人) of ability (才). The star of the team.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 才 (ability, talent).

examples.chinese: 我们公司特别缺技术人才。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī tèbié quē jìshù rén cái.
examples.english: Our company is especially short of technical talent.

examples.chinese: 他是个不可多得的人才。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè bùkě duōdé de rén cái.
examples.english: He is a rare and invaluable talent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A high-value term for skilled or gifted individuals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People (人) of the populace (民). The collective body of ordinary citizens.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 民 (populace, common people).

examples.pinyin: Rén mín bì shì Zhōngguó de huòbì.
examples.english: Renminbi is China's currency.

examples.chinese: 这项政策是为了人民的利益。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè shì wèile rén mín de lìyì.
examples.english: This policy is for the benefit of the people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A collective, political term. Rarely used to refer to an individual ('一个人').

vocabulary.mnemonic: The people's (人民) money (币). China's official currency.
vocabulary.etymology: 人民 (the people) + 币 (currency, money).

examples.chinese: 这本书多少钱？二十人民币。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duōshao qián? Èrshí rén mín bì.
examples.english: How much is this book? Twenty Renminbi.

examples.chinese: 我现在用手机付人民币。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòng shǒujī fù rén mín bì.
examples.english: I pay in RMB using my phone now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The formal name. In daily speech, '钱' (money) or '块' (yuan) is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person's (人) birth and life (生). The whole rollercoaster ride from start to finish.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 生 (life, birth).

examples.pinyin: Rén shēng jiù xiàng yī chǎng lǚxíng.
examples.english: Life is like a journey.

examples.chinese: 这是他人生中最重要的一天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā rén shēng zhōng zuì zhòngyào de yī tiān.
examples.english: This is the most important day of his life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Philosophical, refers to the human life experience, not biological '生命'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People (人) of a category/type (类). The whole human species.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 类 (category, type).

examples.pinyin: Rén lèi yǐjīng dēng shàngguo yuèqiú.
examples.english: Humankind has already landed on the moon.

examples.chinese: 保护环境对人类很重要。
examples.pinyin: Bǎohù huánjìng duì rén lèi hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: Protecting the environment is very important for humanity.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A collective, scientific term for the human species.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A group (群) of people (人). A gathering or throng.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (person) + 群 (group, flock).

examples.chinese: 广场上聚集了一大群人群。
examples.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng shàng jùjí le yī dà qún rén qún.
examples.english: A large crowd gathered in the square.

examples.chinese: 他在人群中一眼就看到了我。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài rén qún zhōng yī yǎn jiù kàn dào le wǒ.
examples.english: He spotted me in the crowd at first glance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Note the potential redundancy: '一群人' is more common for 'a crowd'. '人群' often stands alone or with '在...中'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You take (取) the meeting and extinguish (消) it - cancel it.
vocabulary.etymology: 取 means to take, 消 means to disappear or extinguish. Combined, it means to 'take something away and make it disappear' – cancel.

examples.chinese: 因为下雨，我们取消了野餐。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, wǒmen qǔxiāo le yěcān.
examples.english: We cancelled the picnic because of the rain.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qǔxiāo wǒ de dìngdān.
examples.english: I want to cancel my order.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with plans, orders, reservations, and events.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a hand (爫) and a boat (舟-like shape), handing you something to RECEIVE, or something sinking to SUFFER.
vocabulary.etymology: The original character depicts a hand (爫) passing an object to a recipient (冖 and 又). The core meaning is 'to receive', which extends to 'to suffer' (receive something bad).

examples.chinese: 我收到了你的礼物，非常感谢！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōu dào le nǐ de lǐwù, fēicháng gǎnxiè!
examples.english: I received your gift, thank you very much!

examples.pinyin: Tā zuótiān shòu le shāng.
examples.english: He got injured yesterday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile verb. Can be passive (受批评 - be criticized). Also used in many common compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You SUFFER (受) physical DAMAGE (伤).
vocabulary.etymology: 受 (receive/suffer) + 伤 (wound/injury) = receive an injury.

examples.chinese: 踢足球的时候要小心，别受伤。
examples.pinyin: Tī zúqiú de shíhou yào xiǎoxīn, bié shòu shāng.
examples.english: Be careful when playing soccer, don't get injured.

examples.chinese: 他的腿受伤了，所以没来上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shòushāng le, suǒyǐ méi lái shàngbān.
examples.english: His leg was injured, so he didn't come to work.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used alone (我受伤了) or with a body part as subject (我的手受伤了).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a caterpillar that CHANGES (变) BECOMING (为) a butterfly.
vocabulary.etymology: 变 (to change) + 为 (to act as/to be) = change into being (something else).

examples.chinese: 那个小镇已经变为一个现代化城市。
examples.pinyin: Nàge xiǎo zhèn yǐjīng biàn wéi yīgè xiàndàihuà chéngshì.
examples.english: That small town has changed into a modern city.

examples.pinyin: Shuǐ jiā rè huì biàn wéi shuǐzhēngqì.
examples.english: Water will turn into steam when heated.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for a significant or complete transformation. Very similar to '变成'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a stone carving with TEN (十) lines of MOUTH (口) stories from long ago.
vocabulary.etymology: An ideogram; one interpretation depicts a memorial tablet with inscriptions, symbolizing things from antiquity.

examples.chinese: 这座城市有很多古建筑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō gǔ jiànzhú.
examples.english: This city has many ancient buildings.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì Hàncháo de gǔwù.
examples.english: This is an ancient artifact from the Han dynasty.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to things from the distant past (centuries+). Often used in compound words.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ANCIENT (古) TIMES/GENERATIONS (代).
vocabulary.etymology: 古 (ancient) + 代 (generation/era) = ancient era.

examples.chinese: 我对中国古代的历史很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó gǔdài de lìshǐ hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I'm very interested in ancient Chinese history.

examples.pinyin: Gǔdài de rén méiyǒu shǒujī.
examples.english: People in ancient times didn't have phones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common historical period term.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Another (另) one (一) side (方面) of the story.
vocabulary.etymology: 另 (another) + 一 (one) + 方面 (aspect/side) = another aspect.

examples.chinese: 这个工作钱多。另一方面，它非常累。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngzuò qián duō. Lìng yī fāngmiàn, tā fēicháng lèi.
examples.english: This job pays well. On the other hand, it's very tiring.

examples.chinese: 他很有经验，但另一方面，他年纪大了。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yǒu jīngyàn, dàn lìng yī fāngmiàn, tā niánjì dà le.
examples.english: He is very experienced, but on the other hand, he's getting old.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to introduce a contrasting point or a different perspective.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think 'another OUTSIDE (外)' option.
vocabulary.etymology: 另 (another) + 外 (outside) = another (one) outside (the current set).

examples.chinese: 我还有另外一件事要告诉你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái yǒu lìngwài yī jiàn shì yào gàosù nǐ.
examples.english: I have another thing to tell you.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen fēnkāi zǒu, lìngwài zàijiàn.
examples.english: Let's go separately, see you later.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common. Can modify nouns (另外的人), act as an adverb (另外买), or start a new sentence (另外，...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: JUST (只) have to make do with what's GOOD (好) enough.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only/just) + 好 (good) = only (this) is good (as a course of action).

examples.chinese: 公共汽车没了，我只好走路回家。
examples.pinyin: Gōnggòng qìchē méi le, wǒ zhǐhǎo zǒulù huí jiā.
examples.english: The bus is gone, so I have to walk home.

examples.chinese: 他不同意，我们只好明天再谈。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù tóngyì, wǒmen zhǐhǎo míngtiān zài tán.
examples.english: He doesn't agree, so we can only talk again tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses reluctant acceptance of the only available option. Often precedes a verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: JUST (只) IS (是) nothing more.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 是 (to be) = it's only.

examples.chinese: 别生气，我只是开个玩笑。
examples.pinyin: Bié shēngqì, wǒ zhǐshì kāi gè wánxiào.
examples.english: Don't be mad, I was just joking.

examples.chinese: 我不是不帮忙，只是现在没时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bùshì bù bāngmáng, zhǐshì xiànzài méi shíjiān.
examples.english: It's not that I won't help, it's just that I don't have time now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to soften a statement, limit scope, or introduce a mild contrasting explanation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: ONLY (只) when you HAVE (有) this condition.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 有 (to have) = only have (this one condition/person).

examples.pinyin: Zhǐyǒu nǔlì, cáinéng chénggōng.
examples.english: Only if you work hard can you succeed.

examples.chinese: 现在家里只有我一个人。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài jiālǐ zhǐyǒu wǒ yīgè rén.
examples.english: Right now, there's only me at home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to set a necessary condition. Often paired with '才' (cái) to indicate 'only then'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: CAN (可) make you HAPPY (乐) drink.
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic and semantic translation: 可 (can) + 乐 (joy/happiness) = a drink that brings joy.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē kělè háishì xuěbì?
examples.english: Do you want to drink cola or Sprite?

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ yī bēi bīng kělè.
examples.english: Give me a glass of iced cola.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In casual conversation, often specifically refers to Coca-Cola. Can be used as a generic term for cola.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone you CAN (可) LEAN ON (靠).
vocabulary.etymology: 可 (can) + 靠 (to lean on/to depend on) = can be depended on.

examples.chinese: 他是一个很可靠的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yīgè hěn kěkào de péngyou.
examples.english: He is a very reliable friend.

examples.chinese: 这个消息的来源可靠吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi de láiyuán kěkào ma?
examples.english: Is the source of this news reliable?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes people, information, things, or systems. Can be used as 很可靠/不可靠.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of the stage (Tái) on a talk show.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally a pictograph of a raised platform or pedestal. Used phonetically for 'Taiwan'.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì Táizhōng rén.
examples.english: He's from Taichung, Taiwan.

examples.pinyin: Zhǔchírén zǒu dào le tái qián.
examples.english: The host walked to the front of the stage.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Primarily used as an abbreviation for 台湾 (Taiwan). Also a common word in compounds meaning platform, stage, or counter.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A box for EACH item, with a MOUTH (口) to say 'EVERY one'.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a foot arriving at a destination, later borrowed to mean 'each' (arriving at each one).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā gè ná yīgè píngguǒ.
examples.english: Please, everyone take one apple each.

examples.pinyin: Gè rén yǒu gè rén de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: Each person has their own way of thinking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before nouns or verbs to indicate 'each'. Often used in fixed phrases (各位, 各种).

vocabulary.mnemonic: EACH (各) POSITION/PERSON (位) – every person present.
vocabulary.etymology: 各 (each) + 位 (position/person [polite]) = each person.

examples.chinese: 各位老师、各位同学，大家好！
examples.pinyin: Gèwèi lǎoshī, gèwèi tóngxué, dàjiā hǎo!
examples.english: Dear teachers and classmates, hello everyone!

examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè gèwèi jīntiān de dàolái.
examples.english: Thank you all for coming today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal/polite way to address a group. Used at the beginning of speeches or announcements.

vocabulary.mnemonic: EACH (各) PLACE (地).
vocabulary.etymology: 各 (each) + 地 (place/location) = each place.

examples.chinese: 中国的各地都有好吃的。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de gèdì dōu yǒu hǎochī de.
examples.english: Every region of China has delicious food.

examples.chinese: 这个产品在全国各地都能买到。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn zài quánguó gèdì dōu néng mǎi dào.
examples.english: This product can be bought everywhere across the country.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used after a larger area (e.g., 中国各地, 世界各地).

vocabulary.mnemonic: EACH (各) KIND (种).
vocabulary.etymology: 各 (each) + 种 (kind/type) = each kind.

examples.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: The supermarket has all kinds of fruit.

examples.chinese: 他试了各种方法，都没成功。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì le gèzhǒng fāngfǎ, dōu méi chénggōng.
examples.english: He tried all sorts of methods, but none worked.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used directly before a noun to describe diversity. Very common in everyday speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: EACH (各) SELF (自).
vocabulary.etymology: 各 (each) + 自 (self) = each self/own.

examples.chinese: 会议结束后，大家各自回家。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì jiéshù hòu, dàjiā gèzì huí jiā.
examples.english: After the meeting ended, everyone went home separately.

examples.chinese: 你们有各自的问题，要自己解决。
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen yǒu gèzì de wèntí, yào zìjǐ jiějué.
examples.english: You each have your own problems to solve yourselves.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes individuality or separate action within a group.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A LID (亼) covering a BOX (口) – fitting together.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a lid fitting tightly on a container, signifying joining or closing.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū gě shàng.
examples.english: Please close the book.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè yánsè hěn hé.
examples.english: These two colors go well together.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile character with many readings. Here at HSK3, 'hé' is primary, but 'gě' (a measure word for pints) is also listed. The examples focus on 'hé'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: People JOIN (合) forces to WORK (作).
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (join/combine) + 作 (to do/work) = to work together.

examples.chinese: 我们需要合作才能完成这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào hézuò cáinéng wánchéng zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: We need to cooperate to finish this project.

examples.pinyin: Gǎnxiè nín de hézuò.
examples.english: Thank you for your cooperation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in both business and casual contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It COMBINES/FITS (合) the required STANDARD (格).
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to fit) + 格 (standard/criterion) = fitting the standard.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yīgè hégé de yīshēng.
examples.english: He is a qualified doctor.

examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn zhìliàng hégé.
examples.english: The quality of this product meets the standard.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for people (qualified), products (up to standard), or test results (passing).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It FITS (合) within the LAW (法).
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to fit) + 法 (law) = fitting within the law.

examples.chinese: 在中国，18岁才能合法开车。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, shíbā suì cáinéng héfǎ kāichē.
examples.english: In China, you can drive legally only at 18.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā de héfǎ shōurù.
examples.english: This is his legal income.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Opposite of 非法 (illegal).

vocabulary.mnemonic: FITS (合) LOGIC/REASON (理).
vocabulary.etymology: 合 (to fit) + 理 (reason/logic) = fitting reason, logical.

examples.chinese: 我觉得你的要求很合理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde nǐ de yāoqiú hěn hélǐ.
examples.english: I think your request is very reasonable.

examples.pinyin: Zhège jiěshì bù hélǐ.
examples.english: This explanation is not reasonable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe ideas, requests, prices, explanations, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: AFTER (后) next YEAR (年).
vocabulary.etymology: 后 (behind/after) + 年 (year) = the year after (this upcoming one).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hòunián dàxué bìyè.
examples.english: I will graduate from university the year after next.

examples.chinese: 我们计划后年去日本旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà hòunián qù Rìběn lǚxíng.
examples.english: We plan to travel to Japan the year after next.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to two years from the current year. Sequence: 去年 (last year), 今年 (this year), 明年 (next year), 后年.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a story being '传' (passed on) and '说' (spoken) from person to person over generations.
vocabulary.etymology: 传 means to pass on or transmit; 说 means to speak or say. Together, they mean something spoken and passed down.

examples.chinese: 这是一个关于龙的有趣传说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè guān yú lóng de yǒu qù chuán shuō.
examples.english: This is an interesting legend about a dragon.

examples.chinese: 传说那个地方以前是个皇宫。
examples.pinyin: Chuán shuō nà ge dì fang yǐ qián shì ge huáng gōng.
examples.english: It is said that place used to be an imperial palace.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, it's a legend/folklore. As a verb, it's used in passive constructions like '据说'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The left part 亻is a person, and the right 殳 was an ancient weapon. A person + weapon = injured.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant wound or injury. Composed of 亻(person) and 殳 (an ancient weapon or strike), indicating harm to a person.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shàng yǒu yī chù shāng.
examples.english: There's a wound on his leg.

examples.pinyin: Bié luàn pǎo, xiǎo xīn shāng dào zì jǐ.
examples.english: Don't run around, be careful not to injure yourself.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a verb-object like '伤到 (shāng dào)' meaning 'to hurt'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your heart (心) is injured (伤). Think of a broken heart emoji.
vocabulary.etymology: 伤 means to injure; 心 means heart. Literally, 'injured heart'.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu diū le, tā hěn shāng xīn.
examples.english: He's very sad because the puppy is lost.

examples.pinyin: Bié wèi zhè jiàn shì shāng xīn le.
examples.english: Don't be sad about this.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a state of deep sadness, more intense than '难过'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your body (体) meets (会) a situation and understands it from within.
vocabulary.etymology: 体 means body or personal; 会 means to meet or understand. It implies understanding gained through personal physical/mental engagement.

examples.chinese: 这次旅行让我体会到了农村生活。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚ xíng ràng wǒ tǐ huì dào le nóng cūn shēng huó.
examples.english: This trip let me experience rural life.

examples.chinese: 你有什么特别的体会吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shén me tè bié de tǐ huì ma?
examples.english: Do you have any special realizations?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the internal, personal understanding gained from an experience.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It makes an abstract quality '现' (appear) in a concrete '体' (body/form). Like a mirror reflecting.
vocabulary.etymology: 体 means body or form; 现 means to appear or manifest. To make something appear in a tangible form.

examples.chinese: 他的行动体现了他的善良。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xíng dòng tǐ xiàn le tā de shàn liáng.
examples.english: His actions reflect his kindness.

examples.chinese: 这个设计体现了现代风格。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shè jì tǐ xiàn le xiàn dài fēng gé.
examples.english: This design embodies a modern style.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used when an abstract concept (spirit, quality, principle) becomes visible in something concrete.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Use your '体' (body) to '验' (test/verify) something firsthand, like riding a rollercoaster.
vocabulary.etymology: 体 means body or personal; 验 means to test or examine. It implies a personal, often firsthand, test or trial of something.

measure_word.example: 一次体验 (yī cì tǐ yàn)

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tǐ yàn yī xià bèng jí.
examples.english: I want to try bungee jumping.

examples.chinese: 这次文化体验非常有趣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì wén huà tǐ yàn fēi cháng yǒu qù.
examples.english: This cultural experience was very interesting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the act of personally trying or undergoing something, often for the first time.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something '作' (made/created) and ranked as a '品' (item/product). Think of a finished painting.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 means to make or create; 品 means article or product. A created product, especially of art or intellect.

measure_word.example: 一部作品 (yī bù zuò pǐn)

examples.chinese: 这是我最喜欢的艺术作品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zuì xǐ huān de yì shù zuò pǐn.
examples.english: This is my favorite piece of artwork.

examples.pinyin: Tā fā biǎo le tā de xīn zuò pǐn.
examples.english: He published his new work.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for creative outputs: books, paintings, music, films, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The '者' (person) who '作' (makes/creates) something.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 means to make or create; 者 is a nominalizer meaning 'the one who'. The one who creates.

measure_word.example: 一位作者 (yī wèi zuò zhě)

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de zuò zhě hěn yǒu míng.
examples.english: The author of this book is very famous.

examples.chinese: 你知道这篇文章的作者是谁吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhī dào zhè piān wén zhāng de zuò zhě shì shéi ma?
examples.english: Do you know who the author of this article is?

vocabulary.usage_notes: General term for the creator of a written, artistic, or musical work.

vocabulary.english: to make; to cause; to use
vocabulary.mnemonic: It 'makes' something happen. Think of an arrow causing an action.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person (亻) with a tool (吏, official), implying sending or causing someone to act. Evolved to mean 'to cause'.

examples.chinese: 这个消息使他非常高兴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiāo xi shǐ tā fēi cháng gāo xìng.
examples.english: This news made him very happy.

examples.chinese: 你能使一下这个工具吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shǐ yī xià zhè ge gōng jù ma?
examples.english: Can you use this tool?

vocabulary.usage_notes: In casual speech, '让' is more common for 'to make/cause'. '使' is slightly more formal/written.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) guarding a child (子) under a roof (口-like), like a shield.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 亻(person) and 呆 (ancient form for 'to raise a child'), meaning to protect or nurture.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ huì bǎo nǐ ān quán.
examples.english: I will keep you safe.

examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Bǎo.
examples.english: His surname is Bao.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compound words. Rarely used alone in modern casual speech except in fixed phrases or as a surname.

vocabulary.english: to save; to preserve (like a file)
vocabulary.mnemonic: '保' (protect) it so it '存' (exists/stores) for later. Like saving a computer file.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to protect; 存 means to exist or store. To protect and keep in existence.

examples.pinyin: Jì de bǎo cún nǐ de wén jiàn.
examples.english: Remember to save your document.

examples.chinese: 这些老照片保存得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiē lǎo zhào piàn bǎo cún de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: These old photos are preserved very well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for digital files (保存文件) or preserving physical items in good condition.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The person who '保' (protects) '安' (safety/peace).
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to protect; 安 means peace or safety. Protection and safety.

measure_word.example: 一个保安 (yī gè bǎo ān)

examples.pinyin: Dà lóu mén kǒu yǒu ge bǎo ān.
examples.english: There's a security guard at the building entrance.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo qū de bǎo ān xì tǒng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The residential compound's security system is very good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the person (security guard) or the concept/ department (security).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '保' (guard) and '护' (defend) together - double protection!
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to protect; 护 means to guard or defend. A reinforced meaning of guarding.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào bǎo hù huán jìng.
examples.english: We must protect the environment.

examples.pinyin: Mā ma zǒng shì xiǎng bǎo hù wǒ.
examples.english: Mom always wants to protect me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and versatile word for protection, from people to ideas to the environment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '保' (preserve) a certain '持' (hold/grasp). Like pressing pause to keep things the same.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to preserve; 持 means to hold. To hold and preserve a state.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎo chí ān jìng.
examples.english: Please keep quiet.

examples.chinese: 他一直保持着乐观的态度。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī zhí bǎo chí zhe lè guān de tài dù.
examples.english: He has always maintained an optimistic attitude.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for maintaining an abstract state, condition, or attitude over time.

vocabulary.english: to keep; to reserve; to retain
vocabulary.mnemonic: '保' (preserve) and '留' (leave behind) — keep it and don't let it go.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to preserve; 留 means to stay or remain. To cause something to remain preserved.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎo liú le wǒ de jiù wán jù.
examples.english: I kept my old toys.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng wèi wǒ bǎo liú yī gè wèi zi.
examples.english: Please reserve a seat for me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean physically keeping something, reserving something (like a seat), or retaining an opinion/right.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '保' (ensure) and '证' (proof) — I give you proof it will happen.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to ensure; 证 means proof or certificate. To provide proof of certainty.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎo zhèng míng tiān yī dìng dào.
examples.english: I guarantee I'll be there tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 这个产品有一年的质量保证。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chǎn pǐn yǒu yī nián de zhì liàng bǎo zhèng.
examples.english: This product has a one-year quality guarantee.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A strong word for promising something will definitely happen or be true.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It '保' (protects) you from '险' (danger/risk). The paper (policy) that gives you safety.
vocabulary.etymology: 保 means to protect; 险 means danger or risk. Protection against risk.

measure_word.example: 一份保险 (yī fèn bǎo xiǎn)

examples.pinyin: Nǐ mǎi jiàn kāng bǎo xiǎn le ma?
examples.english: Have you bought health insurance?

examples.pinyin: Zhè yàng zuò bǐ jiào bǎo xiǎn.
examples.english: Doing it this way is safer/more secure.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, it's insurance. As an adjective, it means safe/secure/reliable (colloquial).

vocabulary.mnemonic: '信' (believe) and '任' (assign responsibility) someone — you trust them with tasks.
vocabulary.etymology: 信 means to believe or letter; 任 means to assign or responsibility. To believe in someone enough to give them responsibility.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wán quán xìn rèn nǐ.
examples.english: I trust you completely.

examples.pinyin: Xìn rèn shì yǒu yì de jī chǔ.
examples.english: Trust is the foundation of friendship.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger than just '相信'. It implies trust based on reliability and confidence in someone's character.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The '封' (seal) for your '信' (letter).
vocabulary.etymology: 信 means letter; 封 means to seal or envelope. The thing that seals a letter.

measure_word.example: 一个信封 (yī gè xìn fēng)

examples.chinese: 我需要一个信封来寄信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào yī gè xìn fēng lái jì xìn.
examples.english: I need an envelope to mail the letter.

examples.pinyin: Bǎ zhào piàn fàng jìn xìn fēng lǐ.
examples.english: Put the photo into the envelope.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Standard word for envelope. The '封' is also the measure word for letters (一封信).

vocabulary.english: to repair; to fix; to study (a subject)
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) with tools (like 彡 representing strokes/decoration) fixing something. Think of a wrench.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted decorative patterns (彡) and a person (亻), meaning to adorn or decorate. Meaning extended to repairing/improving something.

examples.chinese: 我的手机坏了，你能修吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒu jī huài le, nǐ néng xiū ma?
examples.english: My phone is broken, can you fix it?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài dà xué xiū guo zhōng wén.
examples.english: I studied Chinese in university.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for physical repair. Also means 'to take a course' in an academic context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '修' (tweak/improve) and then '改' (change) it. Like editing an essay.
vocabulary.etymology: 修 means to repair or adorn; 改 means to change. To change something for improvement.

examples.chinese: 我需要修改一下我的文章。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào xiū gǎi yī xià wǒ de wén zhāng.
examples.english: I need to revise my essay a bit.

examples.chinese: 计划有修改，请看一下邮件。
examples.pinyin: Jì huà yǒu xiū gǎi, qǐng kàn yī xià yóu jiàn.
examples.english: The plan has been modified, please check your email.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for revising documents, plans, software code, etc.

vocabulary.english: to be worth; to be on duty; value
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (亻) standing straight (直) guarding something of value, or assessing its worth.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 亻(person) and 直 (straight, upright). Originally meant to meet face-to-face, later extended to 'be worth' (as in a straight exchange).

examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn zhí liǎng bǎi kuài.
examples.english: This meal is worth two hundred yuan.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān lún dào wǒ zhí rì.
examples.english: It's my turn to be on duty today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb: 1) to be worth X money, 2) to be on duty. As a noun: value (e.g., 价值观).

vocabulary.english: to be worth it; to deserve
vocabulary.mnemonic: If something '值' (has value) and you '得' (get/obtain) it, it's worth it!
vocabulary.etymology: 值 means to be worth; 得 means to obtain. Worth obtaining.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng zhí de yī kàn.
examples.english: This movie is worth watching.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de nǔ lì zhí de biǎo yáng.
examples.english: Your hard work deserves praise.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Always followed by a verb or verb phrase. 值得 + V (e.g., 值得去, 值得买).

vocabulary.english: to be a guest (at someone's home)
vocabulary.mnemonic: You '做' (act as) a '客' (guest). You're not the host, you're visiting.
vocabulary.etymology: 做 means to act as; 客 means guest. To act in the role of a guest.

examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ qù péng you jiā zuò kè.
examples.english: I'm going to a friend's house as a guest this weekend.

examples.pinyin: Huān yíng lái wǒ jiā zuò kè!
examples.english: Welcome to come to my home as a guest!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically means visiting someone's home socially. The host is 主人.

vocabulary.english: to be full of; filled with
vocabulary.mnemonic: '充' (fill up) until it's '满' (full). Like a balloon filling with air.
vocabulary.etymology: 充 means to fill or sufficient; 满 means full. To fill to fullness.

examples.pinyin: Fáng jiān lǐ chōng mǎn le xiào shēng.
examples.english: The room was filled with laughter.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì wèi lái chōng mǎn xī wàng.
examples.english: He is full of hope for the future.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for abstract things (hope, joy, energy) or atmospheres/sounds. Followed by 着 or 了.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a person (民) working the NONG-lands (农).
vocabulary.etymology: 农 (agriculture) + 民 (people). It literally means 'agricultural people'.

measure_word.example: 一个农民 (yī gè nóng mín)

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye yǐqián shì nóng mín.
examples.english: My grandpa was a farmer in the past.

examples.chinese: 这里的农民每天很早起床。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de nóng mín měi tiān hěn zǎo qǐchuáng.
examples.english: The farmers here get up very early every day.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general term for people who farm for a living.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like two icicles (夂) hanging under a roof.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictograph originally representing the end of a year, when the harvest is stored. It came to represent the cold season.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié shì dōng.
examples.english: My favorite season is winter.

examples.pinyin: Běijīng dōngtiān xià xuě ma?
