examples.english: He is the director of the research institute.

examples.pinyin: Suǒzhǎng zhèngzài kāihuì.
examples.english: The director is in a meeting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A specific title for the head of an institute, office, or station (e.g., 派出所所长).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The branch (指) of your hand (手).
vocabulary.etymology: 手 (shǒu) 'hand'. 指 (zhǐ) 'finger; to point', from 扌(hand) + 旨 (meaning). The part of the hand that points.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn qiē dào le shǒuzhǐ.
examples.english: I accidentally cut my finger.

examples.chinese: 他竖起一根手指让我安静。
examples.pinyin: Tā shù qǐ yī gēn shǒuzhǐ ràng wǒ ānjìng.
examples.english: He held up a finger to tell me to be quiet.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The hand (手) work of continuing (续) something officially.
vocabulary.etymology: 手 (shǒu) 'hand', implying manual/human process. 续 (xù) 'to continue, sequence'. The sequence of steps to be handled.

examples.pinyin: Bàn qiānzhèng de shǒuxù hěn máfan.
examples.english: The visa application procedure is very troublesome.

examples.chinese: 我们得先办完这些手续。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen děi xiān bàn wán zhèxiē shǒuxù.
examples.english: We need to finish these formalities first.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always used in the context of official or bureaucratic processes.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The capability (能) you are made of/talent (才).
vocabulary.etymology: 才 (cái) originally meant 'just now', but in this context means 'innate quality, talent'. 能 (néng) 'ability, capability'. Innate capability.

examples.chinese: 他在音乐方面很有才能。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīnyuè fāngmiàn hěn yǒu cáinéng.
examples.english: He has great talent in music.

examples.pinyin: Fāhuī nǐ de cáinéng!
examples.english: Make use of your talents!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes innate or special talent, not just general skill.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'hit' (打) around with your ears (听) to get information.
vocabulary.etymology: 打 (dǎ) here functions as a verb prefix with an extensive meaning. 听 (tīng) 'to listen'. To listen around by asking questions.

examples.chinese: 我帮你打听一下火车票的事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bāng nǐ dǎtīng yīxià huǒchē piào de shì.
examples.english: I'll help you ask about the train tickets.

examples.chinese: 别到处打听别人的私事。
examples.pinyin: Bié dàochù dǎtīng biérén de sīshì.
examples.english: Don't go around asking about other people's private business.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies asking around, often about news or information not publicly available.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Hit (打) until it's broken/split (破).
vocabulary.etymology: 打 (dǎ) 'to hit'. 破 (pò) 'broken, to break'. To hit and break something.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn bié dǎpò bēizi.
examples.english: Be careful not to break the glass.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎpò le shìjiè jìlù.
examples.english: He broke the world record.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (break an object) or figuratively (break a record, a deadlock).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A document is critiqued (批) and given the standard (准) OK.
vocabulary.etymology: 批 (pī) 'to criticize, to comment (on documents)'. 准 (zhǔn) 'standard, to permit'. To comment and permit according to standards.

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn pīzhǔn le wǒ de jiàqī.
examples.english: The boss approved my vacation.

examples.chinese: 这个计划需要领导批准。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà xūyào lǐngdǎo pīzhǔn.
examples.english: This plan needs the leader's approval.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in formal or official contexts, often from a higher authority.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To critique (批) and evaluate (评).
vocabulary.etymology: 批 (pī) 'to critique, to comment'. 评 (píng) 'to evaluate, to judge'. To judge and comment, often negatively.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī pīpíng tā shàngkè chídào.
examples.english: The teacher criticized him for being late to class.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiēshòu nǐ de pīpíng.
examples.english: I accept your criticism.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually implies negative criticism or fault-finding.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The skill (术) of your hand/craft (技).
vocabulary.etymology: 技 (jì) 'skill, ability', from 扌(hand) + 支 (support). 术 (shù) 'art, method'. The art/method of a skill.

examples.pinyin: Tā de diànnǎo jìshù hěn bàng.
examples.english: His computer skills are great.

examples.pinyin: Xiàndài jìshù fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
examples.english: Modern technology develops very fast.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to broad 'technology' or personal 'technical skill'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'hand' that helps you handle sentences. Think of grabbing the object.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand holding a sickle, meaning 'to grasp, to hold'. This evolved into its grammatical use as a disposal marker.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén guān shang.
examples.english: Please close the door.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ yī bǎ yǐzi.
examples.english: Give me a chair.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Its main grammatical function is in the '把 (bǎ)' structure: Subject + 把 + Object + Verb + Other, which emphasizes the disposal of the object.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Use your hand (把) to take hold (握) of an opportunity or idea.
vocabulary.etymology: 把 (bǎ) 'to grasp, to hold'. 握 (wò) 'to grip, to hold fast'. To hold firmly in hand.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào bǎwò hǎo zhè cì jīhuì.
examples.english: You need to grasp this opportunity well.

examples.pinyin: Tā duì kǎoshì hěn yǒu bǎwò.
examples.english: He is very confident about the exam.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb: to seize/grasp. As a noun (often in 有/没把握): confidence/certainty.

vocabulary.english: to grab, to catch, to scratch
vocabulary.mnemonic: A hand (扌) with claws (爪) grabbing something.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌(hand) + 爪 (zhǎo, claw). To grasp with hand or claw.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo xǐhuan zhuā shāfā.
examples.english: Kittens like to scratch the sofa.

examples.pinyin: Kuài zhuāzhù wǒ de shǒu!
examples.english: Quick, grab my hand!

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and versatile verb for grabbing, catching, arresting, or scratching.

vocabulary.english: to grab hold of; to catch
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine using a HAND (扌) with CLAWS (爪) to GRAB and HOLD (住) something.
vocabulary.etymology: 抓 combines hand (扌) with claws/scratch (爪). 住 means to reside or stop, here giving the sense of 'holding fast'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhuā zhù le nà ge qiú.
examples.english: I caught that ball.

examples.pinyin: Kuài zhuā zhù zhè ge jī huì!
examples.english: Quickly grab this opportunity!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for both physical grasping (e.g., catching a ball) and abstract grasping (e.g., seizing an opportunity).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone with a STRONG ARM (扌/幸 ancient form) is REPORTING news, like a newspaper delivery.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted restraining a criminal (幸) and reporting (艮/服). Evolved to mean 'to report' or a 'report' (like a newspaper).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān kàn bào.
examples.english: I read the newspaper every day.

examples.chinese: 我要向老板报一下工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào xiàng lǎo bǎn bào yī xià gōng zuò.
examples.english: I need to report the work to my boss.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, often short for 报纸 (newspaper). As a verb, often part of compound verbs (e.g., 报告, 报名).

vocabulary.english: to check in; to register arrival
vocabulary.mnemonic: You REPORT (报) that you have ARRIVED (到) at school or a new job.
vocabulary.etymology: 报 (to report) + 到 (to arrive). Literally 'report arrival'.

examples.pinyin: Xīn shēng jīn tiān qù xué xiào bào dào.
examples.english: New students go to school to register today.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiǔ diǎn lái gōng sī bào dào.
examples.english: I'll come to the company to check in at 9 o'clock.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for formal registration upon arriving at a new workplace, school, camp, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A REPORTER (报) GUIDES (导) you through the news story.
vocabulary.etymology: 报 (to report) + 道 (path, way, to guide). Originally meant to report along proper channels. Now means news reporting.

examples.chinese: 他报道了那场足球比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā bào dào le nà chǎng zú qiú bǐ sài.
examples.english: He reported on that football match.

examples.chinese: 我看了一篇关于他的报道。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàn le yī piān guān yú tā de bào dào.
examples.english: I read a news report about him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a verb (to report news) or a noun (a news report/article). Pronounced the same as 报到 but different meaning.

vocabulary.english: to pat; to clap; to take (a photo)
vocabulary.mnemonic: A HAND (扌) goes WHITE (白) from clapping or from a camera's flash.
vocabulary.etymology: 扌 (hand) + 白 (white). Possibly depicting a hand clapping (making a white impression) or patting something to make it clean/white.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ pāi zhāng zhào piàn ba.
examples.english: Take a photo for me, please.

examples.pinyin: Dà jiā wèi biǎo yǎn zhě pāi shǒu.
examples.english: Everyone clapped for the performer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very versatile: 拍照片 (take a photo), 拍手 (clap hands), 拍桌子 (slap the table), 拍电影 (make a film).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine HOLDING (持) a thread that CONNECTS (续) one moment to the next, making time CONTINUE.
vocabulary.etymology: 持 (to hold, maintain) + 续 (to continue, connect). Literally 'hold and continue'.

examples.pinyin: Yǔ chí xù xià le sān tiān.
examples.english: The rain lasted for three days.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào chí xù nǔ lì.
examples.english: We need to make sustained efforts.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes an uninterrupted continuation over a period of time. Often used before verbs (持续 + V).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You use your HAND (扌) to hook something over TWO (两个) points, like a coat HANGER.
vocabulary.etymology: 扌 (hand) + 圭 (a type of jade tablet, possibly representing something to hang or a phonetic component).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yī fu guà zài yī guì lǐ.
examples.english: I hung the clothes in the wardrobe.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō "zài jiàn" jiù guà le diàn huà.
examples.english: She said "goodbye" and hung up the phone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for hanging objects, putting things on a hook, and ending a phone call (挂电话).

vocabulary.english: to point (at); to refer to; finger
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person's HAND (扌) is like the SUN (日) pointing the way.
vocabulary.etymology: 扌 (hand) + 旨 (purpose, will). A hand indicating purpose or direction.

examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu zhǐ zhe dì tú.
examples.english: He pointed at the map with his finger.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cí shì zhǐ shén me?
examples.english: What does this word refer to?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean both the physical action of pointing and the abstract action of indicating/referring to something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You POINT (指) something OUT (出) from a group or conversation.
vocabulary.etymology: 指 (to point) + 出 (to go out). Literally 'point out'.

examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī zhǐ chū le wǒ de cuò wù.
examples.english: The teacher pointed out my mistake.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐ chū le wèn tí de guān jiàn.
examples.english: He pointed out the key to the problem.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for pointing out facts, mistakes, key points, etc., often in a helpful or corrective context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone POINTS (指) the ROAD/PATH (导) for you, giving GUIDANCE.
vocabulary.etymology: 指 (to point) + 导 (to guide, lead). Literally 'point and guide'.

examples.pinyin: Jiào liàn zhèng zài zhǐ dǎo qiú yuán.
examples.english: The coach is instructing the players.

examples.pinyin: Xiè xie nín de zhǐ dǎo.
examples.english: Thank you for your guidance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in educational, professional, or coaching contexts. More formal than 教 (to teach).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A HAND (扌) rests on a WOMAN (女) under a ROOF (安), like pressing a button to feel safe/secure.
vocabulary.etymology: 扌 (hand) + 安 (peace, safe). The original meaning was to press down, suppress to bring peace.

examples.pinyin: Àn zhè ge àn niǔ.
examples.english: Press this button.

examples.pinyin: Àn jì huà, wǒ men míng tiān chū fā.
examples.english: According to the plan, we leave tomorrow.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb: to press. As a preposition: 'according to', similar to 按照 but slightly more formal/concise.

vocabulary.mnemonic: PRESS (按) and FOLLOW (照) the rules on the checklist.
vocabulary.etymology: 按 (to press, according to) + 照 (to shine, illuminate, according to). Reinforces the meaning of 'acting in accordance with' something that illuminates the way.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng àn zhào shuō míng cāo zuò.
examples.english: Please operate according to the instructions.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì àn zhào tā shuō de zuò de.
examples.english: I did it according to what he said.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common preposition. Followed by a noun (计划, 规定) or a phrase (他说的). Similar to 按 but more common in spoken instructions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You LEAN ON/BASE ON (据) what people SAY (说) – it's hearsay.
vocabulary.etymology: 据 (to depend on, according to) + 说 (to say). Literally 'according to what is said'.

examples.pinyin: Jù shuō zhè jiā cān tīng hěn hǎo chī.
examples.english: It is said that this restaurant is very tasty.

examples.pinyin: Jù shuō tā yào qù Běi jīng gōng zuò.
examples.english: Reportedly, he is going to work in Beijing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to introduce information you've heard from others but can't personally confirm. Goes at the beginning of a sentence.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You ARRANGE (排) NAMES (名) in order to get a RANKING.
vocabulary.etymology: 排 (to arrange in a row) + 名 (name, fame). Literally 'arrange names'.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐ sài zhōng pái míng dì sān.
examples.english: He ranked third in the competition.

examples.pinyin: Xué xiào de pái míng hěn zhòng yào ma?
examples.english: Is the school's ranking very important?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a verb (排名第三) or a noun (学校的排名).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You CONNECT (接) and WAIT ON (待) visitors, giving them a warm RECEPTION.
vocabulary.etymology: 接 (to connect, receive) + 待 (to treat, await). Literally 'receive and treat'.

examples.pinyin: Tā fù zé jiē dài xīn kè hù.
examples.english: She is responsible for receiving new clients.

examples.pinyin: Xiè xie nǐ men de rè qíng jiē dài.
examples.english: Thank you for your warm hospitality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for formally or officially receiving guests, clients, tourists, etc. More formal than just 接.

vocabulary.english: to get close to; to approach; close/near
vocabulary.mnemonic: You CONNECT (接) and get NEAR (近) to something.
vocabulary.etymology: 接 (to connect) + 近 (near). Literally 'connect near'.

examples.pinyin: Bié jiē jìn nà zhī gǒu.
examples.english: Don't get close to that dog.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men kuài jiē jìn zhōng diǎn le.
examples.english: We are approaching the finish line.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (physically close) or abstractly (close to a goal, a certain age, etc.).

vocabulary.mnemonic: PUSH (推) something to MAKE IT MOVE (动), driving progress.
vocabulary.etymology: 推 (to push) + 动 (to move). Literally 'push to move'.

examples.pinyin: Kē jì tuī dòng le shè huì jìn bù.
examples.english: Technology has pushed forward social progress.

examples.chinese: 我们需要推动这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào tuī dòng zhè ge xiàng mù.
examples.english: We need to promote this project.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in abstract contexts like promoting development, progress, or change.

vocabulary.mnemonic: PUSH (推) something to make it WIDE/VAST (广) and known, like an advertisement.
vocabulary.etymology: 推 (to push) + 广 (wide, broad). Literally 'push to broaden'.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī zhèng zài tuī guǎng xīn chǎn pǐn.
examples.english: The company is promoting its new product.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào tuī guǎng huán bǎo lǐ niàn.
examples.english: We need to popularize environmental protection ideas.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically means to spread something (a product, idea, technology) to make it widely known and used.

vocabulary.english: to push open; to push aside
vocabulary.mnemonic: PUSH (推) something so it OPENS (开) or moves away.
vocabulary.etymology: 推 (to push) + 开 (to open). Literally 'push open'.

examples.pinyin: Tā tuī kāi mén zǒu le jìn qù.
examples.english: He pushed the door open and walked in.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhuō shàng de shū tuī kāi le.
examples.english: She pushed the books on the table aside.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for physically pushing something (like a door, window, or object) to open or move it out of the way.

vocabulary.english: to advance; to propel; to move forward
vocabulary.mnemonic: PUSH (推) something to make it ADVANCE/ENTER (进) further.
vocabulary.etymology: 推 (to push) + 进 (to advance, enter). Literally 'push forward'.

examples.chinese: 军队向前推进了十公里。
examples.pinyin: Jūn duì xiàng qián tuī jìn le shí gōng lǐ.
examples.english: The army advanced ten kilometers forward.

examples.chinese: 这次会议推进了我们的计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì huì yì tuī jìn le wǒ men de jì huà.
examples.english: This meeting moved our plan forward.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to 推动 but often emphasizes the process of making forward progress in a specific, step-by-step way.

vocabulary.english: to do in advance; ahead of schedule
vocabulary.mnemonic: LIFT (提) the time to be in FRONT (前) of the deadline.
vocabulary.etymology: 提 (to lift, raise) + 前 (front, ahead). The idea of bringing something forward in time.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men děi tí qián chū fā.
examples.english: We have to leave early.

examples.pinyin: Huì yì tí qián jié shù le.
examples.english: The meeting ended ahead of schedule.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used before a verb (提前完成) or as an adverbial phrase at the start of a sentence.

vocabulary.english: to ask a question; to pose a question
vocabulary.mnemonic: LIFT/RAISE (提) a QUESTION (问) in class.
vocabulary.etymology: 提 (to lift, raise) + 问 (to ask). The image of raising or bringing up a question.

examples.pinyin: Huān yíng tóng xué men tí wèn.
examples.english: Students are welcome to ask questions.

examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī xiàng wǒ tí wèn le.
examples.english: The teacher asked me a question.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in formal or educational settings (classrooms, presentations, Q&A sessions).

vocabulary.mnemonic: GRASP/HOLD (握) someone's HAND (手) to greet them.
vocabulary.etymology: 握 (to grasp, hold) + 手 (hand). Literally 'hold hands'.

examples.pinyin: Tā men jiàn miàn shí hù xiāng wò shǒu.
examples.english: They shook hands when they met.

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ men wò ge shǒu ba.
examples.english: Let's shake hands.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard verb for the act of shaking hands as a greeting or agreement.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You use your HAND (扌) with EFFORT (般) to MOVE a heavy box.
vocabulary.etymology: 扌 (hand) + 般 (a type, sort; originally depicted using a tool to move a boat). Combined to mean moving something with effort.

examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ bān yī xià zhè ge xiāng zi.
examples.english: Help me move this box.

examples.pinyin: Tā xià ge yuè yào bān dào Shàng hǎi.
examples.english: He is moving to Shanghai next month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for moving physical objects or for relocating oneself (搬家). For non-heavy or abstract moving, use 移动.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You MOVE (搬) your whole HOUSE/HOME (家).
vocabulary.etymology: 搬 (to move) + 家 (home, house). Literally 'move home'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men shàng ge xīng qī gāng bān jiā.
examples.english: We just moved house last week.

examples.pinyin: Bān jiā zhēn lèi a!
examples.english: Moving house is so tiring!

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard phrase for moving from one residence to another. 搬 alone can also mean this when context is clear.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'sha' sounding like 'shower' – sand gets everywhere.
vocabulary.etymology: 沙 means sand; 子 is a common suffix for nouns.

measure_word.example: 一粒沙子 (yī lì shā zi) – a grain of sand

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xié lǐ jìn shā zi le.
examples.english: I got sand in my shoe.

examples.pinyin: Hái zi men zài hǎi biān wán shā zi.
examples.english: The kids are playing with sand at the beach.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to granular particles in general, not just beach sand.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 没 (not) + 用 (use) = no use.
vocabulary.etymology: 没 means 'not'; 用 means 'use' or 'useful'.

examples.chinese: 这台旧电脑已经没用了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái jiù diàn nǎo yǐ jīng méi yòng le.
examples.english: This old computer is useless now.

examples.pinyin: Gēn tā shuō méi yòng, tā bù tīng.
examples.english: It's no use talking to him, he won't listen.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe objects or actions that are ineffective.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 住 (stop) + 意 (meaning/intention) = 'stop and focus your intention'.
vocabulary.etymology: 注 originally meant 'to pour' (concentrate); 意 means 'thought' or 'meaning'.

examples.pinyin: Guò mǎ lù yào zhù yì ān quán.
examples.english: Pay attention to safety when crossing the street.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhù yì, huì yì yào kāi shǐ le.
examples.english: Attention please, the meeting is about to start.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in warnings, instructions, and polite requests.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '活' (huó) water flowing – flowing is living.
vocabulary.etymology: Character originally depicted water flowing, representing life or liveliness.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huó dé kāi xīn yī diǎn.
examples.english: I want to live a little happier.

examples.pinyin: Zhè yú hái shì huó de!
examples.english: This fish is still alive!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe people, animals, or a flexible (不死板) way of doing things.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a 'pie' (pài) being sent to someone.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally related to a branch of water, extending to mean 'to send out'.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī pài wǒ qù Shàng hǎi chū chāi.
examples.english: The company is sending me to Shanghai on a business trip.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ pài gè chē ba.
examples.english: Let me send a car for you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for official or organizational assignments.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 浪 (wave) + 费 (expense) = 'throwing money to the waves'.
vocabulary.etymology: 浪 means 'wave' or 'unrestrained'; 费 means 'expense' or 'cost'.

examples.pinyin: Bié làng fèi shuǐ.
examples.english: Don't waste water.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zài làng fèi shí jiān.
examples.english: This is a waste of time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for time, money, resources, or opportunities.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 海 (sea) + 关 (pass/checkpoint) = checkpoint at the sea border.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally referred to a strategic pass near the sea, now the official border control agency.

measure_word.example: 一个海关官员 (yī gè hǎi guān guān yuán) – a customs officer

examples.pinyin: Guò hǎi guān de shí hou bié jǐn zhāng.
examples.english: Don't be nervous when going through customs.

examples.pinyin: Hǎi guān jiǎn chá le wǒ de xíng li.
examples.english: Customs checked my luggage.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to both the agency and the physical checkpoint.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 消 (melt away) + 失 (lose) = melt away and get lost.
vocabulary.etymology: 消 means 'to melt' or 'dissipate'; 失 means 'to lose'.

examples.pinyin: Tài yáng xiāo shī zài yún hòu miàn.
examples.english: The sun disappeared behind the clouds.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yào shi zěn me xiāo shī le?
examples.english: How did my keys disappear?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for people, objects, or abstract things (e.g., fear disappears).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 消 (melt) + 息 (rest) = information that 'melts away' uncertainty and lets you 'rest'.
vocabulary.etymology: 息 can mean 'breath' or 'news'; combined, it refers to information that spreads.

measure_word.example: 一条消息 (yī tiáo xiāo xi) – a piece of news/message

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng dào yī gè hǎo xiāo xi.
examples.english: I heard a piece of good news.

examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ fā le gè xiāo xi.
examples.english: He sent me a message.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for both personal messages (短信) and general news.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 消 (use up) + 费 (expense) = use up your money.
vocabulary.etymology: See above for 消 and 费.

examples.pinyin: Nián qīng rén xǐ huān wǎng shàng xiāo fèi.
examples.english: Young people like to shop online.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè yuè de xiāo fèi yǒu diǎn gāo.
examples.english: This month's spending is a bit high.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A more formal term for 'spending money', commonly used in economics.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like water (氵) in a deep well.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 氵(water) and 罙 (deep), pictographically representing depth.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
examples.english: This river is very deep.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì tā liǎo jiě bù shēn.
examples.english: I don't know her very well (deeply).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used literally (depth) and figuratively (profound knowledge, deep night).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 深 (deep) + 入 (enter) = enter deeply.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 深 (deep) and 入 (to enter).

examples.chinese: 我们需要深入调查这件事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào shēn rù diào chá zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: We need to investigate this matter thoroughly.

examples.chinese: 他深入思考了这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn rù sī kǎo le zhè gè wèn tí.
examples.english: He thought deeply about this problem.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for research, investigation, or thought.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 深 (deep) + 刻 (engrave) = engraved deeply.
vocabulary.etymology: 深 means deep; 刻 means to engrave or carve.

examples.chinese: 这次旅行给我留下了深刻的印象。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚ xíng gěi wǒ liú xià le shēn kè de yìn xiàng.
examples.english: This trip left a deep impression on me.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà hěn shēn kè.
examples.english: What he said was very profound.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes deep impressions, thoughts, or meanings.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 温 (warm temperature) + 暖 (sun warmth) = double warm.
vocabulary.etymology: 温 means 'warm/lukewarm'; 暖 means 'warm/sunny'.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān yáng guāng hěn wēn nuǎn.
examples.english: The sunshine is very warm today.

examples.pinyin: Xiè xie nǐ wēn nuǎn de zhù fú.
examples.english: Thank you for your warm wishes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe temperature or a warm/kind feeling.

vocabulary.english: to swim; to travel; to wander
vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a person (方) swimming in water (氵).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person with a flag crossing a river, meaning to travel on water.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐ huān zài hǎi lǐ yóu.
examples.english: I like to swim in the sea.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men qù nián yóu le Ōu zhōu.
examples.english: We traveled around Europe last year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a single verb, it often means 'to swim'. In compounds, it can mean to travel or play.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 游 (play/wander) + 戏 (drama/play) = play-play.
vocabulary.etymology: See above for 游. 戏 originally meant 'theatre' or 'play-acting'.

measure_word.example: 一个游戏 (yī gè yóu xì) – a game

examples.pinyin: Hái zi men zài wán yī gè yóu xì.
examples.english: The kids are playing a game.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐ huān shén me diàn nǎo yóu xì?
examples.english: What computer games do you like?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Covers all kinds of games: board games, video games, playground games.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 满 (full) + 足 (foot/sufficient) = 'feet are full' -> completely satisfied.
vocabulary.etymology: 满 means 'full'; 足 means 'foot' or 'sufficient'.

examples.chinese: 我对现在的生活很满足。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì xiàn zài de shēng huó hěn mǎn zú.
examples.english: I'm very satisfied with my current life.

examples.chinese: 这个结果满足了大家的要求。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè jié guǒ mǎn zú le dà jiā de yāo qiú.
examples.english: This outcome satisfied everyone's demands.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a feeling (感到满足) or an action (满足需求).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '演' (yǎn) sounding like 'yen' – actors yen to perform.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 氵(water) and 寅, originally implying 'to spread out' like water, evolving to mean 'to perform'.

examples.chinese: 他在电影里演一个警察。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diàn yǐng lǐ yǎn yī gè jǐng chá.
examples.english: He plays a policeman in the movie.

examples.pinyin: Tā chàng gē yǎn dé dōu hěn hǎo.
examples.english: She sings and acts very well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Core verb for acting in plays, movies, or any performance.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 演 (perform) + 出 (out) = perform out (on stage).
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 演 (perform) and 出 (to go out, to put out).

measure_word.example: 一场演出 (yī chǎng yǎn chū) – a performance

examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn yǒu huà jù yǎn chū.
examples.english: There's a drama performance tonight.

examples.pinyin: Yuè duì xià gè yuè huì lái yǎn chū.
examples.english: The band will come to perform next month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be the event (看演出) or the action (他们正在演出).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 演 (perform) + 员 (person/member) = performing person.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 演 (perform) and 员 (member of a group).

measure_word.example: 一位演员 (yī wèi yǎn yuán) – an actor/actress

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chéng wéi yī míng yǎn yuán.
examples.english: She wants to become an actress.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè yǎn yuán hěn shòu huān yíng.
examples.english: This actor is very popular.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A gender-neutral term for performer in film, TV, or theatre.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 演 (perform) + 唱 (sing) = perform-singing.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 演 (perform) and 唱 (sing).

examples.pinyin: Tā yǎn chàng le yī shǒu xīn gē.
examples.english: He performed a new song.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐ huān tīng tā yǎn chàng.
examples.english: I like listening to her sing (in performance).

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than just 唱; implies singing as a formal performance.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 演唱 (sing) + 会 (meeting/gathering) = singing gathering.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 演唱 (to sing/perform) and 会 (gathering).

measure_word.example: 一场演唱会 (yī chǎng yǎn chàng huì) – a concert

examples.chinese: 我们买到了演唱会的票。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men mǎi dào le yǎn chàng huì de piào.
examples.english: We managed to buy tickets for the concert.

examples.chinese: 他的演唱会门票卖得很快。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎn chàng huì mén piào mài dé hěn kuài.
examples.english: Tickets for his concert sold out quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to a pop/rock singer's live concert.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a flickering flame.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictograph of a flame.

measure_word.example: 一团火 (yī tuán huǒ) – a ball of fire

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo xīn, huǒ hěn tàng!
examples.english: Be careful, fire is hot!

examples.pinyin: Tā fā huǒ le.
examples.english: He got angry (lit. 'issued fire').

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used metaphorically for anger (发火) or popularity (很火).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 火 (fire) + 因 (cause) = smoke is caused by fire.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 火 (fire) and 因 (cause), originally meaning 'smoke from a fire'.

measure_word.example: 一根烟 (yī gēn yān) – a cigarette

examples.pinyin: Fáng jiān lǐ dōu shì yān.
examples.english: The room is full of smoke.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiè yān le.
examples.english: He quit smoking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Context determines meaning: smoke from fire or a cigarette.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 热 (hot) + 烈 (intense) = hot and intense feelings.
vocabulary.etymology: 热 means 'hot'; 烈 means 'fierce' or 'intense'.

examples.pinyin: Dà jiā rè liè huān yíng xīn tóng xué.
examples.english: Everyone gave the new classmate a warm welcome.

examples.pinyin: Tǎo lùn jìn xíng dé hěn rè liè.
examples.english: The discussion was very lively and enthusiastic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes an atmosphere, applause, or emotions that are warm and intense.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a radio tower **broadcasting** a show; '播' is sow/seeds, '出' is out — sowing the signal out to the public.
vocabulary.etymology: 播 originally meant 'to sow seeds.' 出 means 'to go/come out.' Combined, it metaphorically means to send out (information) like sowing seeds widely.

examples.chinese: 这个节目每天晚上七点播出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jiémù měi tiān wǎnshang qī diǎn bō chū.
examples.english: This program airs every night at 7 o'clock.

examples.chinese: 新电视剧下周一开始播出。
examples.pinyin: Xīn diànshìjù xià zhōuyī kāishǐ bō chū.
examples.english: The new TV drama starts airing next Monday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for TV/radio programs or official announcements.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of hitting the **play** button; '播' is broadcast, '放' is release/put — releasing the broadcast.
vocabulary.etymology: 播 (sow/broadcast) + 放 (to release, to let go). Means to release or set a broadcast or recording into motion.

examples.pinyin: Néng bāng wǒ bō fàng zhè shǒu gē ma?
examples.english: Can you help me play this song?

examples.chinese: 广告播放完就可以看电影了。
examples.pinyin: Guǎnggào bō fàng wán jiù kěyǐ kàn diànyǐng le.
examples.english: After the ad finishes playing, we can watch the movie.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for audio, video, or slideshows. Slightly more technical/device-oriented than 放 alone.

vocabulary.english: measure word for long, thin objects; to support; branch
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture a **支** of a pen, a branch, or a team — all long and thin or a division of a whole.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand holding a branch. Evolved to mean 'branch' or 'support,' and later as a measure word for stick-like items.

measure_word.example: 一支笔 (yī zhī bǐ) — a pen

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yī zhī xīn kǒuhóng.
examples.english: I bought a new lipstick.

examples.chinese: 我们公司在北京有一支团队。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī zài Běijīng yǒu yī zhī tuánduì.
examples.english: Our company has a team in Beijing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common measure word for pens, guns, troops, songs, and long, thin objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of **paying** a bill; '支' is support/branch (like a payment slip), '付' is hand over money.
vocabulary.etymology: 支 (to disburse, branch) + 付 (to hand over). Together, it means to hand over money in discharge of a debt.

examples.chinese: 请问这里可以手机支付吗？
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn zhèlǐ kěyǐ shǒujī zhīfù ma?
examples.english: Excuse me, can I pay by phone here?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng zhīfù le fángzū.
examples.english: I've already paid the rent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in modern contexts like digital payments, bills, and formal transactions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine giving someone a **support**ive hand; '支' is prop up, '持' is hold — holding someone up.
vocabulary.etymology: 支 (to prop up, support) + 持 (to hold, to maintain). Means to uphold or maintain support.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wánquán zhīchí nǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: I completely support your decision.

examples.pinyin: Xièxiè nǐ de zhīchí!
examples.english: Thank you for your support!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for moral, technical, or physical support. Can be emotional or practical.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You **listen** and **receive** a broadcast; '收' is receive, '听' is listen.
vocabulary.etymology: 收 (to receive) + 听 (to listen). Means to receive and listen, specifically to radio or audio broadcasts.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷每天收听新闻广播。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye měi tiān shōutīng xīnwén guǎngbō.
examples.english: My grandpa listens to the news broadcast every day.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīngcháng shōutīng nǎ ge diàntái?
examples.english: Which radio station do you often listen to?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost exclusively for radio, podcasts, or other scheduled audio broadcasts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You **watch** and **receive** a TV show; '收' is receive, '看' is look/watch.
vocabulary.etymology: 收 (to receive) + 看 (to look, watch). Means to receive and watch, specifically TV or video broadcasts.

examples.chinese: 欢迎大家收看我们的节目。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng dàjiā shōukàn wǒmen de jiémù.
examples.english: Welcome, everyone, to watch our program.

examples.chinese: 你昨晚收看足球比赛了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuó wǎn shōukàn zúqiú bǐsài le ma?
examples.english: Did you watch the soccer match last night?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for watching scheduled TV programs, live streams, or broadcast content.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a place that **charges** money; '收' is collect, '费' is fee — collecting fees.
vocabulary.etymology: 收 (to collect) + 费 (fee, expense). Literally 'collect fees.'

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge tíngchē chǎng shōufèi ma?
examples.english: Does this parking lot charge a fee?

examples.pinyin: Xiū shǒujī shōufèi hěn guì.
examples.english: Fixing a phone charges a high fee.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a verb-noun. The opposite is 免费 (free of charge).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A machine that **receives** **sound**; '收' receive, '音' sound, '机' machine.
vocabulary.etymology: 收 (to receive) + 音 (sound) + 机 (machine). A machine that receives sound (broadcasts).

measure_word.example: 一台收音机 (yī tái shōuyīnjī) — a radio

examples.chinese: 我爸爸有一个很老的收音机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba yǒu yī gè hěn lǎo de shōuyīnjī.
examples.english: My dad has a very old radio.

examples.chinese: 开车的时候我喜欢听收音机。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou wǒ xǐhuan tīng shōuyīnjī.
examples.english: I like to listen to the radio when driving.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the physical device. The content is 广播.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Making something better by **changing** it to **advance**; '改' change, '进' advance.
vocabulary.etymology: 改 (to change, alter) + 进 (to advance, enter). Means to change for the better, to advance through alteration.

examples.chinese: 我们需要改进学习方法。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào gǎijìn xuéxí fāngfǎ.
examples.english: We need to improve our study methods.

examples.chinese: 这个软件有了很大的改进。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎnjiàn yǒu le hěn dà de gǎijìn.
examples.english: This software has had a big improvement.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for methods, systems, quality, or processes. Focuses on making positive changes.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Completely **change** and **make** something new; '改' change, '造' make/create.
vocabulary.etymology: 改 (to change) + 造 (to make, build). Means to change and remake, often involving physical reconstruction.

examples.chinese: 他们打算改造这间旧厨房。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn gǎizào zhè jiān jiù chúfáng.
examples.english: They plan to remodel this old kitchen.

examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng zhèngzài gǎizào shēngchǎn xiàn.
examples.english: The factory is transforming its production line.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies a significant, often physical, alteration or overhaul of something existing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: **Put** it **to** a specific spot; '放' put, '到' to/until.
vocabulary.etymology: 放 (to place, put) + 到 (to, until). A verb+preposition combination indicating placement with a destination.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàng dào shūjià shàng.
examples.english: Please put the book onto the bookshelf.

examples.chinese: 我把钥匙放到抽屉里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yàoshi fàng dào chōutì lǐ le.
examples.english: I put the keys into the drawer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common daily phrase. Followed by a location. 在 (zài) can also be used, but 放到 emphasizes the action of moving to a destination.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The **old** **village** you're from; '故' old/former, '乡' village/countryside.
vocabulary.etymology: 故 (old, former, reason) + 乡 (village, countryside). Refers to one's old village or place of origin.

measure_word.example: 一个故乡 (yī gè gùxiāng) — a hometown

examples.chinese: 我的故乡是一个小城市。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de gùxiāng shì yī gè xiǎo chéngshì.
examples.english: My hometown is a small city.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn jiǔ méi huí gùxiāng le.
examples.english: I haven't been back to my hometown for a long time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has an emotional, nostalgic feel. 家乡 is more common in daily speech; 故乡 is slightly more literary.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The **effect** or **fruit** of an action; '效' effect, '果' fruit/result.
vocabulary.etymology: 效 (effect, imitate) + 果 (fruit, result). Means the resulting effect or outcome.

measure_word.example: 一种效果 (yī zhǒng xiàoguǒ) — a kind of effect

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge miànmó xiàoguǒ zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How is the effect of this face mask?

examples.pinyin: Yùndòng jiǎnféi xiàoguǒ hěn hǎo.
examples.english: Exercising has a very good effect for losing weight.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Neutral term for the outcome, whether good or bad. Common in advertising, medicine, and reviews.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone shouting "**Save** me!" with a helping hand; character looks like a hand (攵) giving aid.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 求 (to beg, seek) and 攵 (a hand holding a stick, suggesting action). Originally meant to give aid to someone in desperate need.

examples.pinyin: Kuài jiào jiùhùchē jiù rén!
examples.english: Quick, call an ambulance to save them!

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo māo shì wǒ jiù de.
examples.english: This little cat is one I rescued.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for saving lives, rescuing from danger, or helping in emergencies. 救命 (jiù mìng) means "Help!" or "Save my life!"

vocabulary.mnemonic: **Teaching** **materials**; '教' teach, '材' material.
vocabulary.etymology: 教 (to teach) + 材 (material). Materials used for teaching.

measure_word.example: 一本教材 (yī běn jiàocái) — a textbook

examples.pinyin: Zhè xuéqī de jiàocái yǒudiǎn guì.
examples.english: This semester's textbooks are a bit expensive.

examples.chinese: 老师正在准备新的教材。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhèngzài zhǔnbèi xīn de jiàocái.
examples.english: The teacher is preparing new teaching materials.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to textbooks, workbooks, or any educational resources. More formal than 课本.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone who **teaches** you to **practice**; '教' teach, '练' practice/train.
vocabulary.etymology: 教 (to teach) + 练 (to practice, train). A person who teaches and trains.

measure_word.example: 一位教练 (yī wèi jiàoliàn) — a coach (polite)

examples.chinese: 我们的篮球教练很严格。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de lánqiú jiàoliàn hěn yángé.
examples.english: Our basketball coach is very strict.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng yújiā jiàoliàn.
examples.english: She wants to be a yoga instructor.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for sports, driving, fitness, etc. A respectful title.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine someone puffing their chest, saying "I **dare** you!" The character has 耳 (ear) — listening for courage?
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand (𠬞) capturing a boar (豕), showing bravery. The modern form is a simplification.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ gǎn zuò guòshānchē ma?
examples.english: Do you dare to ride a roller coaster?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù gǎn yī gè rén zǒu yèlù.
examples.english: I don't dare to walk alone at night.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before verbs to indicate courage to do something. 不敢 means 'don't dare' or 'I'm afraid to.'

vocabulary.english: to take a walk, to stroll
vocabulary.mnemonic: **Scatter** your **steps** leisurely; '散' scatter, '步' step.
vocabulary.etymology: 散 (to scatter, disperse) + 步 (step). To walk in a leisurely, scattered way.

examples.chinese: 吃完饭我们出去散散步吧。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán fàn wǒmen chūqù sàn san bù ba.
examples.english: Let's go out for a walk after eating.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zài hé biān sànbù.
examples.english: I like to take walks by the river.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A relaxed, unhurried walk for leisure or health. Can be reduplicated: 散散步.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The **study** of **numbers**; '数' number, '学' study/ology.
vocabulary.etymology: 数 (number, to count) + 学 (study, -ology). The study of numbers and quantities.

measure_word.example: 一门数学 (yī mén shùxué) — a course of mathematics

examples.chinese: 我妹妹的数学成绩特别好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei de shùxué chéngjī tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: My younger sister's math grades are especially good.

examples.pinyin: Shùxué duì wǒ lái shuō tài nán le.
examples.english: Math is too difficult for me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A school subject. 算数 is more about basic arithmetic calculation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: How many **numbers** and how much **volume**? '数' number, '量' measure.
vocabulary.etymology: 数 (number) + 量 (to measure, quantity). The measurable number of things.

examples.chinese: 我们需要统计一下学生的数量。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào tǒngjì yīxià xuéshēng de shùliàng.
examples.english: We need to count the number of students.

examples.pinyin: Shāngpǐn shùliàng yǒuxiàn, kuài mǎi ba!
examples.english: The quantity of goods is limited, buy quickly!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to countable amount or number. Often contrasted with 质量 (quality).

vocabulary.english: whole, entire; to put in order
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of something **whole** and **neat**, or **fixing** it to be so. Looks like a hand (攵) putting things straight.
vocabulary.etymology: Derived from 正 (upright, correct) and 束 (to bind). Originally meant to correct, put in order, leading to meanings of completeness and tidiness.

examples.chinese: 我等了你整整一个小时！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le nǐ zhěngzhěng yī gè xiǎoshí!
examples.english: I waited for you a whole hour!

examples.pinyin: Bǎ nǐ de fángjiān zhěng yī zhěng.
examples.english: Tidy up your room.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective, it means whole/entire. As a verb, it means to tidy or fix. Can be reduplicated for emphasis: 整整, 整一整.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The **whole** **个** thing; '整' whole, '个' general measure word.
vocabulary.etymology: 整 (whole) + 个 (general measure word). A compound emphasizing the entirety of a single unit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhěnggè zhōumò dōu zài jiā.
examples.english: I was at home the entire weekend.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zhěnggè dàngāo dōu chī le.
examples.english: He ate the whole cake.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Modifies nouns to mean 'the whole [noun].' Very common in spoken Chinese.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The **whole** **body** or system; '整' whole, '体' body.
vocabulary.etymology: 整 (whole) + 体 (body, entity). The whole body or complete entity.

examples.chinese: 我们要从整体上考虑这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng zhěngtǐ shàng kǎolǜ zhè ge wèntí.
examples.english: We need to consider this problem as a whole.

examples.chinese: 房子的整体风格很现代。
examples.pinyin: Fángzi de zhěngtǐ fēnggé hěn xiàndài.
examples.english: The overall style of the house is very modern.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More abstract than 整个, often used for systems, concepts, or overall appearance.

vocabulary.mnemonic: **Whole** **day**; '整' whole, '天' day.
vocabulary.etymology: 整 (whole) + 天 (day). The entire day from start to finish.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān dōu zài dǎ yóuxì.
examples.english: He's been playing games all day.

examples.pinyin: Máng le yī zhěngtiān, lèi sǐ le.
examples.english: I've been busy the whole day, I'm exhausted.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common time expression. Can imply something is continuous or excessive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like 'jeng jeng' – think of the 'full jingling' of coins when you've saved the ENTIRE amount.
vocabulary.etymology: The character 整 means 'whole, complete.' Reduplication of 整 intensifies the meaning of completeness or exactness.

examples.chinese: 我等了你整整两个小时。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng le nǐ zhěng zhěng liǎng ge xiǎo shí.
examples.english: I waited for you for a full two hours.

examples.pinyin: Tā hē le zhěng zhěng yì píng shuǐ.
examples.english: He drank a whole bottle of water.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before measure words to emphasize that the quantity is the full/complete amount, often for time or countable items.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine 'arranging' (整) and 'reasoning' (理) all the clutter in your room into order.
vocabulary.etymology: 整 (to put in order) + 理 (to manage, reason). The combination means to bring things into order through arrangement.

examples.chinese: 我要整理一下我的书桌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào zhěng lǐ yīxià wǒ de shū zhuō.
examples.english: I need to tidy up my desk.

examples.chinese: 她在整理旅行用的行李。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhěng lǐ lǚxíng yòng de xíngli.
examples.english: She is organizing the luggage for the trip.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for physical spaces (rooms, desks) and abstract things like documents or thoughts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of soldiers standing in a perfectly 'whole' (整) and 'even' (齐) line.
vocabulary.etymology: 整 (whole, orderly) + 齐 (even, uniform). Together they describe a state of being orderly and uniform.

examples.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān zǒng shì hěn zhěngqí.
examples.english: His room is always very neat.

examples.chinese: 学生们排着整齐的队伍。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshēngmen pái zhe zhěngqí de duìwu.
examples.english: The students are lined up in neat rows.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe physical appearance (hair, clothes), arrangement of objects, or formations of people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'writings' (文) and 'pieces' (件) of paper or data you work with.
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (writing, document) + 件 (item, piece). Literally 'a piece of writing/document.'

examples.chinese: 这个文件很重要，别丢了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wénjiàn hěn zhòngyào, bié diū le.
examples.english: This document is important, don't lose it.

examples.chinese: 我把文件保存在电脑里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ wénjiàn bǎocún zài diànnǎo lǐ le.
examples.english: I saved the file on the computer.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical paper documents or digital computer files.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'transforming' (化) through 'language/literature' (文) – that's what culture does.
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (writing, civility) + 化 (to transform, change). Originally referred to the civilizing influence of literature and education.

examples.chinese: 我对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: I am very interested in Chinese culture.

examples.chinese: 每个地方都有自己的文化。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge dìfang dōu yǒu zìjǐ de wénhuà.
examples.english: Every place has its own culture.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A broad term encompassing customs, arts, social institutions, and ways of life of a group.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's literally the 'writings' (文) and 'characters' (字) you see on a page.
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (writing, language) + 字 (character). The term specifically refers to written symbols or script.

measure_word.example: 一个文字 (yí ge wénzì) (for a single character)

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shì gǔdài de wénzì.
examples.english: These are ancient characters/script.

examples.chinese: 他用简单的文字解释了这个概念。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng jiǎndān de wénzì jiěshì le zhège gàiniàn.
examples.english: He explained the concept using simple language.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers specifically to written characters, especially Chinese characters, but can also mean written language in general.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'study/learning' (学) of beautiful 'writings' (文).
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (writing, literature) + 学 (study, learning). The study or body of written artistic works.

examples.pinyin: Tā dàxué zhuānyè shì wénxué.
examples.english: Her university major is literature.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó wénxué.
examples.english: I like reading Chinese literature.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A society made 'bright/clear' (明) through 'culture/language' (文) is a civilization.
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (culture, civility) + 明 (bright, clear). Implies a cultured and enlightened state.

measure_word.example: 一个文明 (yí ge wénmíng) (for a civilization)

examples.pinyin: Gǔ Āijí wénmíng fēicháng yǒumíng.
examples.english: Ancient Egyptian civilization is very famous.

examples.chinese: 在公共场所要文明一点。
examples.pinyin: Zài gōnggòng chǎngsuǒ yào wénmíng yīdiǎn.
examples.english: Be more civilized in public places.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun: a civilization. As an adjective: describes polite, courteous behavior.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'chapter' (章) of 'writing' (文) – a complete piece of writing.
vocabulary.etymology: 文 (writing) + 章 (chapter, section). Originally meant a literary composition or a patterned piece of writing.

examples.chinese: 他在网上看了一篇很有意思的文章。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎngshàng kàn le yì piān hěn yǒu yìsi de wénzhāng.
examples.english: He read a very interesting article online.

examples.chinese: 老师让我们写一篇五百字的文章。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī ràng wǒmen xiě yì piān wǔ bǎi zì de wénzhāng.
examples.english: The teacher asked us to write a 500-character essay.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a non-fiction written piece, like a news article, blog post, or school essay.

vocabulary.english: to break, to sever, to disconnect
vocabulary.mnemonic: Picture an axe (斤) cutting a rope (丨 and other lines) in two – snap! It's broken.
vocabulary.etymology: The original pictograph depicted cutting silk threads with a knife, leading to the meaning 'to sever, break off.'

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn bié bǎ shéngzi nòng duàn le.
examples.english: Be careful not to break the rope.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tā zǎo jiù duàn le liánxì.
examples.english: I lost contact with him a long time ago.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for physical breaking, ending relationships, or interrupting flows (like electricity, water).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of the 'direction/form' (式) of doing something and the 'square' (方) process you follow.
vocabulary.etymology: 方 (direction, method) + 式 (pattern, style). Together they mean a patterned method or style.

examples.chinese: 每个人的学习方式都不一样。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén de xuéxí fāngshì dōu bù yīyàng.
examples.english: Everyone's learning style is different.

examples.chinese: 他用一种很特别的方式道歉。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng yì zhǒng hěn tèbié de fāngshì dàoqiàn.
examples.english: He apologized in a very special way.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More about the style or manner of doing something, while 方法 is more about the concrete method or technique.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'agency/office' (社) that plans your 'journey' (旅行).
vocabulary.etymology: 旅行 (to travel) + 社 (society, agency). An agency for travel services.

examples.chinese: 我们通过旅行社订了机票和酒店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tōngguò lǚxíngshè dìng le jīpiào hé jiǔdiàn.
examples.english: We booked the flight tickets and hotel through a travel agency.

examples.chinese: 这条街上有好几家旅行社。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shàng yǒu hǎo jǐ jiā lǚxíngshè.
examples.english: There are several travel agencies on this street.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'building/hostel' (馆) for 'travelers' (旅) to stay in.
vocabulary.etymology: 旅 (travel) + 馆 (building, establishment). A building for travelers.

examples.chinese: 我们找一家便宜的旅馆住吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo yì jiā piányi de lǚguǎn zhù ba.
examples.english: Let's find a cheap hotel to stay in.

examples.pinyin: Nàge xiǎo lǚguǎn hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: That small inn is very clean.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 旅馆 often implies a simpler, more budget-friendly accommodation than the more formal 酒店.

vocabulary.mnemonic: What happens 'every day' (日) as a matter of 'usual routine' (常).
vocabulary.etymology: 日 (sun, day) + 常 (constant, usual). Refers to the usual affairs of the day.

examples.chinese: 刷牙是我的日常生活的一部分。
examples.pinyin: Shuāyá shì wǒ de rìcháng shēnghuó de yī bùfen.
examples.english: Brushing teeth is part of my daily life.

examples.chinese: 超市里可以买到日常用品。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ kěyǐ mǎi dào rìcháng yòngpǐn.
examples.english: You can buy daily necessities at the supermarket.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as an adjective before nouns like 生活 (life), 工作 (work), 用品 (necessities).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sun (日) setting behind a bird (隹) on a perch (丨) – a scene from the 'old' days.
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional form 舊 originally depicted an owl on a perch. It came to mean 'old, former' through association with things of the past.

examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng zìxíngchē shì jiù de.
examples.english: This bicycle is old/used.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de jiù tóngshì.
examples.english: He is my former colleague.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes objects that are not new, or relationships/statuses from the past. Not usually for people's age (use 老).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Early' (早) and 'already' (已) combined – it happened way earlier than you thought.
vocabulary.etymology: 早 (early) + 已 (already). Emphasizes that something was completed at an earlier point in time.

examples.pinyin: Tā zǎo yǐ zhīdào zhè jiàn shì le.
examples.english: He already knew about this matter long ago.

examples.chinese: 电影早已开始了，我们快进去吧。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng zǎo yǐ kāishǐ le, wǒmen kuài jìnqù ba.
examples.english: The movie started a while ago, let's hurry in.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger than 已经, emphasizing that the action was completed significantly earlier, often with a hint of 'you're late to know/do this.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sun (日) moving past a temple/temple step (寺) marks the passage of 'time.'
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 時. Combines 日 (sun, day) with 寺 (temple, court). Originally meant 'season,' extended to 'time' in general.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài jǐ shí le?
examples.english: What time is it now? (somewhat formal/literary)

examples.pinyin: Sì shí biànhuà hěn míngxiǎn.
examples.english: The changes of the four seasons are very obvious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal or used in compounds (e.g., 时间, 时候, 时代). In casual speech, 时候 or 时间 is more common for 'time.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'generation' (代) defined by the 'times' (时) they live in.
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (time) + 代 (generation, to substitute). Refers to a generation or period of time with defining characteristics.

examples.chinese: 我们生活在互联网时代。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shēnghuó zài hùliánwǎng shídài.
examples.english: We live in the internet age.

examples.pinyin: Nà shì shǔyú tāmen de shídài.
examples.english: That was their era.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a significant historical period or the current zeitgeist.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A specific 'point' (刻, like a notch on a sundial) on the 'time' (时) line.
vocabulary.etymology: 时 (time) + 刻 (to carve, a quarter [of an hour], moment). Refers to a carved-out, precise moment in time.

examples.chinese: 这是我生命中最幸福的时刻。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ shēngmìng zhōng zuì xìngfú de shíkè.
examples.english: This is the happiest moment in my life.

examples.chinese: 请在关键时刻保持冷静。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài guānjiàn shíkè bǎochí lěngjìng.
examples.english: Please stay calm at the critical moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes a specific, often significant or precise, instant in time.

vocabulary.mnemonic: So 'bright' (明) and 'apparent' (显) that you can't miss it.
vocabulary.etymology: 明 (bright, clear) + 显 (to appear, manifest). Something that appears clearly.

examples.pinyin: Tā de bù gāoxìng hěn míngxiǎn.
examples.english: His unhappiness is obvious.

examples.chinese: 这两个答案有明显的区别。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng ge dá'àn yǒu míngxiǎn de qūbié.
examples.english: These two answers have a clear distinction.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to describe facts, differences, feelings, or results that are easy to see or understand.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 'bright/clear' (明) and 'accurate' (确) – no ambiguity.
vocabulary.etymology: 明 (bright, clear) + 确 (true, definite). Something that is clear and certain.

examples.chinese: 请给我一个明确的回答。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí ge míngquè de huídá.
examples.english: Please give me a clear and definite answer.

examples.chinese: 我们必须明确下一步的计划。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bìxū míngquè xià yī bù de jìhuà.
examples.english: We must clarify the next step of the plan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger than 明显; focuses on precision, definition, and lack of vagueness, often for instructions, goals, or answers.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sun (日) warming the plants and people (屯 depicts a sprouting seed) – it's spring!
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts the sun (日) shining on growing plants (the 屯 component represents a sprout). It represents the season of growth.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié shì chūn.
examples.english: My favorite season is spring.

examples.pinyin: Chūn nuǎn huā kāi.
examples.english: In warm spring, flowers bloom. (Idiom)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds like 春天 (springtime), 春节 (Spring Festival). In modern casual speech, 春天 is more common than 春 alone.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It 'manifests/obtains' (得) a certain 'appearance' (显) – how it seems to others.
vocabulary.etymology: 显 (to appear, manifest) + 得 (a particle indicating result or possibility). The result of how something appears.

examples.chinese: 你穿这件衣服显得很瘦。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ chuān zhè jiàn yīfu xiǎn de hěn shòu.
examples.english: You look very slim in this outfit.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān xiǎn de bù tài gāoxìng.
examples.english: He seems a bit unhappy today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe the impression or appearance someone/something gives. Followed by an adjective or adjective phrase.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something 'apparent' (显) and 'so/such' (然) that you exclaim 'Obviously!'
vocabulary.etymology: 显 (to appear, manifest) + 然 (suffix meaning '-ly' or 'state of'). In a state of being apparent.

examples.chinese: 他显然忘了我们的约会。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎnrán wàng le wǒmen de yuēhuì.
examples.english: He obviously forgot our appointment.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dàolǐ shì xiǎnrán de.
examples.english: This principle is obvious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a sentence or clause to state something that is self-evident from the situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To make something 'apparent' (显) and 'show' (示) it to others.
vocabulary.etymology: 显 (to appear, manifest) + 示 (to show, indicate). To cause something to be seen or shown.

examples.chinese: 手机屏幕上显示着时间。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī píngmù shàng xiǎnshì zhe shíjiān.
examples.english: The phone screen displays the time.

examples.chinese: 数据清楚地显示了问题所在。
examples.pinyin: Shùjù qīngchǔ de xiǎnshì le wèntí suǒzài.
examples.english: The data clearly shows where the problem lies.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for screens, indicators, data, evidence, or signs that present information.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a signal tower (普) spreading (及) information everywhere.
vocabulary.etymology: 普 (universal, widespread) + 及 (to reach); originally meaning 'to reach everywhere'.

examples.chinese: 现在智能手机在中国很普及。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài zhìnéng shǒujī zài Zhōngguó hěn pǔjí.
examples.english: Smartphones are very widespread in China now.

examples.chinese: 政府正在普及九年义务教育。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ zhèngzài pǔjí jiǔ nián yìwù jiàoyù.
examples.english: The government is popularizing nine-year compulsory education.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe technology, knowledge, or policies becoming common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A general (普) experience shared everywhere (遍).
vocabulary.etymology: 普 (universal) + 遍 (everywhere); meaning 'found everywhere'.

examples.chinese: 这个想法在这里很普遍。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ zài zhèlǐ hěn pǔbiàn.
examples.english: This idea is very common here.

examples.chinese: 人们普遍认为健康最重要。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen pǔbiàn rènwéi jiànkāng zuì zhòngyào.
examples.english: People generally believe health is most important.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things that are widespread or commonly accepted. Often precedes 认为 (rènwéi, to think).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The scene (景) and the colors (色) of nature.
vocabulary.etymology: 景 (scene, view) + 色 (color); literally 'the colors of a scene'.

examples.pinyin: Shān shàng de jǐngsè tài měi le!
examples.english: The scenery on the mountain is so beautiful!

examples.chinese: 我喜欢从我家窗户看的景色。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan cóng wǒ jiā chuānghu kàn de jǐngsè.
examples.english: I like the view from my window.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 风景, but 风景 might feel a bit more poetic or grand.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sun makes the day (日) warm (暖), and it feels good (和).
vocabulary.etymology: 暖 (warm) + 和 (gentle, harmonious); the second character 和 is neutral tone 'huo' in this word.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhēn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: The weather is really warm today.

examples.pinyin: Hē bēi chá, shēntǐ jiù nuǎnhuo le.
examples.english: Drink a cup of tea, and your body will feel warm.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for weather, temperatures, or physical sensation. The 'huo' is neutral tone.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Already 'more' (更), then add some more (加).
vocabulary.etymology: 更 (more) + 加 (to add); literally 'to add more'.

examples.pinyin: Xià yǔ le, lù shàng gèngjiā dǔchē.
examples.english: It's raining, so the traffic is even worse.

examples.chinese: 他说完后，我更加糊涂了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuō wán hòu, wǒ gèngjiā hútu le.
examples.english: After he spoke, I became even more confused.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to emphasize an increase in degree, often before adjectives or verbs.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '层' (layer) of time you've gone through (经).
vocabulary.etymology: 曾 (once, ever) + 经 (to pass through); meaning 'has passed through (a time)'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ céngjīng zhù zài Shànghǎi sān nián.
examples.english: I once lived in Shanghai for three years.

examples.pinyin: Tā céngjīng shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
examples.english: He used to be my good friend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Indicates a past experience or state that is no longer true. Often used with 过 (guo).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Having (有) a sharp blade (利) gives you an advantage.
vocabulary.etymology: 有 (to have) + 利 (sharp, benefit); literally 'to have benefit'.

examples.pinyin: Zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ duì jiànkāng yǒulì.
examples.english: Going to bed and waking up early is beneficial for health.

examples.chinese: 这个位置对我们很有利。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèizhi duì wǒmen hěn yǒulì.
examples.english: This position is very advantageous for us.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often followed by 于 (yú) or 对... (duì...), meaning 'beneficial to...'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Having (有) an effect (效) that works.
vocabulary.etymology: 有 (to have) + 效 (effect, result); literally 'to have effect'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège fāngfǎ hěn yǒuxiào.
examples.english: This method is very effective.

examples.chinese: 药的有效期是到明年三月。
examples.pinyin: Yào de yǒuxiào qī shì dào míngnián sān yuè.
examples.english: The medicine's expiry date is until next March.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things (methods, medicine, policies) that produce the desired result.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You have (有) it, and there is (的是) more!
vocabulary.etymology: 有 (to have) + 的是 (a colloquial structure indicating abundance).

examples.pinyin: Bié zháojí, shíjiān yǒudeshì.
examples.english: Don't worry, there's plenty of time.

examples.pinyin: Tā jiā lǐ qián yǒudeshì.
examples.english: His family has plenty of money.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very casual, confident way to say 'there's no shortage of...'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Serves (服务) people as a member (员).
vocabulary.etymology: 服务 (to serve) + 员 (personnel); a person who serves.

examples.pinyin: Fúwùyuán, qǐng ná yīxià càidān.
examples.english: Waiter, please bring the menu.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài kāfēiguǎn dāng fúwùyuán.
examples.english: She works as a waitress in a cafe.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in restaurants, hotels, etc. A polite way to call for service.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Clothes (服) you put on and decorate (装) yourself with.
vocabulary.etymology: 服 (clothes) + 装 (to dress, attire); refers to attire as a whole.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de fúzhuāng hěn shíshàng.
examples.english: The clothing in this store is very fashionable.

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yánjiū chuántǒng fúzhuāng.
examples.english: He likes to study traditional clothing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than 衣服 (yīfu); often refers to clothing as a category or industry.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sun (朝) rises toward the east.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted the sun (日) amid grass (艹) and a moon (月), indicating morning. Extended to mean 'facing'.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng cháo qián zǒu.
examples.english: Please walk forward.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fángjiān chuānghu cháo nán.
examples.english: My room's window faces south.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a preposition, it indicates direction. Also a verb meaning 'to face'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A certain (其) period of time under the moon (月).
vocabulary.etymology: 其 (that, certain) + 月 (moon, month); originally meaning 'a period of time', often a month.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià ge xīngqī jiànmiàn ba.
examples.english: Let's meet next week.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zuìxīn yī qī de zázhì.
examples.english: This is the latest issue of the magazine.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile noun for periods of time or numbered issues of publications.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A tree (木) that feels like a head (头) - hard and solid.
vocabulary.etymology: 木 (tree, wood) + 头 (head, suffix indicating a thing); literally 'wood stuff'.

examples.chinese: 他用木头做了一张桌子。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng mùtou zuò le yī zhāng zhuōzi.
examples.english: He used wood to make a table.

examples.pinyin: Bié xiàng ge mùtou yīyàng zhàn zhe!
examples.english: Don't stand there like a block of wood! (i.e., stiffly)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the material. Can be used metaphorically to describe someone dull or unresponsive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your root/base (本) skill for doing things (事).
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (root, origin) + 事 (matter, affair); one's foundational capability to handle affairs.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiū diànnǎo hěn yǒu běnshì.
examples.english: He's very skilled at fixing computers.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme běnshì?
examples.english: What skills do you have?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial word for practical skills or capability. Often used with 有/没有 (yǒu/méiyǒu).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The root/base (本) from which things come (来).
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (root, original) + 来 (to come); meaning 'coming from the origin'.

examples.chinese: 我本来想去，但是下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù, dànshì xià yǔ le.
examples.english: I originally wanted to go, but it rained.

examples.pinyin: Tā běnlái jiù shì ge hǎo rén.
examples.english: He is a good person, of course.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can state the original situation, or add emphasis meaning 'it goes without saying'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your root/base (本) leadership (领) in a skill.
vocabulary.etymology: 本 (root) + 领 (collar, to lead); one's fundamental leading ability.

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu zhēn běnlǐng, bú shì chuīniú.
examples.english: He has real skills, he's not boasting.

examples.chinese: 学一门外语是很有用的本领。
examples.pinyin: Xué yī mén wàiyǔ shì hěn yǒuyòng de běnlǐng.
examples.english: Learning a foreign language is a very useful skill.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to 本事 but can sound slightly more formal or impressive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A wooden (木) device with many mouths/orifices (几, 口 in 器) that works.
vocabulary.etymology: 机 (mechanism, loom) + 器 (utensil, vessel); an assembled utensil with moving parts.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tái kāfēi jīqì huài le.
examples.english: This coffee machine is broken.

examples.chinese: 别把自己变成工作机器。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ zìjǐ biàn chéng gōngzuò jīqì.
examples.english: Don't turn yourself into a work machine.

vocabulary.usage_notes: General term for any machine from small appliances to large industrial equipment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Mixed (杂) records (志) of information bound together.
vocabulary.etymology: 杂 (mixed, miscellaneous) + 志 (records, annals); a publication recording miscellaneous topics.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài kàn yī běn shíshàng zázhì.
examples.english: I'm reading a fashion magazine.

examples.chinese: 医生办公室有很多杂志。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng bàngōngshì yǒu hěnduō zázhì.
examples.english: There are many magazines in the doctor's office.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The common word for periodical magazines.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Trees (木) and more trees, that's the countryside.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a settlement among trees or vegetation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye zhù zài cūn lǐ.
examples.english: My grandfather lives in the village.

examples.pinyin: Zhège cūn hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: This village is very beautiful.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The basic word for a village. Often used in 农村 (nóngcūn, countryside).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A tree (木) with a rope (口) around it, tying it up.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts tying something with a rope around a bundle.

examples.pinyin: Tā sòng le wǒ yī shù huā.
examples.english: He gave me a bunch of flowers.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa shù qǐlái le.
examples.english: She tied her hair up.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, 'to tie up'; as a measure word, for things in a bunch (flowers, light rays).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A tree (木) that's been reversed/processed (反) into a flat piece.
vocabulary.etymology: 木 (wood) + 反 (reverse); the origin is complex, but relates to a flat piece of wood.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xiě zài hēibǎn shàng.
examples.english: The teacher writes on the blackboard.

examples.chinese: 我需要一块木板做架子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yī kuài mùbǎn zuò jiàzi.
examples.english: I need a plank of wood to make a shelf.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A flat, stiff piece of material. Found in many compound words like 黑板 (hēibǎn, blackboard).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Reaching the pole/ultimate (极) point, and that's it (了)!
vocabulary.etymology: 极 (extreme, pole) + 了 (particle indicating change/completion); 'to have reached the extreme'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hǎokàn jíle!
examples.english: This movie is extremely good!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān lèi jíle.
examples.english: I'm extremely tired today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Adds strong emphasis. Place it directly after an adjective. Very common in spoken Chinese.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The fruit (果) of expectation ripens naturally (然).
vocabulary.etymology: 果 (fruit, result) + 然 (suffix meaning '-ly' or 'so'); 'the result being so'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shuō huì xià yǔ, guǒrán xià le.
examples.english: I said it would rain, and sure enough it did.

examples.pinyin: Tā guǒrán shì ge gāoshǒu.
examples.english: He really is an expert, as expected.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used when reality matches a previous prediction or expectation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A wooden (木) structure where you add (加) things.
vocabulary.etymology: 加 (to add) + 木 (wood); a wooden structure to add things onto.

examples.pinyin: Shūjià shàng yǒu hěnduō shū.
examples.english: There are many books on the bookshelf.

examples.pinyin: Tiān shàng yǒu yī jià fēijī.
examples.english: There's an airplane in the sky.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun: a frame or rack. As a measure word: primarily for airplanes, also for items like pianos or radios.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 票 (ticket) + 价 (price) = literally 'ticket price'.
vocabulary.etymology: 价, a simplified form of 價, means price or value.

examples.chinese: 这场演唱会的票价太贵了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǎn chàng huì de piào jià tài guì le.
examples.english: The ticket price for this concert is too expensive.

examples.chinese: 学生买票可以享受优惠票价。
examples.pinyin: Xué sheng mǎi piào kě yǐ xiǎng shòu yōu huì piào jià.
examples.english: Students can enjoy discounted ticket prices.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 很常用，直接说'票价'就行。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 过年时门上贴的'福'字倒过来，意思是'福到了'。
vocabulary.etymology: 甲骨文像双手捧着酒坛献祭，祈求神灵赐福。

examples.chinese: 祝你新年快乐，福气满满！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ xīn nián kuài lè, fú qì mǎn mǎn!
examples.english: Wish you a happy new year, full of good fortune!

examples.pinyin: Tā zhēn shì gè yǒu fú de rén.
examples.english: He is really a blessed person.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与'气'合用为'福气'，指好运。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 离 (to leave) + 婚 (marriage) = to leave a marriage.
vocabulary.etymology: 离，本义为黄鹂鸟，假借为'分离'。

examples.pinyin: Tā men liǎ qù nián lí hūn le.
examples.english: They got divorced last year.

examples.pinyin: Lí hūn shǒu xù bàn wán le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished the divorce procedures?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 可以说'他们离婚了'或'他们是离婚的'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '禾' (grain) + '火' (fire, color of leaves) = 谷物成熟、叶子变红的季节。
vocabulary.etymology: 甲骨文像蟋蟀或蝗虫形，秋天是虫鸣的季节，后加'禾'表谷物成熟。

examples.pinyin: Běi jīng de qiū tiān tè bié piào liang.
examples.english: Autumn in Beijing is especially beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐ huān de jì jié shì qiū.
examples.english: My favorite season is autumn.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语常说'秋天'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 这个'种'(zhǒng)是种子和种类的意思。
vocabulary.etymology: 种是種的简化字。種，从禾童声，本义为先种后熟的谷物，引申为种类。

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐ huān nǎ yī zhǒng yán sè?
examples.english: Which kind/type of color do you like?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī zhǒng xīn de shuǐ guǒ.
examples.english: This is a new kind of fruit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作量词时很常用，如'一种感觉'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 种(zhǒng, kind/seed) + 子(suffix) = 种子。就像植物的小宝宝。
vocabulary.etymology: 子，本义为婴儿，用作名词后缀。

examples.chinese: 我把苹果种子种在土里了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ píng guǒ zhǒng zi zhòng zài tǔ lǐ le.
examples.english: I planted the apple seed in the soil.

examples.chinese: 这些种子很快就会发芽。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiē zhǒng zi hěn kuài jiù huì fā yá.
examples.english: These seeds will sprout soon.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 注意'种'在这里读第三声zhǒng。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 科 (science) + 技 (skill) = 科学技术。
vocabulary.etymology: 科，从禾从斗，本义为品类、等级，引申为学科；技，从手支声，本义为技艺。

examples.chinese: 现在的科技发展太快了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài de kē jì fā zhǎn tài kuài le.
examples.english: Technology is developing too fast these days.

examples.chinese: 他对科技产品特别感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì kē jì chǎn pǐn tè bié gǎn xìng qù.
examples.english: He is very interested in tech products.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 泛指科学技术，口语常说'高科技'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 积极的人总是'积极举手'回答问题。
vocabulary.etymology: 积，从禾责声，本义为聚谷，引申为积累；极，本义为屋脊之栋，引申为顶点、最高。积极原指努力积累，力求达到最高。

examples.pinyin: Tā duì gōng zuò tài dù hěn jī jí.
examples.english: He has a very positive/proactive attitude towards work.

examples.chinese: 要积极面对生活中的困难。
examples.pinyin: Yào jī jí miàn duì shēng huó zhōng de kùn nán.
examples.english: You should face difficulties in life proactively.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 与'消极'相对。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 积极 (positive) + 性 (-ness) = 积极性。有干劲儿的状态。
vocabulary.etymology: 性，从心生声，本义为人的本性，引申为性质、状态等。

examples.chinese: 老板表扬了我们的工作积极性。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo bǎn biǎo yáng le wǒ men de gōng zuò jī jí xìng.
examples.english: The boss praised our work initiative.

examples.chinese: 这个游戏提高了孩子们的学习积极性。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè yóu xì tí gāo le hái zi men de xué xí jī jí xìng.
examples.english: This game increased the children's enthusiasm for learning.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与'提高'、'调动'等动词搭配。

vocabulary.english: to be called / to be known as
vocabulary.mnemonic: 称 (to call) + 为 (as) = 被称为...
vocabulary.etymology: 称，本义为测定重量，引申为称呼；为，本义是做，引申为当作、作为。

examples.chinese: 这种水果被称为'水果之王'。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐ guǒ bèi chēng wéi 'shuǐ guǒ zhī wáng'.
examples.english: This fruit is known as the 'king of fruits'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men tōng cháng chēng tā wéi Lǎo Wáng.
examples.english: We usually call him Lao Wang.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 较正式，口语中也用'叫'或'叫做'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '穴' (hole/cave) 里面'工' (work) 作完了，就空了。读kōng。
vocabulary.etymology: 从穴工声，本义为孔穴，引申为空虚、天空。

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè píng zi shì kōng de.
examples.english: This bottle is empty.

examples.pinyin: Niǎo er zài tiān kōng zhōng fēi xiáng.
examples.english: Birds are flying in the sky.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 注意与第四声kòng（空儿）的区别。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 把时间(kòng)出来的一小'空儿'。
vocabulary.etymology: 空，空闲义。儿，儿化音后缀，表细小、亲切。

examples.chinese: 你什么时候有空儿？我们喝杯咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shén me shí hòu yǒu kòng r? Wǒ men hē bēi kā fēi.
examples.english: When do you have free time? Let's have a coffee.

examples.chinese: 我这周一点空儿都没有。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhè zhōu yī diǎn kòng r dōu méi yǒu.
examples.english: I don't have any free time at all this week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语词，常说'有空儿'或'没空儿'。注意读kòng r。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 空 (air) + 调 (to adjust) = 调节空气的机器。
vocabulary.etymology: 调，从言周声，本义为和谐、协调，引申为调节。

examples.chinese: 夏天太热了，我们必须开空调。
examples.pinyin: Xià tiān tài rè le, wǒ men bì xū kāi kōng tiáo.
