examples.english: It's too hot in summer, we have to turn on the air conditioner.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè fáng jiān de kōng tiáo huài le.
examples.english: The air conditioner in this room is broken.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语中也简称'空调'，动词用'开/关空调'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 突 (sudden/protrude) + 出 (out) = 突然冒出来，很显眼 → 突出。
vocabulary.etymology: 突，从穴从犬，本义为犬从穴中突然冲出；出，象草木生出之形。突出本义为冲出，引申为凸出、显著。

examples.chinese: 他在比赛中表现非常突出。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐ sài zhōng biǎo xiàn fēi cháng tū chū.
examples.english: He performed outstandingly in the competition.

examples.pinyin: Bào gào yào tū chū zhǔ yào wèn tí.
examples.english: The report should highlight the main issues.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作形容词时，可以说'很突出'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '立'刻就去做！站着(立)就开始雕刻(刻)，不耽误。
vocabulary.etymology: 立，象人站立之形；刻，从刀亥声，本义为雕刻，引申为计时单位（一刻钟），表短时间。

examples.chinese: 收到消息后，他立刻出发了。
examples.pinyin: Shōu dào xiāo xī hòu, tā lì kè chū fā le.
examples.english: After receiving the message, he set off immediately.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng lì kè bǎ wén jiàn fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please send me the document immediately.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 和'马上'意思相近，'立刻'感觉更急一些。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 等 (wait) + 待 (stay) = 等着待着。
vocabulary.etymology: 等，从竹寺声，本义为整齐竹简，引申为等级、等待；待，从彳寺声，本义为等候。

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài kā fēi diàn děng dài péng you.
examples.english: I'm waiting for my friend at the coffee shop.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men děng dài hǎo xiāo xī.
examples.english: We are waiting for good news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 比单独的'等'稍正式一点，但口语也常用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 用来表达'简直不敢相信！'的夸张语气。
vocabulary.etymology: 简，从竹间声，本义为竹简，引申为简单；直，象目测直线之形，本义为不弯曲。简直原指简朴而刚直，后虚化为副词表强调。

examples.chinese: 这个蛋糕简直太好吃了！
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè dàn gāo jiǎn zhí tài hǎo chī le!
examples.english: This cake is simply delicious!

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō huà jiǎn zhí xiàng gè hái zi.
examples.english: He talks just like a child.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用于加强语气，表示程度很高或出人意料。

vocabulary.english: to manage / to be in charge of / to care (about)
vocabulary.mnemonic: '管理员'管着大家。口语中'我不管了'表示不想负责或干涉。
vocabulary.etymology: 筦是管的异体字。管，从竹官声，本义为竹制乐器，假借为管理、管辖。

examples.chinese: 他管这个项目的技术部分。
examples.pinyin: Tā guǎn zhè gè xiàng mù de jì shù bù fèn.
examples.english: He is in charge of the technical part of this project.

examples.chinese: 别管我，我想一个人静静。
examples.pinyin: Bié guǎn wǒ, wǒ xiǎng yī gè rén jìng jìng.
examples.english: Don't bother about me, I want to be alone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 多义常用词。'管不了'意思是管不住或没能力管。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 管 (to manage) + 理 (to organize) = 管理。
vocabulary.etymology: 理，从玉里声，本义为治玉，引申为整理、道理。

examples.chinese: 她管理着一家很大的公司。
examples.pinyin: Tā guǎn lǐ zhe yī jiā hěn dà de gōng sī.
examples.english: She manages a very large company.

examples.pinyin: Xué xiào de guǎn lǐ fēi cháng yán gé.
examples.english: The school's management is very strict.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 适用范围很广，从企业管理到自我管理。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '大米'是一种'类'别的粮食。
vocabulary.etymology: 類，从犬頪声，本义为种类相似的大，引申为种类、类似。

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐ huān zhè lèi de diàn yǐng.
examples.english: I like this type/category of movie.

examples.pinyin: Dòng wù kě yǐ fēn wéi hěn duō lèi.
examples.english: Animals can be divided into many categories.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常作量词用，如'一类人'、'两类问题'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 类 (kind) + 似 (to resemble) = 同一种类，很相似。
vocabulary.etymology: 似，从人以声，本义为相像。

examples.chinese: 这两个手机的功能很类似。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè shǒu jī de gōng néng hěn lèi sì.
examples.english: The functions of these two phones are very similar.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yù dào guò lèi sì de qíng kuàng.
examples.english: I've encountered a similar situation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 可以说'A和B类似'或'A类似于B'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 精 (essence) + 彩 (color) = 精华和色彩都到位，很精彩。
vocabulary.etymology: 精，从米青声，本义为上等细米，引申为精华；彩，从彡采声，本义为文采、色彩。

examples.chinese: 昨晚的演出真是太精彩了！
examples.pinyin: Zuó wǎn de yǎn chū zhēn shì tài jīng cǎi le!
examples.english: Last night's performance was absolutely brilliant!

examples.chinese: 这部电影有很精彩的打斗场面。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng yǒu hěn jīng cǎi de dǎ dòu chǎng miàn.
examples.english: This movie has some very exciting fight scenes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用于赞美表演、比赛、演讲等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: 精 (essence) + 神 (deity/spirit) = 精神和神灵有关，也指人的活力。读jīngshén。
vocabulary.etymology: 神，从示申声，本义为神灵，引申为精神、神采。

examples.chinese: 他今天看起来精神很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīn tiān kàn qǐ lái jīng shén hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He looks very energetic/lively today.

examples.chinese: 我们要学习他的奉献精神。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yào xué xí tā de fèng xiàn jīng shén.
examples.english: We should learn from his spirit of dedication.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作形容词(读jīng shen)时，常指人有活力；作名词指抽象的精神世界。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '唐'代人就喜欢吃的甜'米'（糖的部首是米）东西。
vocabulary.etymology: 糖，从米唐声，本义为饴糖，用米麦等制成。

examples.pinyin: Kā fēi lǐ xū yào jiā táng ma?
examples.english: Do you need to add sugar to your coffee?

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo hái zi dōu xǐ huān chī táng.
examples.english: Children all like to eat candy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 泛指糖和糖果。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Hot (热) love (爱), like your feelings are on fire.
vocabulary.etymology: 热 (rè) means 'hot' or 'warm,' and 爱 (ài) means 'love.' Together they mean 'to love fervently.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tài rè ài wǒ de gōngzuò le!
examples.english: I am so passionate about my job!

examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù rè ài lánqiú.
examples.english: He has loved basketball since he was a kid.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger and more formal than just 喜欢. Often used for abstract concepts like careers, hobbies, or countries.

vocabulary.english: to shine; to take a photo; according to
vocabulary.mnemonic: It's like saying 'photo' or 'shine a light on this, please.'
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person holding a torch, representing illumination. Later extended to mean 'reflection' and 'photo.'

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng zhào de wǒ zhēng bù kāi yǎn.
examples.english: The sun is shining so bright I can't open my eyes.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiù zhào wǒ shuō de zuò.
examples.english: Just do it as I said.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile word. Can be a verb (shine/take photo) or preposition (according to).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A machine (机) that takes a photo (照相).
vocabulary.etymology: Compound word: 照 (zhào, to shine/reflect) + 相 (xiàng, appearance/image) + 机 (jī, machine). Literally 'image-shining machine.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhàoxiàngjī méi diàn le.
examples.english: My camera is out of battery.

examples.chinese: 现在大家都用手机，很少带照相机了。
examples.pinyin: Xiànzài dàjiā dōu yòng shǒujī, hěn shǎo dài zhàoxiàngjī le.
examples.english: Now everyone uses their phones, and rarely carries a camera.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In casual speech, 相机 is more common than the full 照相机.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A bear (熊) that's a cat (猫), but it's not a cat at all.
vocabulary.etymology: 熊 (xióng) means 'bear.' 猫 (māo) means 'cat.' So, 'bear-cat,' named for its cat-like face.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的动物是熊猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān de dòngwù shì xióngmāo.
examples.english: My favorite animal is the panda.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kànguo zhēn de xióngmāo ma?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a real panda?

vocabulary.usage_notes: National treasure of China. 大熊猫 is the more formal/specific term for the giant panda.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (人) you know well/cooked (熟).
vocabulary.etymology: 熟 (shú) means 'ripe,' 'cooked,' or 'familiar.' 人 (rén) means 'person.' So a 'familiar person.'

examples.chinese: 我在街上遇到了一个熟人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài jiē shàng yù dào le yī gè shúrén.
examples.english: I ran into an acquaintance on the street.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ dōu shì shúrén, bié kèqi.
examples.english: We're all familiar faces here, make yourself at home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Not as close as a 朋友 (friend). It's someone you know, but maybe not intimately.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A heart (心) full of love (爱).
vocabulary.etymology: 爱 (ài) means 'love.' 心 (xīn) means 'heart.' Together they form a concept of 'loving heart' or 'compassion.'

examples.chinese: 她是一个很有爱心的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī gè hěn yǒu àixīn de rén.
examples.english: She is a very compassionate person.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ de àixīn juānkuǎn.
examples.english: Thank you for your charitable donation.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe a kind, charitable nature or actions done out of compassion.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The male (父) relative (亲). More formal than 爸爸.
vocabulary.etymology: 父 (fù) is a pictograph of a hand holding a tool, representing the male head of family. 亲 (qīn) means 'relative' or 'close.'

examples.pinyin: Tā de fùqīn shì yī wèi lǎoshī.
examples.english: His father is a teacher.

examples.pinyin: Fùqīn jié kuàilè!
examples.english: Happy Father's Day!

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and written than 爸爸. Used in official contexts or when showing respect.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Father (父) and mother (母) together.
vocabulary.etymology: 父 (fù) means 'father.' 母 (mǔ) is a pictograph of a woman with breasts, meaning 'mother.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de fùmǔ dōu zhù zài Běijīng.
examples.english: My parents both live in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ yào qù kànwàng fùmǔ.
examples.english: I'm going to visit my parents this weekend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common and slightly more formal than 爸妈. Can refer to parents as a unit.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A sign (牌) with a child (子) suffix — a little sign or name tag.
vocabulary.etymology: 牌 (pái) originally meant a wooden plaque or tablet. 子 (zi) is a noun suffix. Together it refers to a small plaque, sign, or brand label.

examples.chinese: 你这个包是什么牌子的？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè ge bāo shì shénme páizi de?
examples.english: What brand is your bag?

examples.chinese: 你看清楚那个店牌子了吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kàn qīngchu nà ge diàn páizi le ma?
examples.english: Did you see the store sign clearly?

vocabulary.usage_notes: In casual talk, 牌子 usually means 'brand.' 品牌 is more formal for 'brand.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: The animal is strong, so calling someone 牛 means they're 'strongly' awesome.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of the head of a cow with horns. Represents the animal, and by extension, traits like strength and stubbornness.

examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng lǐ yǒu hěn duō niú.
examples.english: There are many cows on the farm.

examples.pinyin: Tā pīngpāngqiú dǎ de zhēn niú!
examples.english: He's really awesome at playing table tennis!

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective (awesome/cool), it's very casual slang. The measure word for the animal is 头.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's the special (特) color (色) that makes something stand out.
vocabulary.etymology: 特 (tè) means 'special' or 'unique.' 色 (sè) means 'color' or 'appearance.' Together, 'special characteristic.'

examples.chinese: 这家餐厅的菜很有地方特色。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn yǒu dìfāng tèsè.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant has strong local characteristics.

examples.chinese: 你们学校最大的特色是什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen xuéxiào zuì dà de tèsè shì shénme?
examples.english: What's the biggest special feature of your school?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe unique aspects of places, cultures, or products.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The shape (状) and condition (况) of things — how things are.
vocabulary.etymology: 状 (zhuàng) means 'form' or 'shape.' 况 (kuàng) means 'condition' or 'circumstance.'

examples.chinese: 最近公司的状况不太好。
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn gōngsī de zhuàngkuàng bù tài hǎo.
examples.english: The company's situation hasn't been great lately.

examples.pinyin: Fāshēng shénme zhuàngkuàng le?
examples.english: What happened? / What's the situation?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to 情况. Often used for describing overall or specific conditions, sometimes negative.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The shape (状) and attitude (态) you're in right now.
vocabulary.etymology: 状 (zhuàng) means 'form' or 'shape.' 态 (tài) means 'attitude' or 'condition.'

examples.chinese: 我今天不在状态，老是犯错。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān bù zài zhuàngtài, lǎo shì fàn cuò.
examples.english: I'm not in good form today, I keep making mistakes.

examples.pinyin: Bǎ shǒujī tiáo chéng jìngyīn zhuàngtài.
examples.english: Set your phone to silent mode.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More about a personal or internal condition (mood, form, mode) compared to the external 状况.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of the character looking like a pig with its snout and ear.
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional character 豬 is a phono-semantic compound with 豕 (shǐ, pig) as the meaning component.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōngwǔ chī zhūròu.
examples.english: We're having pork for lunch.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié shuì le, kuài qǐchuáng, lǎn zhū!
examples.english: Stop sleeping, get up, you lazy pig!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used as a playful insult (like 'silly pig' or 'lazy pig') among friends.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something you play (玩) with as a tool (具).
vocabulary.etymology: 玩 (wán) means 'to play.' 具 (jù) means 'tool' or 'implement.' So, a 'plaything.'

examples.chinese: 我给弟弟买了一个新玩具。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi dìdi mǎi le yī gè xīn wánjù.
examples.english: I bought my younger brother a new toy.

examples.chinese: 他的房间全是乐高玩具。
examples.pinyin: Tā de fángjiān quán shì Lègāo wánjù.
examples.english: His room is full of Lego toys.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to toys for children or even adults (like collectibles).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It looks like a jade环! A circular piece of jade.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a round piece of jade with a hole (a bi disc). It signifies something circular or surrounding.

examples.chinese: 她戴了一个漂亮的耳环。
examples.pinyin: Tā dài le yī gè piàoliang de ěrhuán.
examples.english: She is wearing a beautiful earring.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lùxiàn huán hú yī zhōu.
examples.english: This route goes all the way around the lake.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds. As a standalone noun, it commonly means a physical ring or loop.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Protecting (保) the environment (环).
vocabulary.etymology: Abbreviation of 环境保护 (huánjìng bǎohù). 环 (huán) short for 环境 (environment). 保 (bǎo) means 'protect.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yǒu huánbǎo yìshí.
examples.english: We need to have environmental awareness.

examples.chinese: 这个袋子是环保材料做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dàizi shì huánbǎo cáiliào zuò de.
examples.english: This bag is made from eco-friendly materials.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common term. Can be a noun (the concept) or adjective (describing something as green/eco).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The condition (境) that surrounds (环) you.
vocabulary.etymology: 环 (huán) means 'to surround' or 'ring.' 境 (jìng) means 'border' or 'condition.' The area and conditions that surround something.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de zìrán huánjìng hěn měi.
examples.english: The natural environment here is very beautiful.

examples.chinese: 我需要一个安静的学习环境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào yī gè ānjìng de xuéxí huánjìng.
examples.english: I need a quiet study environment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical surroundings (nature) or abstract settings (work environment).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The present (现) era (代).
vocabulary.etymology: 现 (xiàn) means 'present' or 'appear.' 代 (dài) means 'era' or 'generation.' So, 'the present era.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān xiàndài yīnyuè.
examples.english: I like modern music.

examples.chinese: 现代人的生活节奏很快。
examples.pinyin: Xiàndài rén de shēnghuó jiézòu hěn kuài.
examples.english: The pace of life for modern people is very fast.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used as an adjective (modern) or noun (modern times). Often contrasts with 古代 (ancient).

vocabulary.mnemonic: To make (化) something modern (现代).
vocabulary.etymology: 现代 (xiàndài, modern) + 化 (huà, suffix meaning '-ization' or 'to make become').

examples.chinese: 中国的现代化发展很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó de xiàndàihuà fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
examples.english: China's modernization is developing very quickly.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng xūyào xiàndàihuà.
examples.english: This factory needs to be modernized.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 化 (huà) turns the noun 现代 into a process or action. Common in political and social contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The present (现) place/field (场).
vocabulary.etymology: 现 (xiàn) means 'present' or 'on the spot.' 场 (chǎng) means 'field' or 'site.'

examples.pinyin: Shìgù xiànchǎng yǒu hěn duō jǐngchá.
examples.english: There are many police at the accident scene.

examples.chinese: 我们去看现场音乐会吧！
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù kàn xiànchǎng yīnyuè huì ba!
examples.english: Let's go to a live concert!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean the physical location of an event (crime scene) or an event happening in real time (live show).

vocabulary.mnemonic: What appears (现) to be real (实).
vocabulary.etymology: 现 (xiàn) means 'to appear' or 'manifest.' 实 (shí) means 'solid,' 'true,' or 'real.'

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào miànduì xiànshí.
examples.english: You need to face reality.

examples.pinyin: Tā de xiǎngfǎ hěn bù xiànshí.
examples.english: His ideas are very unrealistic.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in contrast with 理想 (ideal). Can be a harsh word meaning 'the cold, hard truth.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: Present (现) money (金). Money you can see right now.
vocabulary.etymology: 现 (xiàn) means 'present' or 'on hand.' 金 (jīn) originally meant 'metal,' then 'money.' So, 'money on hand.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēnshang méi dài duōshao xiànjīn.
examples.english: I don't have much cash on me.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ kěyǐ yòng xiànjīn ma?
examples.english: Do you accept cash here?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to physical money (bills and coins). In China, digital支付 is very common, making 现金 less frequent.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A team (班) of levels (级) — your class year and group.
vocabulary.etymology: 班 (bān) originally meant 'to divide jade,' later 'team' or 'squad.' 级 (jí) means 'grade' or 'level.'

examples.chinese: 我们班级有三十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bānjí yǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
examples.english: There are thirty students in our class.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì nǎ ge bānjí de?
examples.english: Which class is he in?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the specific group of students in a school class, not the subject being taught (that's 课).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A fan (迷) of ball (球) games.
vocabulary.etymology: 球 (qiú) means 'ball' or 'sphere.' 迷 (mí) means 'fan,' 'enthusiast,' or 'to be crazy about.'

examples.chinese: 我爸爸是个铁杆足球球迷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba shì gè tiěgǎn zúqiú qiúmí.
examples.english: My dad is a die-hard soccer fan.

examples.chinese: 球迷们都在为球队加油。
examples.pinyin: Qiúmímen dōu zài wèi qiúduì jiāyóu.
examples.english: The fans are all cheering for the team.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically a fan of ball sports (soccer, basketball, etc.). For other types of fans, use 粉丝 or other words.

vocabulary.english: to get a haircut / hair salon
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine managing (理) your hair (发) at the barber's.
vocabulary.etymology: 理 (manage, arrange) + 髮/发 (hair). Together they mean 'arrange the hair'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào qù lǐfà.
examples.english: I need to get a haircut tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǐfà diàn hěn piányi.
examples.english: This barbershop is very cheap.

vocabulary.usage_notes: When used as a noun, it's often shortened from 理发店.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'path' (由) you give to 'manage' (理) an argument - your reason.
vocabulary.etymology: 理 (logic, principle) + 由 (cause, reason). Meaning 'a principled cause or reason'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme lǐyóu chídào?
examples.english: What's your reason for being late?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hǎo lǐyóu.
examples.english: This is a good reason.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in questions to ask for justification.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'untie' (解) the 'logic' (理) of something to understand it.
vocabulary.etymology: 理 (principle, logic) + 解 (to untie, to explain). Together they mean 'to untie the logic', i.e., to comprehend.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wánquán lǐjiě nǐ de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: I completely understand your thinking.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ lǐjiě wǒ.
examples.english: Thank you for understanding me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can express deeper, empathetic understanding.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Systematic 'discussion' (论) of 'principles' (理) = theory.
vocabulary.etymology: 理 (principle) + 論/论 (to discuss, discourse). Refers to 'discourse on principles'.

examples.chinese: 这只是个理论，还没被证明。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ shì gè lǐlùn, hái méi bèi zhèngmíng.
examples.english: This is just a theory; it hasn't been proven yet.

examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yánjiū jīngjì lǐlùn.
examples.english: He likes to study economic theory.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 实践 (practice).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Give 'birth' (产) to something 'new' (生) - to produce it.
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (to give birth, to grow) + 產/产 (to produce). Original meaning linked to childbirth, extended to general production.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng shēngchǎn qìchē.
examples.english: This factory manufactures cars.

examples.pinyin: Tā xià zhōu yào shēngchǎn le.
examples.english: She's going to give birth next week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean both industrial production and childbirth.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A description that feels 'alive' (生) and 'moving' (动).
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (life, living) + 動/动 (to move). Something that is 'living and moving', hence vivid.

examples.pinyin: Tā de gùshi jiǎng de hěn shēngdòng.
examples.english: He tells his story very vividly.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì fú shēngdòng de huà.
examples.english: This is a vivid painting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe stories, descriptions, art, or performances.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your 'life' (命) and everything that 'lives' (生).
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (to live, life) + 命 (life, fate). Refers to the state of being alive.

examples.pinyin: Shēngmìng shì zuì bǎoguì de.
examples.english: Life is the most precious thing.

examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiù le tā de shēngmìng.
examples.english: The doctor saved his life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to life itself, more formal/philosophical than 生活 (lifestyle).

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'exist' (存) and stay 'alive' (生).
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (to live) + 存 (to exist, to preserve). Means 'to live and exist'.

examples.pinyin: Zài shāmò lǐ hěn nán shēngcún.
examples.english: It's very hard to survive in the desert.

examples.pinyin: Shēngcún háishì huǐmiè?
examples.english: To be or not to be? (To survive or be destroyed?)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the basic struggle to stay alive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Creating 'life' (生) from 'ideas/intent' (意) - that's business.
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (to generate) + 意 (idea, intention). The generation of ideas/profit through commerce.

examples.pinyin: Tā bàba shì zuò shēngyì de.
examples.english: His dad is in business.

examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn shēngyì zěnmeyàng?
examples.english: How's business lately?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to commerce/trade, not academic 'meaning' (that's 意思).

vocabulary.mnemonic: From 'birth' (生) to getting 'longer/taller' (长).
vocabulary.etymology: 生 (to be born) + 長/长 (to grow). The process of growing after birth.

examples.chinese: 这种植物在北方生长不了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù zài běifāng shēngzhǎng bù liǎo.
examples.english: This kind of plant can't grow in the north.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shēngzhǎng zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: I grew up in Shanghai.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for biological growth of living things.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as an arrow pointing to the 'source' or 'doer'.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a hand guiding a sprout out of the ground, indicating 'origin' or 'cause'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège juédìng yóu nǐ lái zuò.
examples.english: This decision is to be made by you.

examples.pinyin: Huìyì yóu jīnglǐ zhǔchí.
examples.english: The meeting is chaired by the manager.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A key preposition indicating the agent or cause in passive-like structures.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 'because of' the 'reason' (由) and 'at' (于) its root.
vocabulary.etymology: 由 (cause, reason) + 於/于 (at, in). Meaning 'at the cause of'.

examples.pinyin: Yóuyú xià yǔ, bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.english: Due to the rain, the match was canceled.

examples.chinese: 由于你的帮助，我才成功了。
examples.pinyin: Yóuyú nǐ de bāngzhù, wǒ cái chénggōng le.
examples.english: Because of your help, I succeeded.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Starts a cause clause, often followed by a result. More formal than 因为 in writing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'station/stand' (台) for 'electric' (电) broadcasts.
vocabulary.etymology: 電/电 (electricity) + 臺/台 (platform, station). An electric broadcasting platform.

examples.chinese: 我喜欢听这个音乐电台。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan tīng zhège yīnyuè diàntái.
examples.english: I like listening to this music radio station.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài diàntái gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works at a radio station.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The platform/broadcaster itself, not the physical radio (收音机).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Tiny electric (电) particles/children (子).
vocabulary.etymology: 電/电 (electricity) + 子 (child, small thing). A term for 'electron' and by extension, anything electronic.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zuì xīn de diànzǐ shèbèi.
examples.english: This is the latest electronic device.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn diànzǐ shū.
examples.english: I like to read e-books.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most often used as a modifier before other nouns (e.g., 电子邮件).

vocabulary.mnemonic: An 'electronic' (电子) piece of 'mail' (邮件).
vocabulary.etymology: 電子/电子 (electronic) + 郵件/邮件 (mail). A direct translation of 'electronic mail'.

measure_word.example: 一封电子邮件 (yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn)

examples.chinese: 我给你发了一封电子邮件。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ fā le yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn.
examples.english: I sent you an email.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng cháshōu nǐ de diànzǐ yóujiàn.
examples.english: Please check your email.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often shortened to 邮件 in casual conversation. 封 is the measure word for letters/mails.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'play/drama' (剧) on 'television' (电视).
vocabulary.etymology: 電視/电视 (television) + 劇/剧 (drama, play). A drama made for television.

examples.chinese: 我每天晚上都看电视剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān wǎnshang dōu kàn diànshìjù.
examples.english: I watch TV dramas every night.

examples.chinese: 最近有什么好看的电视剧？
examples.pinyin: Zuìjìn yǒu shénme hǎokàn de diànshìjù?
examples.english: Are there any good TV dramas lately?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to multi-episode shows, not single films (电影).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'broadcasting station' (台) for 'television' (电视).
vocabulary.etymology: 電視/电视 (television) + 臺/台 (platform, station). The broadcaster/platform for TV.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànshìtái dāng jìzhě.
examples.english: He works as a reporter at a TV station.

examples.chinese: 这是本地最大的电视台。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì běndì zuì dà de diànshìtái.
examples.english: This is the largest local TV station.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The organization, not the TV set (电视机).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'male' (男) 'person/child' (子).
vocabulary.etymology: 男 (man, male) + 子 (child, person). Originally 'son', now a general term for an adult male.

examples.chinese: 那个穿黑衣服的男子是谁？
examples.pinyin: Nàge chuān hēi yīfu de nánzǐ shì shéi?
examples.english: Who is that man wearing black clothes?

examples.chinese: 男子一百米比赛开始了。
examples.pinyin: Nánzǐ yì bǎi mǐ bǐsài kāishǐ le.
examples.english: The men's 100-meter race has started.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal or descriptive than 男人. Common in news/sports contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To 'stay/remain' (留) in another country to 'study' (学).
vocabulary.etymology: 留 (to stay, to remain) + 學/学 (to study). To stay in a foreign land for study.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie zài Měiguó liúxué.
examples.english: My older sister is studying abroad in the U.S.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎr liúxué?
examples.english: Where do you plan to study abroad?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The person who does this is 留学生.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Feels like a disease (疒) in a hole (甬) in your body.
vocabulary.etymology: 疒 (sickness radical) + 甬 (phonetic component). Originally depicted a painful disease.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu hěn tòng.
examples.english: My head hurts a lot.

examples.pinyin: Bié shuō le, nǐ ràng wǒ xīn tòng.
examples.english: Stop talking, you're breaking my heart.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 疼 for physical pain. Can be used for emotional pain (心痛).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A double dose of 'pain' (痛) and 'bitterness' (苦).
vocabulary.etymology: 痛 (pain) + 苦 (bitterness). Intense pain or distress.

examples.pinyin: Fēnshǒu hòu tā hěn tòngkǔ.
examples.english: He was in great pain after the breakup.

examples.chinese: 这是一种精神上的痛苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì zhǒng jīngshén shàng de tòngkǔ.
examples.english: This is a kind of mental suffering.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Stronger than just 痛, often describing deep emotional or physical suffering.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The common, 'white' (白) leafy 'vegetable' (菜).
vocabulary.etymology: 白 (white) + 菜 (vegetable). Refers to the light-colored variety of Chinese cabbage.

examples.chinese: 今天晚上我们炒白菜吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒmen chǎo báicài chī ba.
examples.english: Let's stir-fry some bok choy for dinner tonight.

examples.pinyin: Báicài duōshao qián yì jīn?
examples.english: How much is a jin of bok choy?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and inexpensive vegetable in Chinese cuisine.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a hand (又) scraping the 'skin' off a piece of meat (肉- simplified form).
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified form origin is unclear. Traditional form 皮 is a pictograph of a hand removing animal skin.

examples.pinyin: Chī píngguǒ yào xiāo pí.
examples.english: You need to peel the apple before eating it.

examples.pinyin: Zhège píbāo shì zhēnpí de.
examples.english: This leather bag is made of real leather.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile word for outer coverings of fruits, animals, and objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'bag' (包) made of 'leather/skin' (皮).
vocabulary.etymology: 皮 (leather, skin) + 包 (bag). A bag made from leather.

examples.pinyin: Tā de xīn píbāo hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: Her new leather handbag is very beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié bǎ píbāo diū le.
examples.english: Be careful, don't lose your handbag.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to women's handbags or briefcases, especially if made of leather.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Right in front of your 'eyes' (目) and 'in front' (前).
vocabulary.etymology: 目 (eye) + 前 (front). Meaning 'before the eyes', i.e., the present moment.

examples.pinyin: Mùqián wǒ hái zài zhǎo gōngzuò.
examples.english: I'm currently still looking for a job.

examples.pinyin: Mùqián de qíngkuàng jiù shì zhèyàng.
examples.english: The current situation is just like this.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used at the beginning of a sentence to state the present situation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Mǒu sounds like "mo" + "u", think 'mystery one, unspecified person'. It's vague on purpose.
vocabulary.etymology: From 甘 (sweet) and 木 (tree). The original meaning was 'plum' (now written 梅), but it was borrowed for its sound to mean 'a certain'.

examples.chinese: 我昨天在街上遇到某个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zài jiē shàng yù dào mǒu ge rén.
examples.english: I met a certain person on the street yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tīng mǒu shǒu gē le ma?
examples.english: Have you listened to a certain song?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used when you don't want to specify something precisely, or you don't know. Commonly followed by a measure word.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 标 (mark) + 准 (accurate) = the accurate mark you measure things against. Think of a ruler (📏).
vocabulary.etymology: 标 originally meant 'treetop', later 'sign, mark'. 准 means 'level, accurate'. Combined, they mean 'an accurate mark to measure by'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de fāyīn hěn biāozhǔn.
examples.english: Your pronunciation is very standard.

examples.chinese: 公司有严格的质量标准。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yǒu yángé de zhìliàng biāozhǔn.
examples.english: The company has strict quality standards.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be both a noun ('a standard') and an adjective ('it's standard').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 标 (mark) + 题 (topic) = the marked topic at the top. Like a name tag (🏷️) for an article.
vocabulary.etymology: 标 as in 'sign'. 题 means 'topic, theme', originally referring to the forehead. Combined, it means the 'headmark' or heading of a piece of writing.

examples.chinese: 这个视频的标题太吸引人了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shìpín de biāotí tài xīyǐn rén le.
examples.english: This video's title is so attractive.

examples.chinese: 文章的标题你写好了吗？
examples.pinyin: Wénzhāng de biāotí nǐ xiě hǎo le ma?
examples.english: Have you written the article's title?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically for the title of articles, videos, books, etc. Not usually for people's names.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 根 (root) + 本 (base) = the root and base of something. A tree (🌳) can't stand without it. As an adverb, it means 'from the root' -> 'not at all'.
vocabulary.etymology: 根 means 'root of a tree'. 本 means 'base, origin'. Together they emphasize the very foundation or essence of something.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèntí hěn gēnběn.
examples.english: This problem is very fundamental.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēnběn méi kàn nà bù diànyǐng.
examples.english: I didn't watch that movie at all.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adverb (used before a negative verb), it intensifies the negation meaning 'not at all'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks a bit like two towers holding up a road over water. Qiáo sounds like 'chow', imagine enjoying a meal on a bridge.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 橋. The phonetic component is 喬 (tall, high) and the semantic component is 木 (wood), originally meaning a wooden structure built high to cross over something.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen guò qiáo qù mǎi dōngxi ba.
examples.english: Let's cross the bridge to go shopping.

examples.pinyin: Nà zuò lǎo qiáo hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: That old bridge is very famous.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and straightforward noun for a physical bridge. The measure word 座 is most common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 概 (general) + 念 (thought) = a general thought in your mind. Like a lightbulb (💡) idea.
vocabulary.etymology: 概 originally meant 'leveling tool', extended to mean 'general'. 念 means 'to think, thought'. Together, it means a generalized thought or idea.

examples.chinese: 我大概明白这个概念了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dàgài míngbái zhè ge gàiniàn le.
examples.english: I roughly understand this concept now.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gàiniàn tài chōuxiàng le.
examples.english: This concept is too abstract.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for abstract ideas, especially in learning, philosophy, or science. Often paired with 明白 (understand) or 清楚 (clear).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 欢 (happy) + 乐 (happy) = double happiness! It's a party (🎉) word.
vocabulary.etymology: 欢 originally meant the joyful sound of birds, from 雚 (a type of bird) and 欠 (to lack, implying opening the mouth). 乐 means music/happiness.

examples.pinyin: Fángjiān lǐ chōngmǎn le huānlè.
examples.english: The room was filled with joy.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ xīnnián huānlè!
examples.english: Wishing you a joyful New Year!

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal and literary than 快乐 or 开心. Often used in songs, greetings, and descriptions of a happy atmosphere.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 歌 (song) + 声 (sound) = the sound of a song. Think of a microphone (🎤) picking up a voice.
vocabulary.etymology: 歌 is song. 声, derived from 聲, depicts a musical stone (磬) and an ear, meaning 'sound'. Literally, 'song-sound'.

examples.pinyin: Yuǎn chù chuán lái yí zhèn gēshēng.
examples.english: The sound of singing came from the distance.

examples.pinyin: Tā de gēshēng zhēn hǎotīng.
examples.english: Her singing voice is really pleasant.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the auditory quality of someone singing, not the song itself.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 歌 (song) + 手 (hand/person) = a song-person, someone whose 'hands' work is singing. A performer (👩🎤).
vocabulary.etymology: 手 here means 'person skilled in an activity' (like 水手 for sailor). A 歌手 is a person skilled in singing.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng zhíyè gēshǒu.
examples.english: She is a professional singer.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的歌手要来开演唱会了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de gēshǒu yào lái kāi yǎnchànghuì le.
examples.english: My favorite singer is coming to hold a concert.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word for any singer, from pop stars to folk singers.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 歌 (song) + 迷 (fan/enthusiast) = someone who is crazy about songs. The starry-eyed fan (🤩).
vocabulary.etymology: 迷 means 'to be fascinated by, to be lost in'. A 歌迷 is someone fascinated by or lost in songs/singing.

examples.chinese: 演唱会外面有很多歌迷。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnchànghuì wàimiàn yǒu hěn duō gēmí.
examples.english: There are many fans outside the concert.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì Zhōu Jiélún de gēmí.
examples.english: I'm a fan of Jay Chou.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically for fans of singers or bands. For movie/TV stars, use 影迷.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 正 (proper) + 式 (style) = proper style. Think of someone in a suit (🤵).
vocabulary.etymology: 正 means 'correct, proper'. 式 means 'pattern, style, form'. Together, they mean 'in correct form', i.e., formal or official.

examples.chinese: 今天下午有一个正式会议。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ yǒu yí gè zhèngshì huìyì.
examples.english: There is a formal meeting this afternoon.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hái méi zhèngshì rènshi ne.
examples.english: We haven't officially met yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can modify nouns (正式会议) or verbs (正式认识). Its opposite is 非正式.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like two feet walking apart. Bù sounds like 'boo' — you might say 'boo!' after one more step.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictograph of two feet walking. The top part (止) originally meant 'foot', and the bottom part depicts another foot stepping forward.

examples.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu shí bù jiù dào le.
examples.english: Walk ten steps forward and you'll be there.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yào yí bù yí bù lái.
examples.english: We need to take this matter one step at a time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a measure word, it's used for steps in a literal or metaphorical process. A very common word.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 武 (military) + 器 (tool) = a military tool. Think of crossed swords (⚔️).
vocabulary.etymology: 武 depicts a foot (止) and a halberd (戈), meaning military or martial. 器 means tool or utensil. A weapon is a martial tool.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng wǔqì fēicháng lìhai.
examples.english: This kind of weapon is very powerful.

examples.pinyin: Zhīshi shì zuì hǎo de wǔqì.
examples.english: Knowledge is the best weapon.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (gun, sword) or metaphorically (words, knowledge).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 武 (martial) + 术 (art/skill) = the martial art. Picture someone in a gi (🥋).
vocabulary.etymology: 武 as above. 术 (from 術) originally meant a path or method, later 'art, technique'. The art of combat.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xuéxí Zhōngguó wǔshù.
examples.english: He is learning Chinese martial arts.

examples.pinyin: Wǔshù kěyǐ qiángshēn jiàntǐ.
examples.english: Martial arts can strengthen the body.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The formal term for traditional Chinese martial arts like Kung Fu. 功夫 is more common in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a person kneeling beside bones. Sǐ sounds like 'see' — you don't want to see this. The skull (💀) says it all.
vocabulary.etymology: In oracle bone script, it depicted a person kneeling before bones or a skeleton, representing death.

examples.pinyin: Nà pén huā yǐjīng sǐ le.
examples.english: That potted plant has already died.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kuài lèi sǐ le.
examples.english: I'm exhausted to death (idiomatic exaggeration).

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very direct word. In informal speech, it's often used as an intensifier after adjectives (e.g., 累死了, 烦死了) meaning 'extremely'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 母 (female parent) + 亲 (close relative) = the close female parent. More formal than 妈妈.
vocabulary.etymology: 母 is a pictograph of a woman with prominent breasts, symbolizing motherhood. 亲 means 'kin, relative'. Together, it's the formal term for mother.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǔqīn shì yì míng jiàoshī.
examples.english: My mother is a teacher.

examples.chinese: 祝天下所有的母亲节日快乐！
examples.pinyin: Zhù tiānxià suǒyǒu de mǔqīn jiérì kuàilè!
examples.english: Happy Mother's Day to all the mothers in the world!

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard, slightly formal word for 'mother'. Use 妈妈 in most everyday conversations.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a person (亻) with a hat, maybe checking off each item on a list. Think of 'every' day on a calendar (📅).
vocabulary.etymology: The original form combined 屮 (sprout) and 母 (mother), suggesting 'to produce one after another', hence the meaning 'each'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zǎoshang dōu hē kāfēi.
examples.english: I drink coffee every morning.

examples.pinyin: Měi ge xuéshēng dōu yào xiě zuòyè.
examples.english: Every student must do homework.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Always followed by a measure word (e.g., 个, 天, 次) or words that don't need one (e.g., 人). Often paired with 都.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 比 (compare) + 例 (example/rate) = a comparative rate. Like a pie chart (📊) showing parts of a whole.
vocabulary.etymology: 比 means 'to compare'. 例 means 'example, precedent', but in this context, it implies 'rate' or 'standard'. The rate of comparison.

examples.pinyin: Nán nǚ bǐlì chàbuduō.
examples.english: The male-to-female ratio is about the same.

examples.pinyin: Àn bǐlì fēnpèi jiǎngjīn.
examples.english: Distribute the bonus according to proportion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in math, statistics, and general descriptions of how one part relates to a whole.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 比 (compare/compete) + 赛 (contest) = a contest to compare. Think of a trophy (🏆).
vocabulary.etymology: 比 as 'to compete'. 赛 means 'to compete, contest'. It's a compound emphasizing competition.

examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn yǒu lánqiú bǐsài.
examples.english: There's a basketball game tonight.

examples.chinese: 我们要和他们比赛唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hé tāmen bǐsài chànggē.
examples.english: We are going to compete with them in singing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word for any kind of match, race, or contest. Can be used as a verb: 比赛唱歌 (to compete in singing).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 毛 (hair/fur) + 病 (illness) = a 'hairy illness', a small, annoying problem. Like a glitch needing a tool (🛠️) to fix.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally referred to defects in horses' coats (毛). Extended to mean minor physical ailments or flaws in objects/character.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de chē yòu chū máobìng le.
examples.english: My car has a problem again.

examples.chinese: 他有个毛病，就是爱迟到。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu gè máobìng, jiù shì ài chídào.
examples.english: He has a flaw: he's always late.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very colloquial. Used for minor physical defects, bad habits, or small malfunctions. Not for serious illnesses (use 病).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 民 (people) + 族 (clan) = a clan of people. Think of a diverse family (👨👩👧👦).
vocabulary.etymology: 民 refers to the common people. 族 depicts an arrow under a banner, representing a military clan. Together, they mean a people sharing common culture/descent.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu 56 gè mínzú.
examples.english: China has 56 ethnic groups.

examples.chinese: 每个民族都有自己的节日。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè mínzú dōu yǒu zìjǐ de jiérì.
examples.english: Every ethnic group has its own festivals.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for ethnicities (汉族, 藏族) or in compounds like 中华民族 (Chinese nation).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 民 (people) + 间 (among/between) = among the people. Think of folk art or lanterns (🏮).
vocabulary.etymology: Literally 'among the people', referring to things that originate from, exist among, or are related to the common populace, not the government or elite.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè mínjiān chuánshuō.
examples.english: This is a folk legend.

examples.chinese: 民间有很多志愿者组织。
examples.pinyin: Mínjiān yǒu hěn duō zhìyuànzhě zǔzhī.
examples.english: There are many volunteer organizations in the private sector.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things from non-official, grassroots sources: 民间故事 (folktale), 民间艺术 (folk art), 民间组织 (NGO).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 气 (air/weather) + 候 (wait/season) = the weather you wait for over seasons. The long-term pattern of the Earth (🌍).
vocabulary.etymology: 气 refers to the air/atmosphere. 候 means 'to wait' or 'season' (as in 时候, time). Climate is the seasonal atmospheric conditions over time.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de qìhòu hěn shūfu.
examples.english: The climate here is very comfortable.

examples.pinyin: Qìhòu biànhuà shì gè dà wèntí.
examples.english: Climate change is a big problem.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the long-term average weather patterns of a region. For daily weather, use 天气.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 沙 (sand) + 发 (hair? No, it's a sound!) — it's a phonetic translation of 'sofa'. Think of a comfy couch (🛋️).
vocabulary.etymology: A phonetic loanword from English 'sofa'. 沙 (shā) approximates 'so', 发 (fā) approximates 'fa'.

examples.chinese: 我太累了，想躺在沙发上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tài lèi le, xiǎng tǎng zài shāfā shàng.
examples.english: I'm so tired, I want to lie down on the sofa.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge shāfā shì xīn de.
examples.english: This sofa is new.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common, direct loanword. 沙发 is more common than 长椅 for a living room couch.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 美(beautiful)+元(yuan)=美元, the beautiful dollar.
vocabulary.etymology: 美 (Měi, short for 美国/Měiguó, America) + 元 (yuán, a monetary unit). Literally "American currency unit."

measure_word.example: 一张美元 (yī zhāng měiyuán) - one (bill) US dollar

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yào yībǎi měiyuán.
examples.english: This piece of clothing costs one hundred US dollars.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ yòng měiyuán fù qián ma?
examples.english: Can I pay with US dollars?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to the US currency, not dollars of other countries.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 美好 = 美(beautiful) + 好(good). Something so good, it's beautiful.
vocabulary.etymology: 美 (měi, beautiful) + 好 (hǎo, good). The combination intensifies the positive meaning.

examples.chinese: 祝你有一个美好的周末！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yǒu yī gè měihǎo de zhōumò!
examples.english: Wishing you a wonderful weekend!

examples.pinyin: Nà shì yī duàn měihǎo de shíguāng.
examples.english: That was a wonderful period of time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe abstract things like memories, life, future, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 美(beautiful) + 术(art/skill) = the skill of making beautiful things.
vocabulary.etymology: 美 (měi, beauty) + 术 (shù, art, skill). Literally "the art of beauty."

measure_word.example: 一门美术课 (yī mén měishù kè) - a fine arts class

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi zài dàxué xué měishù.
examples.english: My younger brother is studying fine arts at university.

examples.chinese: 这个美术展览很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhège měishù zhǎnlǎn hěn yǒuyìsi.
examples.english: This fine arts exhibition is very interesting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often refers to visual arts like painting, sculpture, and drawing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 美(delicious) + 食(food) = delicious food, '美食'.
vocabulary.etymology: 美 (měi, here meaning "delicious, fine") + 食 (shí, food). Literally "fine food."

measure_word.example: 一种美食 (yī zhǒng měishí) - a type of delicacy

examples.chinese: 这个城市有很多当地美食。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu hěn duō dāngdì měishí.
examples.english: This city has a lot of local delicacies.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè měishíjiā.
examples.english: He is a gourmet/foodie.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Highlights food that is particularly delicious or well-prepared.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a '群' of sheep - they move together as one unit.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 君 (jūn, lord) over 羊 (yáng, sheep). A lord's sheep, implying a herd under control, thus a group.

examples.pinyin: Yī qún háizi zài gōngyuán lǐ wán.
examples.english: A group of children are playing in the park.

examples.chinese: 我们有一个微信工作群。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu yī gè Wēixìn gōngzuò qún.
examples.english: We have a WeChat work group.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common measure word for groups of people or animals. Also a noun meaning 'group' in social/media contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 老(old) + 太太(madam/lady) = an old lady.
vocabulary.etymology: 老 (lǎo, old) + 太太 (tàitai, madam, lady). A respectful yet familiar term.

measure_word.example: 一位老太太 (yī wèi lǎo tàitai) - an old lady

examples.chinese: 那位老太太每天早晨都来散步。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎo tàitai měitiān zǎochen dōu lái sànbù.
examples.english: That old lady comes for a walk every morning.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bāng lǎo tàitai ná dōngxi.
examples.english: I helped the old lady carry her things.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A polite and common way to refer to an elderly woman. Can be used directly as a form of address.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 老(old) + 头儿(head/guy) = old guy, '老头儿'.
vocabulary.etymology: 老 (lǎo, old) + 头儿 (tóur, a colloquial suffix for a person, similar to '-er' or 'guy').

measure_word.example: 一个老头儿 (yī gè lǎo tóur) - an old man

examples.chinese: 公园里的老头儿在下棋。
examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ de lǎo tóur zài xià qí.
examples.english: The old men in the park are playing chess.

examples.pinyin: Nà lǎo tóur rén tǐng hǎo de.
examples.english: That old fellow is a pretty nice guy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquial and slightly affectionate. Slightly less formal than '老人'. Northern dialect feature with '儿'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 老(old/experienced) + 板(board/plank) = the experienced one holding the board (of the company).
vocabulary.etymology: 老 (lǎo, old, experienced) + 板 (bǎn, board). Originally referred to the owner or manager of a shop (the one behind the counter/board).

measure_word.example: 一位老板 (yī wèi lǎobǎn) - a boss

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen lǎobǎn jīntiān qǐngjià le.
examples.english: Our boss took the day off today.

examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn, zhège duōshǎo qián?
examples.english: Boss/Shopkeeper, how much is this?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to address the boss or the owner of a small business/shop.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 老(old) + 百(hundred) + 姓(surname) = the hundred old surnames, meaning the masses.
vocabulary.etymology: 老 (lǎo, old) + 百 (bǎi, hundred) + 姓 (xìng, surname). Historically refers to the "hundred surnames," a collective term for the common populace.

measure_word.example: 一个老百姓 (yī gè lǎo bǎixìng) - a common person

examples.chinese: 物价上涨影响了老百姓的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wùjià shàngzhǎng yǐngxiǎng le lǎo bǎixìng de shēnghuó.
examples.english: Rising prices affect the lives of ordinary people.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiù shì gè pǔtōng lǎo bǎixìng.
examples.english: I'm just an ordinary person.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Neutral term for the general public, contrasting with officials or elite.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 考(test) + 验(verify) = a double test, a real 'trial by fire'.
vocabulary.etymology: 考 (kǎo, to test, examine) + 验 (yàn, to verify, examine). A compound meaning a severe test or trial.

measure_word.example: 一次考验 (yī cì kǎoyàn) - one trial/test

examples.chinese: 这次旅行对我们是个大考验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng duì wǒmen shì gè dà kǎoyàn.
examples.english: This trip is a big test for us.

examples.pinyin: Shíjiān huì kǎoyàn yīqiè.
examples.english: Time will test everything.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often implies a challenging test of character, ability, or endurance.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 者 looks like a person 老 with a hat. It marks the 'doer'.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph possibly representing a person speaking or a fire (a debated origin). Evolved to mean "one who..." or a nominalizing particle.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yī gè dúzhě.
examples.english: He is a reader.

examples.pinyin: Zuòzhě xiě wán le zhè běn shū.
examples.english: The author finished writing this book.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common suffix attached to verbs or nouns to mean 'the person who does/does X'. Not used alone.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 职(position/duty) + 业(business) = your duty/business, i.e., your job.
vocabulary.etymology: 职 (zhí, duty, post) + 业 (yè, business, trade). The duty or trade one is engaged in.

measure_word.example: 一种职业 (yī zhǒng zhíyè) - a type of profession

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhíyè shì shénme?
examples.english: What is your profession?

examples.chinese: 教师是个受人尊敬的职业。
examples.pinyin: Jiàoshī shì gè shòu rén zūnjìng de zhíyè.
examples.english: Teaching is a respected profession.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than '工作'. Implies a career with specific skills.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 职(job) + 工(worker) = job worker, i.e., an employee.
vocabulary.etymology: 职 (zhí, post, duty) + 工 (gōng, worker). A worker holding a specific post.

measure_word.example: 一名职工 (yī míng zhígōng) - one staff member

examples.chinese: 我们公司有五百名职工。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gōngsī yǒu wǔbǎi míng zhígōng.
examples.english: Our company has five hundred employees.

examples.pinyin: Zhígōng shítáng zài èr lóu.
examples.english: The staff cafeteria is on the second floor.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Collective term for all employees, often used in formal or institutional contexts (factories, state-owned enterprises).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 联(connect) + 合(combine) = connect and combine, to 'unite'.
vocabulary.etymology: 联 (lián, to connect, join) + 合 (hé, to combine, join).

examples.chinese: 几个小公司联合起来对抗大公司。
examples.pinyin: Jǐ gè xiǎo gōngsī liánhé qǐlái duìkàng dà gōngsī.
examples.english: Several small companies united to compete against the big one.

examples.chinese: 他们联合发表了一个声明。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen liánhé fābiǎo le yī gè shēngmíng.
examples.english: They jointly issued a statement.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in formal or organizational contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 联合(unite) + 国(country) = the United Nations.
vocabulary.etymology: 联合 (liánhé, to unite) + 国 (guó, nation).

examples.pinyin: Liánhéguó zǒngbù zài Niǔyuē.
examples.english: The United Nations headquarters is in New York.

examples.chinese: 这个问题应该由联合国来解决。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yīnggāi yóu Liánhéguó lái jiějué.
examples.english: This issue should be resolved by the United Nations.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Proper noun, always capitalized in English context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 联(connect) + 系(tie) = to connect and tie, i.e., 'contact'.
vocabulary.etymology: 联 (lián, to connect) + 系 (xì, to tie, connect).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zěnme liánxì nǐ?
examples.english: How can I contact you?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen hěnjiǔ méiyǒu liánxì le.
examples.english: We haven't been in contact for a long time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common word for all forms of contact (call, message, email, etc.).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 背(back) + 后(behind) = behind the back.
vocabulary.etymology: 背 (bèi, back) + 后 (hòu, behind). Literally "at the back."

examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǒ bèihòu.
examples.english: He is behind me.

examples.chinese: 不要在别人背后说坏话。
examples.pinyin: Bùyào zài biérén bèihòu shuō huàihuà.
examples.english: Don't speak ill of others behind their backs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be literal (spatial) or figurative (doing something secretly).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine half of a '胖' character as 月 (flesh/body) - a fleshy body.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 月 (yuè, flesh radical) and 半 (bàn, half). Possibly suggesting a body that is half-again its ideal size.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuìjìn hǎoxiàng pàng le yīdiǎn.
examples.english: I seem to have gained a little weight recently.

examples.pinyin: Nà zhī māo pàngpàng de, hěn kě'ài.
examples.english: That cat is chubby and very cute.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be neutral or slightly negative. Use with care when describing people directly.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 胜 = 月(flesh/muscle) + 生(grow). Muscles grow with victory.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 月 (flesh/muscle radical) and 生 (shēng, to grow). Implies the ability or strength to prevail.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen duì shèng le!
examples.english: Our team won!

examples.pinyin: Tā shèngguò le suǒyǒu duìshǒu.
examples.english: He defeated all his opponents.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal/literary than '赢'. Common in compound words.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 胜(win) + 利(benefit) = the benefit of winning, 'victory'.
vocabulary.etymology: 胜 (shèng, to win) + 利 (lì, benefit, advantage).

measure_word.example: 一次胜利 (yī cì shènglì) - one victory

examples.pinyin: Qìngzhù wǒmen de shènglì!
examples.english: Celebrate our victory!

examples.chinese: 胜利属于坚持到最后的人。
examples.pinyin: Shènglì shǔyú jiānchí dào zuìhòu de rén.
examples.english: Victory belongs to those who persevere to the end.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for 'victory' in both literal and figurative contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 能(can) + 不能(cannot) = the question "can you or can't you?"
vocabulary.etymology: 能 (néng, can) + 不 (bù, not) + 能 (néng, can). A common A-not-A question form.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bu néng bāng wǒ yī gè máng?
examples.english: Can you do me a favor?

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān néng bu néng xià yǔ?
examples.english: Will it rain tomorrow or not? (lit. Can it rain tomorrow?)

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common way to ask "can you...?" or "is it possible...?" in spoken Chinese. Note the tone sandhi: 'bù' often becomes neutral tone here.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 能(can) + 力(strength) = the strength of 'can', i.e., ability.
vocabulary.etymology: 能 (néng, can, ability) + 力 (lì, strength, power).

measure_word.example: 一种能力 (yī zhǒng nénglì) - a kind of ability

examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn qiáng de xuéxí nénglì.
examples.english: He has a strong ability to learn.

examples.chinese: 这超出了我的能力范围。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chāochū le wǒ de nénglì fànwéi.
examples.english: This is beyond my capabilities.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to inherent or acquired capacity to do something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 自(self) + 主(master) = self-master, being your own boss.
vocabulary.etymology: 自 (zì, self) + 主 (zhǔ, master, to decide). Literally "self-deciding."

examples.chinese: 孩子应该有更多的自主权。
examples.pinyin: Háizi yīnggāi yǒu gèng duō de zìzhǔquán.
examples.english: Children should have more autonomy.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè zìzhǔ pǐnpái.
examples.english: This is an independent brand.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes self-reliance and freedom from external control.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 自(from) + 从(from) = a double 'from', marking the starting point of time.
vocabulary.etymology: 自 (zì, from) + 从 (cóng, from). A reinforcing compound.

examples.chinese: 自从他来了，办公室热闹多了。
examples.pinyin: Zìcóng tā lái le, bàngōngshì rènào duō le.
examples.english: Since he arrived, the office has become much livelier.

examples.chinese: 自从去年开始，我就住在这里。
examples.pinyin: Zìcóng qùnián kāishǐ, wǒ jiù zhù zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: I've been living here since last year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used at the beginning of a sentence to introduce the starting point of a situation that continues to the present.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 自(self) + 动(move) = self-moving, 'automatic'.
vocabulary.etymology: 自 (zì, self) + 动 (dòng, to move, to act).

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zìdòng mén.
examples.english: This is an automatic door.

examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo huì zìdòng bǎocún wénjiàn.
examples.english: The computer automatically saves files.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes things that operate by themselves without human intervention.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of aiming at the 'eyes' (目) of a 'marker' (标) on a target.
vocabulary.etymology: 目 means 'eye' or 'to look at'. 标 originally meant a 'marker' or 'sign'. Combined, it means the target your eyes are set on.

examples.chinese: 我今年的目标是学会游泳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīnnián de mùbiāo shì xuéhuì yóuyǒng.
examples.english: My goal this year is to learn how to swim.

examples.chinese: 他成功实现了自己的目标。
examples.pinyin: Tā chénggōng shíxiàn le zìjǐ de mùbiāo.
examples.english: He successfully achieved his goal.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for both long-term and short-term aims.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a straight line in the character 十, with an extra vertical line for emphasis.
vocabulary.etymology: The character pictographically depicts a straight line. Its original meaning is 'straight', 'direct', or 'upright'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù hěn zhí.
examples.english: This road is very straight.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhàn zhí.
examples.english: Please stand up straight.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can also be used as an adverb meaning 'directly'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Keep going 'straight' (直) 'to' (到) that point in time.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 直 (straight/direct) and 到 (to arrive). Together, they convey the sense of extending straight/directly to a point in time.

examples.chinese: 我昨天晚上工作直到十二点。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang gōngzuò zhídào shí'èr diǎn.
examples.english: I worked until 12 o'clock last night.

examples.pinyin: Zhídào jīntiān wǒ cái míngbai.
examples.english: It wasn't until today that I understood.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 才 or 还 to emphasize a condition lasting up to a point.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It 'straight' (直) 'broadcasts' (播) to you with no delay.
vocabulary.etymology: 直 means 'directly'. 播 means 'to sow' or 'to broadcast'. Combined, it means 'direct broadcast'.

examples.chinese: 他正在抖音上直播打游戏。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài Dǒuyīn shang zhíbō dǎ yóuxì.
examples.english: He is live streaming playing video games on Douyin.

examples.chinese: 我看了那场演唱会的直播。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kàn le nà chǎng yǎnchàng huì de zhíbō.
examples.english: I watched the live stream of that concert.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common modern word for any real-time online video broadcast.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Two people looking at 'each other' (相) and helping one another (互).
vocabulary.etymology: 相 means 'mutually' or 'each other'. 互 also means 'mutual' or 'reciprocal'. Together they reinforce the idea of reciprocity.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi xiānghù zūnzhòng.
examples.english: We should respect each other.

examples.chinese: 他们之间有相互的信任。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhī jiān yǒu xiānghù de xìnrèn.
examples.english: There is mutual trust between them.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used interchangeably with 互相, but 相互 is more commonly used as an adjective.

vocabulary.mnemonic: They look like 'each other' (相) because they 'resemble' (似) one another.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (mutually) + 似 (to resemble). It means to resemble each other.

examples.chinese: 这对双胞胎长得很相似。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì shuāngbāotāi zhǎng de hěn xiāngsì.
examples.english: This pair of twins looks very similar.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xiǎngfǎ hěn xiāngsì.
examples.english: Our thoughts are very similar.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as 和/跟...相似 (similar to...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Things that are 'mutually' (相) 'connected' (关) to each other.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (mutually) + 关 (to close/pass; to involve). Its meaning evolved to 'mutually connected' or 'interrelated'.

examples.chinese: 这和你之前的问题相关吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè hé nǐ zhīqián de wèntí xiāngguān ma?
examples.english: Is this related to your previous question?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎodào le xiāngguān de zīliào.
examples.english: I found relevant information.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in both formal and casual contexts. Often used as 和/跟...相关.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Two things are 'mutually' (相) 'matched' (当) in degree or value.
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (mutually) + 当 (to bear/act as; to match). Originally meant 'to match each other', now also means 'quite'.

examples.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng xiāngdāng hǎokàn.
examples.english: This movie is quite good.

examples.chinese: 他的水平相当于一个专业厨师。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shuǐpíng xiāngdāng yú yí gè zhuānyè chúshī.
examples.english: His level is equivalent to that of a professional chef.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adverb, it's stronger than 很 but less emphatic than 非常.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Place things side-by-side to look at them 'mutually' (相) and 'compare' (比).
vocabulary.etymology: 相 (mutually) + 比 (to compare). It means to compare with each other.

examples.chinese: 相比昨天，今天暖和多了。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngbǐ zuótiān, jīntiān nuǎnhuo duō le.
examples.english: Compared to yesterday, it's much warmer today.

examples.chinese: 相比价格，我更看重质量。
examples.pinyin: Xiāngbǐ jiàgé, wǒ gèng kànzhòng zhìliàng.
examples.english: Compared to price, I value quality more.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common structure: 相比A，B... (Compared to A, B...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: From what I 'look' (看) and it goes 'up' (上) 'to' (去) my eyes, this is how it seems.
vocabulary.etymology: A colloquial phrase combining 看 (to look), 上 (up), and 去 (to go). It literally means 'as seen going up (to the eyes)'.

examples.pinyin: Tā kàn shang qu hěn lèi.
examples.english: He looks very tired.

examples.chinese: 这个蛋糕看上去很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo kàn shang qu hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: This cake looks delicious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese to give a first impression. '上去' is often pronounced as 'shang qu' with neutral tones.

vocabulary.mnemonic: I 'look' (看) and it 'rises' (起) 'to come' (来) to my mind as a judgment.
vocabulary.etymology: A colloquial phrase combining 看 (to look), 起 (to rise), and 来 (to come). It describes an impression that arises from looking.

examples.pinyin: Kàn qǐ lai yào xià yǔ le.
examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì kàn qǐ lai hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: This matter looks very simple.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more common than '看上去' and can be used for both visual and abstract impressions. '起来' is often pronounced 'qǐ lai' with a neutral tone on 'lai'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something that is 'true' (真) and 'solid/substantial' (实).
vocabulary.etymology: 真 means 'true' or 'genuine'. 实 means 'solid', 'full', or 'real'. Together they emphasize authenticity and reality.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tīng nǐ zhēnshí de xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: I want to hear your real thoughts.

examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshì shì zhēnshí de.
examples.english: This story is true.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe feelings, information, or situations that are not fake.

vocabulary.english: before one's eyes / at the moment
vocabulary.mnemonic: Right 'before' (前) your 'eyes' (眼).
vocabulary.etymology: 眼 (eye) + 前 (front). It literally means 'in front of the eyes'.

examples.chinese: 眼前最重要的是你的健康。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnqián zuì zhòngyào de shì nǐ de jiànkāng.
examples.english: The most important thing at the moment is your health.

examples.pinyin: Měijǐng jiù zài yǎnqián.
examples.english: The beautiful scenery is right before our eyes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to something physically visible or to the immediate present moment.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'short' (短) 'place' or 'aspect' (处) about someone.
vocabulary.etymology: 短 (short) + 处 (place/point). It means a point or aspect where someone is lacking or short.

examples.chinese: 每个人都有自己的短处。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de duǎnchù.
examples.english: Everyone has their own shortcomings.

examples.chinese: 不擅长社交可能是他的短处。
examples.pinyin: Bú shàncháng shèjiāo kěnéng shì tā de duǎnchù.
examples.english: Not being good at socializing might be his weakness.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A slightly formal word for weakness, often contrasted with 长处 (strength).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'short' (短) 'period' (期) of time.
vocabulary.etymology: 短 (short) + 期 (period). It means a short period or term.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo le yī fèn duǎnqī gōngzuò.
examples.english: I found a short-term job.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ shì duǎnqī jìhuà.
examples.english: This is just a short-term plan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for plans, trips, courses, or investments.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Short' (短) 'pants' (裤).
vocabulary.etymology: 短 (short) + 裤 (pants/trousers). It literally means 'short pants'.

examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan chuān duǎnkù.
examples.english: In summer, I like to wear shorts.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè tiáo xīn duǎnkù hěn kù.
examples.english: Your new shorts are very cool.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to any shorts, from athletic to casual.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Stone' (石) with the 'head' (头) suffix, making it a casual noun.
vocabulary.etymology: 石 (stone) + 头 (head/suffix for nouns). 头 here is a nominalizing suffix common in colloquial words.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn! Dì shang yǒu kuài shítou.
examples.english: Be careful! There's a stone on the ground.

examples.chinese: 他用石头堆了一座小塔。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shítou duī le yí zuò xiǎo tǎ.
examples.english: He built a small tower with stones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard casual word for stone. '头' is pronounced with a neutral tone.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'stone' (石) 'oil' (油) that comes from the ground.
vocabulary.etymology: 石 (stone) + 油 (oil). It literally means 'stone oil', referring to crude oil.

examples.pinyin: Shíyóu shì zhòngyào de néngyuán.
examples.english: Petroleum is an important energy source.

examples.chinese: 这个国家石油资源很丰富。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā shíyóu zīyuán hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: This country has abundant petroleum resources.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to crude oil. The refined product for cars is 汽油.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'stone' (石) hitting something so hard it makes a 'split' (皮 as in skin?) – it breaks.
vocabulary.etymology: The character's origin is complex, but it's often analyzed as 石 (stone) + 皮 (skin). One interpretation is using a stone to split skin, indicating 'to break'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī píngmù pò le.
examples.english: My phone screen is broken.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎpò le shìjiè jìlù.
examples.english: He broke the world record.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word for things that are broken, torn, or smashed.

vocabulary.mnemonic: To actively 'break' (破) something until it goes 'bad' (坏).
vocabulary.etymology: 破 (to break) + 坏 (bad/to ruin). It means to break something to the point of ruining it.

examples.pinyin: Búyào pòhuài gōnggòng cáiwù.
examples.english: Don't damage public property.

examples.chinese: 这场雨破坏了我们的野餐计划。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǔ pòhuài le wǒmen de yěcān jìhuà.
examples.english: This rain ruined our picnic plans.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to physical damage or abstract things like plans, moods, or relationships.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Make certain' (确) and 'protect/secure' (保) that it happens.
vocabulary.etymology: 确 (definite/sure) + 保 (to protect/guarantee). It means to make something definite and secure.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng quèbǎo mén yǐjīng suǒ hǎo le.
examples.english: Please make sure the door is locked.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen huì quèbǎo zhǔnshí jiāo huò.
examples.english: We will ensure on-time delivery.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies taking active steps to make something certain. More formal than 保证.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'chisel' (确) the details until they are 'fixed/set' (定).
vocabulary.etymology: 确 (originally meant a chisel, later 'definite') + 定 (to set/fix). It means to make something definite or fixed.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ quèdìng míngtiān néng lái ma?
examples.english: Are you sure you can come tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: Huìyì shíjiān hái méi quèdìng.
examples.english: The meeting time hasn't been confirmed yet.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common for asking for or stating certainty about plans or facts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 'definite' (确) and 'real' (实).
vocabulary.etymology: 确 (definite) + 实 (real). It means something is definite and true.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān quèshí hěn rè.
examples.english: It is indeed very hot today.

examples.chinese: 我听到了一个确实的消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng dào le yí gè quèshí de xiāoxi.
examples.english: I heard a reliable piece of news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adverb, it's used to emphasize that something is true. As an adjective, it means 'reliable'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A gathering of people for a 'religious ceremony' (社) and 'meeting' (会).
vocabulary.etymology: 社 originally referred to an altar for the earth god, representing community. 会 means a gathering or meeting. Combined, it means the community where people gather.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zūnshǒu shèhuì guīzé.
examples.english: We must follow the rules of society.

examples.chinese: 这是一个快速发展的社会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè kuàisù fāzhǎn de shèhuì.
examples.english: This is a rapidly developing society.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very broad term used in countless contexts, from 社交媒体 (social media) to 社会问题 (social issues).

vocabulary.english: to wish / to express good wishes
vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (礻, variant of 示) 'speaking' (口) at an altar to express good wishes.
vocabulary.etymology: The left component 礻 is a variant of 示 (altar/to show). The right is 口 (mouth). It depicts a person speaking/praying at an altar, expressing wishes.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè!
examples.english: Happy Birthday to you!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù nǐ lǚxíng yúkuài.
examples.english: I wish you a pleasant trip.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost always followed by an object (祝你...). It's the standard verb for birthday, holiday, and success wishes.

vocabulary.mnemonic: When you're in a 紧 spot, you feel 'jin' (tight).
vocabulary.etymology: From '糸' (silk thread) and '臤' (firm, solid), suggesting something pulled firm or taut.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié tài jǐn le.
examples.english: This pair of shoes is too tight.

examples.pinyin: Shí jiān hěn jǐn, wǒ men kuài zǒu ba.
examples.english: Time is tight, let's hurry up.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe clothing, schedules, or situations where there's little slack.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine being 紧 (tight) and 张 (stretched out) like a bowstring when nervous.
vocabulary.etymology: Combines 紧 (tight) and 张 (to stretch, extend), describing a tense, stretched state.

examples.pinyin: Shàng tái biǎo yǎn qián, wǒ hěn jǐn zhāng.
examples.english: I was very nervous before going on stage to perform.

examples.pinyin: Bié jǐn zhāng, màn man shuō.
examples.english: Don't be nervous, speak slowly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes an emotional state of anxiety or a situation that is tense (e.g., '紧张的局势').

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's so 紧 (tight) and 急 (hurried), there's no time to spare!
vocabulary.etymology: Combines 紧 (tight) and 急 (urgent, hasty).

examples.pinyin: Yǒu jǐn jí qíng kuàng!
examples.english: There's an urgent situation!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào jǐn jí lián xì rén.
examples.english: I need an emergency contact.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for emergencies, urgent matters, or pressing deadlines.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 红 (red) from the color of the brewed 茶 (tea). Think of English 'black tea' vs. Chinese 'red tea'.
vocabulary.etymology: 红 (red) + 茶 (tea). Named for the reddish color of the infused liquor.

examples.chinese: 早上我喜欢喝一杯红茶。
examples.pinyin: Zǎo shang wǒ xǐ huān hē yī bēi hóng chá.
examples.english: I like to drink a cup of black tea in the morning.

examples.pinyin: Jiā niú nǎi de hóng chá hěn hǎo hē.
examples.english: Black tea with milk is delicious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The default tea in many Western countries. In China, often drunk with sugar or lemon.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 红 (red) 酒 (wine) = red wine. Simple and logical.
vocabulary.etymology: 红 (red) + 酒 (wine/alcohol).

examples.pinyin: Wǎn fàn wǒ men hē diǎn hóng jiǔ ma?
examples.english: Shall we have some red wine with dinner?

examples.pinyin: Zhè píng hóng jiǔ shì Fǎ guó chǎn de.
examples.english: This bottle of red wine is from France.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for dining and social occasions. '干红' means dry red wine.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a 约 (yāo) being a 'call' to hang out.
vocabulary.etymology: From '糸' (silk) and '勺' (ladle/spoon), possibly suggesting binding an agreement (like a ladle tying people together for a meal). The reading 'yāo' is a colloquial variant for 'invite'.

examples.chinese: 晚上我约了朋友看电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǎn shang wǒ yāo le péng you kàn diàn yǐng.
examples.english: I invited a friend to watch a movie tonight.

examples.chinese: 我们约在咖啡馆见面吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yāo zài kā fēi guǎn jiàn miàn ba.
examples.english: Let's arrange to meet at the cafe.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The pronunciation 'yāo' is very common in spoken Chinese for 'to invite/arrange a meeting'. Also read as 'yuē' (to agree, approximately).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 纪 (record) 录 (record). Double 'record'! Think of keeping a log.
vocabulary.etymology: 纪 (to record, discipline) + 录 (to record, copy down).

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎ pò le shì jiè jì lù.
examples.english: He broke the world record.

examples.chinese: 这个会议有文字纪录吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge huì yì yǒu wén zì jì lù ma?
examples.english: Is there a written record of this meeting?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for official records, achievements (sports), or logs. Sometimes written as '记录' (more common for 'to record' as a verb).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 纪 (record) + 念 (to think of). You record your thoughts to remember something.
vocabulary.etymology: 纪 (to record) + 念 (to think of, miss).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men jì niàn qù shì de qīn rén.
examples.english: We commemorate our deceased relatives.

examples.chinese: 我从旅行中带回了这个纪念品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng lǚ xíng zhōng dài huí le zhè ge jì niàn pǐn.
examples.english: I brought back this souvenir from my trip.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb: 'to commemorate/mark'. As a noun: often in '纪念品' (souvenir).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Looks like a few threads crossing. Think of a clothesline.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from '綫'. Contains '糸' (silk thread) radical.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ yán zhe zhè tiáo xiàn jiǎn.
examples.english: Please cut along this line.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de máo yī diào le yī gēn xiàn.
examples.english: A thread came loose from my sweater.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for physical threads, lines (e.g., on paper), routes (公交线), and phone lines (占线).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 组 (group) + 合 (join). You group things together into a combo.
vocabulary.etymology: 组 (to organize, group) + 合 (to combine, join).

examples.chinese: 这是一个新的音乐组合。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè xīn de yīn yuè zǔ hé.
examples.english: This is a new music group/band.

examples.chinese: 你可以把这些字母组合成一个单词。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kě yǐ bǎ zhè xiē zì mǔ zǔ hé chéng yī gè dān cí.
examples.english: You can combine these letters to form a word.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun: a group or set (e.g., boy band, furniture set). As a verb: to put together.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 经 (pass through) 历 (calendar/history). What passes through your personal history.
vocabulary.etymology: 经 (to pass through) + 历 (calendar, to experience).

examples.chinese: 他有过一次有趣的旅行经历。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu guò yī cì yǒu qù de lǚ xíng jīng lì.
examples.english: He had an interesting travel experience.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men jīng lì le hěn duō kùn nán.
examples.english: We went through a lot of difficulties.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun: a specific event or period you've lived through. As a verb: to undergo or experience something (often challenging).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 经 (manage) 济 (aid). Managing resources to aid society = economy.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meaning 'to manage the world and aid the people'. Now used for 'economy'.

examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó de jīng jì fā zhǎn hěn kuài.
examples.english: China's economic development is very fast.

examples.pinyin: Zuò dì tiě bǐ dǎ chē gèng jīng jì.
examples.english: Taking the subway is more economical than taking a taxi.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun: the economy. As an adjective: economical, cost-effective.
